In the name of the people,
The Assembly of the Representatives of the People having adopted,
The President of the Republic promulgates the law whose
content follows:

Article 1: This law establishes the statute of the
Central Bank of Tunisia.

TITLE ONE
GENERAL PROVISIONS Article 2:
1) The Central Bank of Tunisia, hereinafter referred to as "the central bank," is a public institution
with legal personality and financial autonomy.

2) The central bank is independent in the achievement of its objectives, the exercise of its missions, and
the management of its resources. It is subject to the oversight of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People and is accountable to it regarding the achievement of its objectives and the exercise of its missions in accordance with the provisions of

Article 80 of this law.

3) No one may infringe upon the independence of the
central bank, nor influence the decisions of its bodies and its agents in the exercise of their functions.

Article 3: The central bank is deemed to be a merchant
in its dealings with third parties to the extent that this is not derogated from by laws and its own statute. The provisions of the public accounting code are not applicable to it.

The staff of the Central Bank are subject to a special statute approved by government decree.
Said statute provides for at least the fundamental rights and guarantees provided for by law n° 78-85 of August 5, 1985, concerning the general statute of agents of offices, public industrial and commercial establishments, and companies whose capital belongs directly and entirely to the State or local authorities.
Said special statute guarantees the possibility of secondment and integration of executives from the public sector to the central bank. TITLE II
OBJECTIVES AND MISSIONS OF THE CENTRAL BANK

Article 7: The primary objective of the central bank is to maintain price stability.
The central bank contributes to maintaining financial stability in a way that supports the achievement of the State's economic policy objectives, including in the areas of development and employment. It works for optimal coordination between monetary policy and the State's economic policy.

Article 8: The central bank is notably responsible for:
- conducting and implementing monetary policy,
- applying laws and regulations relating to foreign exchange,
- holding and managing foreign exchange reserves in foreign currencies and gold.
- working to ensure the stability, efficiency, and security of payment systems, while taking into account the specificities of Islamic finance,
- supervising banks and financial institutions and regulating banking activity,
- issuing and ensuring the maintenance of fiduciary currency and facilitating its circulation in Tunisia,
- acting as the State's cashier and financial agent,
- acting as the government's financial advisor and issuing an opinion on economic and financial matters when requested,
- collecting and managing all data related to the exercise of its missions,
- contributing to the conduct and implementation of macroprudential policy with a view to preventing and mitigating systemic risk,
- working to protect users of banking services.

Article 9: For the exercise of its missions, the Central Bank may notably undertake the following operations:

1) Open cash and securities accounts on its books, regardless of the currency, for the benefit of the State, banks, public enterprises and establishments, financial institutions, foreign banks Article 12: Any refinancing operation of a debt by the central bank automatically results in the subrogation of the central bank in the rights and obligations that the beneficiary of the refinancing has against their own debtor.

CHAPTER II
EMISSION PRIVILEGE
Article 13: The central bank, on behalf of the State, exercises the exclusive privilege of issuing banknotes and coins in Tunisia.

Article 14:
1°) Only banknotes and coins issued by the central bank have legal tender, to the exclusion of all other banknotes and coins.
2°) Banknotes issued by the Central Bank have unlimited purchasing power.
3°) The purchasing power of coins issued by the Central Bank is fixed by law. They are accepted without limitation by the central bank and by public treasuries.

Article 15:
1°) The creation and issuance of banknotes and coins by the central bank, as well as their withdrawal or exchange, are carried out under the conditions determined by Article 64 of this law.

2°) No opposition can be served upon the central bank concerning the loss or theft of banknotes.

3°) The reimbursement of a mutilated or damaged banknote is granted when the banknote bears sufficient identifying marks and signs. In other cases, full or partial reimbursement is at the discretion of the Central Bank. 4°) The reimbursement of a coin whose identification has become impossible or which has been subject to any alteration or mutilation is granted only if it is proven, to the satisfaction of the Central Bank, that the mutilations or alterations in question are the result of an accident or an act of force majeure.

5°) In case of withdrawal from circulation of one or more categories of banknotes or of 2°) Subject to the provisions of the legislation relating to the protection of personal data, the Central Bank may request information useful for the exercise of its duties provided for in the preceding paragraph from entities operating in the private sector and public sector organizations, even if these entities and organizations are not subject to its control, and this, notwithstanding the obligations incumbent upon them under professional secrecy.

3°) The Central Bank may conclude cooperation agreements with foreign authorities responsible for macroprudential supervision and exchange secret information with them, provided that this information is, according to the applicable laws abroad, covered by professional secrecy and that it is necessary for the accomplishment of the missions of the foreign authorities. The foreign authority must undertake not to communicate this information to third parties without the explicit agreement of the Central Bank and to use it only within the framework of the exercise of its powers.

Article 19:
1) In order to preserve the stability of the financial system, the Central Bank may grant financial assistance in the form of operations referred to in Article 10 of this law to solvent banks and financial institutions whose liquidity is temporarily affected.

2) The Central Bank may grant financial assistance to banks and financial institutions whose solvency is compromised and if their failure presents a threat to the stability of the financial system. The granting of this assistance requires obtaining the guarantee of the State in accordance with the legislation in force.

3) The Central Bank may, where applicable, grant financial assistance to the deposit guarantee fund after obtaining the guarantee of the State in accordance with the legislation in force. This prohibition is not applicable to financial assistance operations granted by the central bank, under the conditions provided for by this law, to banks and financial institutions in which the State directly or indirectly holds a stake.

Article 26: The central bank may, at the request of the minister in charge of finance, provide financial services to administrations, public enterprises and establishments, and all financial organizations governed by special legislative provisions or placed under the supervision of the State as defined by current texts. It may carry out for their benefit all cash, banking, and credit operations in accordance with the conditions fixed by agreements concluded with the aforementioned administrations, public enterprises and establishments, and organizations.

Article 27: The central bank assists the government in its relations with international financial institutions. The governor or their authorized representative for this purpose may, under government delegation, represent the State to the aforementioned institutions or at international congresses.

Article 28:
1°) The central bank participates in negotiations concerning the conclusion of payment or compensation agreements. It may be entrusted with their execution as well as the conclusion of all necessary implementing conventions for this purpose.
2°) The aforementioned agreements are executed on behalf of the State. The State benefits from profits and bears losses, expenses, commissions, interest, and charges related to the execution of these agreements, whatever their nature.
The State guarantees the central bank coverage of any loss arising from exchange rates or any other loss arising directly from the execution of the aforementioned agreements.
SECTION 2 - FINANCIAL ADVISOR ROLE FOR THE GOVERNMENT

Article 29: CHAPTER VIII
MISCELLANEOUS OPERATIONS

Article 33: The central bank may, in its own name and for its own account, lend and borrow in foreign currencies within the limits of its necessary needs.

Article 34:
1°) The central bank may accept, in accounts opened with the approval of its Board of Directors, sums deposited by banks, and by individuals and legal entities.
Only credit balances denominated in foreign currencies may bear interest.
2°) The central bank shall settle drafts on the said accounts and commitments made at its counters within the limits of available balances.
3°) The central bank may refinance swap operations, carried out in foreign currencies against dinars, conducted by Tunisian banks with foreign financial institutions.

Article 35:
1°) The central bank may construct, acquire, sell, or exchange real estate according to operational needs.
2°) Expenses related to the operations mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall be charged to the central bank's own funds.
3°) In order to guarantee the recovery of doubtful or outstanding debts, the Central Bank may:
- take all guarantees, particularly in the form of pledges,
- acquire amicably or through forced sale any movable or immovable property. Real estate and assets thus acquired must be disposed of within two years, unless they are used for operational needs in accordance with the legislation in force.

Article 36: The Board of Directors may invest the Central Bank's own funds represented by its capital, reserve, and amortization accounts:
- in real estate in accordance with the provisions of paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 35 of this law,
- in sukuks or listed securities on the stock exchange,
- in sukuks or equity securities issued by non-resident companies or organizations, after In all cases, the amount of the fine cannot exceed 50,000 dinars.
In case of late declaration within the deadlines mentioned in

Article 38 of this law, the offender is liable to a fine of two hundred dinars (200 D) per day of delay. In addition to the penalties mentioned in the two preceding paragraphs, the central bank may suspend, temporarily or permanently, the consultation service with regard to any offender of the provisions of Articles 38 and 39 of this law. The offenses mentioned in the first and second paragraphs of this article are recorded at the headquarters of the central bank or in one of its branches by two sworn agents designated by the governor from among the bank's executives. The two agents draw up a report including the date and stamp of the central bank as well as their identities and signatures. Before the final version of the report is established, the offender is summoned by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt, addressed to their real or elected domicile, in order to present their statements. The offender who presents themselves is required to sign the report. In case of refusal, this is noted in the report. A copy of the report is given to the offender. In case of refusal to appear or to sign, a copy of the report is notified to them by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt.

The fines are imposed by the governor of the central bank after summoning the offender for an hearing. The conclusions of the hearing session are recorded in the report. The offender may be assisted by a lawyer or be represented in accordance with the law. The fines are recovered for the benefit of the General Treasury of Tunisia by means of a liquidation statement issued and made enforceable by the minister in charge of finance or by the one who has received delegation from the m The State assumes the losses incurred by the central bank due to the implementation of international cooperation agreements in the monetary field mentioned in the first paragraph of this article. It guarantees to it, in accordance with current legislation, the payment of any credit or participation granted under these agreements. TITLE III
GOVERNANCE AND ADMINISTRATION OF THE
CENTRAL BANK

Article 45: The governance and administration of the central bank are carried out in the following order by: a governor and a board of directors referred to hereinafter as the "board."

CHAPTER ONE
GOVERNOR OF THE CENTRAL BANK Article 46: The governor of the central bank is appointed in accordance with the provisions of

Article 78 of the constitution for a term of six years, renewable once. He is chosen from among individuals recognized for their competence in economic, monetary, and financial fields.
The functions of the governor may be terminated before the end of the term mentioned in the first paragraph of this article, in accordance with the provisions of

Article 78 of the constitution.

Article 47: The governor shall swear, before the President of the Republic and before taking up his duties, the following oath:
"I swear by Almighty God to direct, with loyalty and fidelity, the affairs of the Central Bank of Tunisia and to fulfill my duties with complete impartiality and independence."

Article 48: Subject to the powers of the board, the governor ensures the management of the Central Bank. To this end, he:
1°) represents the central bank to public authorities, foreign central banks, international financial institutions, and, in general, to third parties,
2°) ensures the application of laws relating to the Central Bank and the deliberations of the board,
3°) implements the monetary policy of the Central Bank as defined by the board, **

Article 54**: The governor, the vice-governor, and the secretary-general are prohibited from combining their duties with those of a member of the people's representative assembly or the government, or from assuming partisan responsibility at the central, regional, or local level, or from combining their duties with any function in the public or private sector.

**

Article 55**:
1. The remuneration and benefits of the governor, the vice-governor, and the secretary-general shall be fixed by the council. They shall be borne by the central bank.
2. In the event of the cessation of their duties, the governor and the vice-governor shall continue to receive their remuneration for one year.
3. If a public office is entrusted to them during this period, a decision by the head of government shall specify the conditions under which the emoluments inherent to the said office are combined with the aforementioned remuneration.
4. During the same period, they are prohibited from providing services to private companies and receiving compensation for advice or services rendered, except with the authorization of the head of government. In such a case, they shall be deprived of the remuneration provided for in the second paragraph of this article.
5. The council shall determine the conditions under which the governor benefits from representation allowance as well as the conditions for reimbursement of his exceptional expenses.

**

Article 56**:
1. During the period of their mandate, the governor and the vice-governor are prohibited from holding any shareholding or having interests in a private company.
2. No commitment signed by the governor or the vice-governor may be admitted into the portfolio of the Central Bank.

**CHAPTER II**
**BOARD OF DIRECTORS**

** Article 57**: The council shall be composed of:
- the governor, president,
- the vice-governor,
- the president of the financial market council,
- the ca 3) The members of the council must declare their
assets on the date of their appointment and on the date of their
cessation of duties, in accordance with current legislation
concerning asset declarations.

Article 60:
During the exercise of their duties, the members
of the council are independent of the bodies to which
they may belong.

They may not suffer any professional or other prejudice in relation
to the bodies mentioned in Article 57 of this law, due to the opinions or
proposals they may make during the
exercise of their duties as members of the
council.

Article 61:
1°) Subject to the obligations imposed on them
by law and except in cases where they are
called to testify in court, council members are
prohibited from disclosing information that they have
acquired, directly or indirectly,
due to their duties.

2°) The same prohibition applies to all
persons whom the governor or the council
calls upon for assistance in the exercise of their
responsibilities.

3°) Anyone who has contravened these provisions
shall incur the penalties provided for by current criminal legislation.

4) No commitment bearing the signature of one
of the council members mentioned in the third,
fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh indents of

Article 57 of this law, may be admitted into the
portfolio of the central bank.

Article 62:
1°) The council meets periodically once
every two months and whenever necessary, upon
convening by the governor.

2°) The governor shall be obliged to convene
the council if requested to do so by at least three members.

3°) Council meetings shall only be valid if all
members have been duly convened and
if the governor and at least five members are present. In the absence of this quorum, the council meeting shall be postponed. 17°) It approves the organization chart of the Central Bank and sets the responsibilities of the departments.

18°) It decides on the establishment and closure of central bank branches.

19°) It decides, where applicable, on the transfer of the Central Bank's head office to any other location.

20°) It approves the emergency plan to ensure the security of the central bank's operations.

21°) It sets the rules governing the awarding of contracts for the central bank, using procedures that guarantee compliance with the principles of transparency, competition, and equal opportunity.

Article 64:
1°) Council decisions are made by a majority vote of the members present. In the event of a tie, the President's vote shall prevail.

2°) The following Council decisions are made by a two-thirds majority vote of the members:
a) the creation, issuance, withdrawal, or exchange of banknotes and coins,
b) the allocation of profits,
c) the determination of the conditions and terms for granting financial assistance mentioned in

Article 19 of this law.

Article 65:
1°) Minutes shall be drawn up for each Council meeting.

2°) The Council members present shall sign the minutes, which shall be recorded in the Council's deliberations register.

3°) The Governor and the Vice-Governor are authorized to sign extracts of the Council's deliberation minutes and to produce them in the context of operations carried out by the Central Bank.

CHAPTER III
OVERSIGHT OF THE CENTRAL BANK

Article 66: The Council shall establish the central bank's internal control system.

Article 67: The Council shall create a permanent audit committee, chaired by one of the Council members mentioned in point 7 of Article 57. At least two members of the Management Board, other than the Governor and the Vice-Governor, shall be among its members. TITLE IV
MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS
CHAPTER ONE
EXEMPTIONS AND PRIVILEGES
Article 72: The central bank is subject to the tax regime of the State, local authorities, and public administrative bodies.

Article 73: For the realization of pledged assets received as security for its debts, the central bank may take the following measures, unless more favorable provisions for pledged creditors are provided by law:
1°) In the event of non-reimbursement at maturity of the sums owed to it, the central bank may, fifteen days after a formal notice served on the debtor by a bailiff, and notwithstanding any opposition, proceed with the sale of the assets subject to pledge, with a view to the full recovery of the sums due in principal, interest, commissions, and costs, without prejudice to other proceedings that may be brought against the debtor. 2°) The sale of the assets subject to pledge takes place by virtue of an order on request from the president of the Court of First Instance of Tunis 1, upon request from the central bank and without the need to summon the debtor. 3°) The sale of securities and related rights, issued by a company making a public offer to save, takes place on one of the stock exchange markets. For securities, company shares, and related rights, issued by companies not making a public offer to save, their sale shall be carried out on the date, at the time and place fixed by the judge, who shall appoint an intermediary for this purpose. The judge shall determine the publication period and its arrangements.

However, securities and related rights, issued by companies not making a public offer to save, may be sold at the request of offerors or claimants interested in market advantages, in accordance with the provisions of the third paragraph of Article 71 of the 5°) Unrealized gains resulting from the revaluation of net foreign currency and gold assets and liabilities must be recorded in an unavailable revaluation account. This operation cannot result in any payment of these unrealized gains to the General Treasury of the State.

6°) If the annual accounts result in a loss, this loss is charged to the reserves constituted in application of paragraph 3 above, and, if applicable, to the legal reserve.
If the reserves do not allow the loss to be fully covered, the remaining balance is covered by the General Treasury of Tunisia, provided that the central bank presents a report to the Minister of Finance indicating the origin and causes of the loss.

Article 79: Within three months following the closing of the financial year, the Governor shall submit the financial statements accompanied by the report of the two statutory auditors to the President of the Republic, the President of the Assembly of People's Representatives, and the Head of Government. These documents shall be published in the Official Gazette of the Tunisian Republic and on the website of the central bank.

CHAPTER III
DUTY OF ACCOUNTABILITY AND RIGHT OF INQUIRY

Article 80:
1) The central bank shall prepare an annual report indicating the exercise of its missions in terms of monetary policy, contribution to financial stability, and supervision of banks and financial institutions. The Governor shall submit the report to the President of the Republic, the President of the Assembly of People's Representatives, and the Head of Government no later than June 30 of the following year.

2) The Assembly of People's Representatives, at its request or on the initiative of the Governor, may summon the Governor to testify or answer questions relating to the economic and financial situation of the country and the activities of the central bank, as well as to **

Article 86: The macroprudential oversight committee is composed of:**
- The governor of the central bank,
- A representative from the ministry responsible for finance,
- The chairman of the financial market council,
- The chairman of the general insurance committee,

Article 1: The purpose of this law is to organize the conditions for carrying out banking operations and the modalities for supervising banks and financial institutions, with a view to preserving their solidity and protecting depositors and users of banking services, in order to contribute to the proper functioning of the banking sector and to achieve financial stability.

Article 2: The provisions of this law apply to banks and financial institutions carrying out their activity in Tunisia, including non-resident banks and financial institutions within the meaning of exchange legislation.
The provisions of the code for the provision of financial services to non-residents, enacted by Law n°2009-64 of August 12, 2009, apply to non-resident banks and financial institutions as long as they are not derogated from by the provisions of this law.
Banks and financial institutions are subject to the provisions of the Commercial Companies Code as long as they are not derogated from by the provisions of this law.

Article 3: The provisions of this law do not apply to entities that carry out banking operations under the laws governing them. They also do not apply to international financial institutions, their representations, or financial cooperation agencies created under agreements concluded with the government of the Tunisian Republic.

Article 42:** Without prejudice to the provisions of Organic Law No. 2015-26 of August 7, 2015, relating to the fight against terrorism and the repression of money laundering, banks and financial institutions are required to adopt rules for the sound management of money laundering and terrorist financing risks, including an internal control system designed to prevent the use of the bank or financial institution for illicit financial and economic activities.

Article 43:** Banks and financial institutions are required to adopt a policy aimed at the effective management of conflicts of interest. To this end, the Central Bank of Tunisia shall establish rules governing operations with persons having ties to the bank or financial institution, within the meaning of this law, and in particular the limits on financing granted.

A person having ties to the bank or financial institution is considered to be:

*   any shareholder whose participation exceeds, directly or indirectly, 5% of the capital of the bank or financial institution,
*   any spouse, ascendant, and descendant of a natural person whose participation exceeds, directly or indirectly, 5% of the capital of the bank or financial institution,
*   any company in which the bank or financial institution holds a stake in the capital such that it leads to its control or decisive influence over its activities,
*   the chairman of the board of directors of a bank or financial institution, the general director, the members of the board of directors, the deputy general directors, the members of the supervisory board, the members of the executive board, the members of the banking standards compliance control committee.

A person is considered an independent member within the meaning of this law if they have no links with the said bank or the said institution, or with its shareholders or its directors, of a nature that could compromise the independence of their decisions or lead them into a situation of actual or potential conflict of interest. Small shareholders are considered to be the public within the meaning of the legislation governing the financial market.

The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the criteria determining the quality of independence.

Article 48: The board of directors or the supervisory board defines the strategy of the bank or financial institution and ensures its execution is monitored. It oversees all significant changes affecting the activity of the bank or financial institution in a manner that preserves the interests of depositors, shareholders, all stakeholders, and generally, the long-term interests of the bank or financial institution.

The board of directors or the supervisory board is notably responsible for:

*   Monitoring the degree of commitment of the bank's or financial institution's management in implementing the governance framework and periodically evaluating this framework for its adaptation to significant changes in the bank or financial institution, particularly in terms of business size, operational complexity, market evolution, and organizational requirements.
*   Establishing, in consultation with the general management or the executive board, a risk appetite strategy that takes into account the competitive and regulatory environment as well as the bank's or financial institution's capacity to control risks.
*   Appointing the general management or the executive board.
*   Closing the financial statements and preparing the annual report of the bank or financial institution. **

Article 50:** The bank or financial institution must create a Risk Committee, stemming from the Board of Directors or the Supervisory Board, which assists it in particular in establishing a risk management strategy and which will be responsible, in particular:
- for advising the Board of Directors or the Supervisory Board on the identification, measurement, and control of risks,
- for periodically evaluating the risk management policy and its implementation,
- for monitoring the activity of the body responsible for risk management.

**

Article 51:** Every bank must create a Nomination and Remuneration Committee, stemming from the Board of Directors or the Supervisory Board, which assists it in particular in the design and monitoring of policies for:
- nomination and remuneration,
- replacement of executives and senior managers and recruitment,
- management of conflict of interest situations.

**

Article 52:** Each of the committees provided for by Articles 49, 50, and 51 of this law must be composed of three members from among the members of the Board of Directors or the Supervisory Board.

The fund shall take into consideration the specificities of banks that exclusively conduct Islamic banking operations and non-resident banks within the meaning of

Article 2 of this law, by allocating a special account to each category of bank.
The fund must take the necessary internal measures to ensure compliance ** Article 152:** The deposit guarantee fund compensates depositors within a determined ceiling.
The ceiling, terms, and compensation procedures shall be set by governmental decree.
For the purpose of depositor compensation, the global account provided for in

Article 21 of this law, opened by payment institutions with the bank, shall not be considered a single account. The nominative list accompanying the payment accounts opened with the payment institution shall be used as a reference.
The following deposits are excluded from the guarantee of the deposit guarantee fund:
- From the State, public enterprises, and establishments,
- From the Central Bank of Tunisia,
- From banks, financial institutions, and their subsidiaries,
- From the Tunisian Post, insurance and reinsurance companies,
- From collective investment undertakings, stockbrokers, and investment companies,
- From members of the board of directors, supervisory board, executive board, chief executive officer, and deputy chief executive officers of the bank concerned by the compensation of its deposits,
- From any shareholder holding a stake of 5% or more in the capital of the bank provided for in

Article 32 of this law and deposits from companies under their control,
- From the auditors of the bank,
- From the spouse, ascendants, and descendants of the natural persons referred to in points 6, 7, and 8 of this article,
- From funds placed with the bank concerned by the compensation in the form of money market financial instruments.

** Article 153:** The Central Bank of Tunisia shall ascertain the unavailability of the funds mentioned in
Article 149 of this law when it appears to it that a bank is no longer, due to its financial situation, able to repay immediately or in the short term the deposits it has received.

Article 156: The supervisory committee of the bank deposit guarantee fund comprises the following five members:
- two members independent of shareholders and members, appointed by governmental decree, one of whom holds the position of chairman,
- a representative of the Central Bank of Tunisia with the rank of Director General, member,
- a representative of the ministry responsible for finance with the rank of Director General, member,
- a third-grade judge, member.
The members of the supervisory committee referred to in points 2, 3, and 4 of this article are appointed by governmental decree upon the proposal of the Central Bank of Tunisia, the minister responsible for finance, and with the concurring opinion of the Superior Council of the Magistracy, each as far as they are concerned.

The members of the supervisory committee are appointed for a term of three years, renewable only once.

Article 157: Within the bank deposit guarantee fund, a committee named the "Audit and Risk Committee" is established, stemming from the supervisory committee and responsible, in particular, for:
- assisting the supervisory committee in the design and implementation of an internal control system,
- examining the annual activity report and the financial statements of the fund before their transmission to the supervisory committee,
- supervising the activities of the internal audit department and, where applicable, supervising and coordinating the work of other departments responsible for control missions,
- proposing a strategy and policy for risk management,
- evaluating the results of investments made and the risk coverage policy.

The Audit and Risk Committee transmits a detailed report on its activities to the supervisory committee.
The composition of the committee and the rules for its operation and the remuneration of its members are determined by a decision of the supervisory committee.

Article 169: The Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia is empowered to impose the sanctions provided for in Article 170 of this law against banks and financial institutions that commit one of the following offenses:
- Non-compliance with prudential, governance, and internal control standards provided for by this law and by the regulatory provisions issued by the Central Bank of Tunisia,
- Non-compliance with the obligation to obtain authorizations and the obligation to inform the Central Bank of Tunisia, particularly concerning appointments, outsourcing, products, banking conditions, establishment inside and outside the country, including the opening and closing of branches, subsidiaries, or periodic offices,
- Non-compliance with legal and regulatory provisions relating to the facilitation of supervision procedures for banks and financial institutions, including responding to requests related to information and data necessary for the Central Bank of Tunisia to exercise its supervisory functions,
- Non-compliance with regulatory provisions concerning internal control rules related to the fight against money laundering and the financing of terrorism,
- Non-compliance with the obligation to notify operations provided for in

Article 37 of this law,
- Non-compliance with the obligation to pay the annual amount provided for in Article 73 of this law.

Article 170: The Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia shall pronounce one of the following two sanctions in respect of the offenses provided for in

Article 169 of this law:
1- A warning,
2- A fine whose amount shall not exceed 15% of the minimum capital of the bank or of the category of the financial institution in question. Members of the sanctions commission are appointed by government decree for a term of 3 years, renewable once.

The commission holds its meetings at the headquarters of the Central Bank of Tunisia. The general directorate responsible for banking supervision provides its secretariat.
The commission's decisions must be reasoned and are taken by a majority of votes.

The commission establishes its internal regulations, which are approved by government decree.

Members of the sanctions commission are bound by professional secrecy regarding information they become aware of in the performance of their duties. They must refrain from using this information, outside of cases permitted by law, for purposes other than those required for the execution of their assigned missions. This obligation continues even after they lose their status, under penalty of facing the sanctions provided for in

Article 254 of the penal code.

Article 172: The sanctions commission shall impose one of the sanctions provided for in Article 173 of the present law against banks and financial institutions that commit any of the following offenses:
- Carrying out banking operations without respecting the category, specialty, or conditions provided for by their license,
- Violation of legal and regulatory provisions concerning transactions with persons connected to banks or financial institutions,
- Obtaining a license by a bank or financial institution through false declarations,
- Refusal to comply with the instructions of the Central Bank of Tunisia,
- Intentional concealment of information or voluntary communication of inaccurate information,
- Intentional obstruction of the missions of banking supervision to be carried out by agents of the Central Bank of Tunisia,
- Refusal to pay the annual contribution to the bank deposit guarantee fund.
Artic The bank, financial institution, or the concerned person may be assisted by a lawyer, concerning offenses within the competence of the sanctions commission.

Article 177: The bank, financial institution, or the concerned person shall be informed of the facts of which they are accused by any means leaving a written record.
The legal representative of the bank, financial institution, or the concerned person or their representative has the right to consult the file of the offenses being prosecuted at the headquarters of the Central Bank of Tunisia.
The legal representative of the bank, financial institution, or the concerned person must send their written observations to the Central Bank of Tunisia or to the sanctions commission within a period of eight days from the date of receipt of the notification provided for in the first paragraph of this article.

Article 178: The sanctions commission is responsible for the investigation of files of offenses within its competence, upon referral by the Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia.
It shall rule on the aforementioned offenses, in accordance with the procedures provided for by this law.

Article 179: Sanctions shall be imposed by the sanctions commission and by the Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia, each in their respective capacities, and shall be communicated to the bank, financial institution in question, or the concerned person by any means leaving a written record.

Article 180: Decisions rendered under

Article 179 of this law shall be included in the annual banking supervision reports issued by the Central Bank of Tunisia and published on its website.

Article 181: Any delay or refusal to communicate the documents, information, clarifications, and justifications referred to in Article 71 of this law shall be subject to a penalty. TITLE X

Article 186: Banks and financial institutions are required to establish a professional association, with the objective of working to study issues related to the practice of the profession and its development, as well as human resource training. The association also plays the role of an intermediary between its members, on the one hand, and the public authorities and the Central Bank of Tunisia, on the other, for any matter concerning the profession. The minister responsible for finance and the governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia may consult the association on any matter relating to the evolution of the profession, and the association may submit proposals to this effect. The association must establish a code of ethics that is binding on its members and work to ensure its compliance.

Article 187: The association referred to in

Article 186 of this law must create a banking mediation body responsible for examining requests submitted to it by clients concerning their disputes with banks and financial institutions. Each bank or financial institution may, for the same purposes, appoint one or more banking mediators. The banking mediation body or the banking mediator shall propose appropriate mediation solutions within a maximum period of two months from their referral. The banking mediation body or the banking mediator shall be seized of requests submitted to them, free of charge and within a maximum period of eight days from the receipt of the mediation request. It may not consider requests for which arbitration or settlement is not permitted or which are the subject of cases pending before the courts. Banks and financial institutions must facilitate the mission of the banking mediation body or the banking mediator and provide them with all documents relating to the subject. half of the minimum capital provided for in

Article 105: Non-resident investment service providers must take all reasonable measures to prevent conflicts of interest from harming the interests of their clients.**

Subject: Definition of Islamic banking operations and establishment of the terms and conditions for their execution.

The Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia,

Having regard to Law n° 89 -94 of July 26, 1994, relating to leasing; Having regard to Law n° 2016 -35 of April 25, 2016, fixing the statute of the Central Bank of Tunisia; Having regard to Law n° 2016 -48 of July 11, 2016, relating to banks and financial institutions, and particularly
its articles 11 and following; Having regard to the opinion of the Compliance Control Committee n°2019 -08 dated October 2, 2019, as provided by

Article 42 of the aforementioned Law n°2016 -35;

Decides:

Article One: The purpose of this circular is to define Islamic banking operations and to establish the terms and conditions for their execution by banks and financial institutions
authorized to undertake them, in accordance with the provisions of Law n° 2016 -48 of July 11, 2016, relating
to banks and financial institutions.

Article 2: For the purposes of this circular, Islamic banking operations take the form
either of commercial financing operations, or of participatory financing operations, or of investment
deposits.

Title One: Commercial Financing Operations Article 3: Commercial financing operations include Mourabaha, Ijara,
Istisna'a and Salam.

Article 4: Financing by "Mourabaha" is an operation whereby the bank or
financial institution, following a request from the client who placed the order, acquires movable or immovable
assets or services from a third party and resells them to the client who placed the order at a price equivalent to their acquisition cost plus a profit margin determined in advance, in the form
of a fixed amount or a fixed percentage of the initial acquisition value. **

Article 6:** "Ijara" financing for professionals is considered an operation by which the bank or financial institution acquires an asset, takes ownership of it, and then leases it to the client, granting them the option to purchase it.

** Article 7:** "Salam" financing is an operation by which the bank or financial institution carries out a forward purchase at a cash price of determined tangible movable goods specified by the client.
The bank or financial institution is obliged to sell the movable goods subject to the "Salam" after their reception, or to mandate the client for this purpose, within the established deadlines.
The bank or financial institution may sell the goods subject to the "Salam" before their reception within the framework of a second "Salam" for the benefit of a third party.

**

Article 8:** "Istisna'a" financing is an operation by which the bank or financial institution finances the manufacturing of a movable or immovable good for its client, acting as the "Mostasni'i," according to determined specifications.
To this end, the bank or financial institution:
- Commissions a third party, known as the "Sani'i," to manufacture the asset requested **Title II: Participatory Financing Operations**

**

Article 9:** Participatory financing operations include, in particular, financing by "Moucharaka" and financing by "Moudharaba."

** Article 10:** Financing by "Moucharaka" is an operation whereby the bank or financial institution co-finances, with its client, according to agreed proportions and duration, the cost of carrying out a project, an activity, or specific commercial operations.

**

Article 11:** Financing by "Moudharaba" is an operation whereby the bank or financial institution provides the entirety of the capital to the client for the purpose of financing a project or an activity. The client's contribution is limited to expertise and management.

**Title III: Investment Deposits**

** Article 12:** Investment deposits are considered to be amounts lodged by their holders, by any means of payment whatsoever, in an investment account opened with a bank, for the purpose of investing them, under a contract of "Moudharaba" or "Wakala investment," in assets for a determined period, with or without restrictions.

"Wakala investment" is an operation whereby the client mandates the bank to invest their funds in assets, in their name and on their behalf, during a determined period, with or without restrictions.

"Moudharaba" is carried out according to the following two modalities:

*   "Restrictive Moudharaba," which consists, for the client, in mandating the bank to invest their funds in well-defined projects and according to agreed deadlines and conditions. In this case, the investment risk is borne by the client.
*   "Non-restrictive Moudharaba," which consists of giving the bank the freedom to invest the client's funds without any restriction.

**

Article 13:** The return on investment deposits is linked to the results of the investment. **

Article 15**: Every six months, the bank is required to inform its investment account holders of the nature of the investment operations carried out, their direct and indirect shares, as well as the profit and loss distribution arrangements.

**Title IV: General Provisions**

**

Article 16**: The financing operations provided for in this circular may be subject to guarantees for the benefit of banks or financial institutions, in the form of mortgages, surety bonds, or other guarantees provided for by current legislation, to the extent that the use of these guarantees does not contradict the international standards of Islamic banking operations.

**

Article 17**: The bank or financial institution may, before concluding any commercial financing contract, request from its client payment of an amount called a "seriousness deposit" equal to a determined percentage of the acquisition value. The "seriousness deposit" is intended to guarantee the execution of the contract and should be managed according to the conditions agreed upon between the bank or financial institution and the client.

**

Article 18**: Banks and financial institutions must inform the Central Bank of Tunisia of any financial product or service they intend to market within the framework of Islamic banking operations, in order to control their compliance with the international standards practiced in this field.
The Central Bank of Tunisia may, within a period of ten working days from the communication of all the information it requests, oppose, by a reasoned decision, the marketing of the financial product or service.

**

Article 19**: Banks and financial institutions are required, concerning Islamic banking contracts and operations, to comply with the international standards adopted in the field of Islamic banking operations.

Article 20: The Central Bank of Tunisia oversees the compliance of Islamic banking operations with international standards practiced in this field.
To this end, banks and financial institutions engaging in Islamic banking operations must submit an annual report to the Central Bank of Tunisia on the control operations carried out by the Islamic banking standards compliance control committee, within a maximum period of one month before the holding of the general meeting of shareholders.
The Central Bank of Tunisia may request clarifications regarding the committee's opinion as well as the results of its work that are the subject of the aforementioned report. **CIRCULAR FROM THE CENTRAL BANK OF TUNISIA**

Article 3 - For the purposes of this circular, the following are understood as:

- Institution: banks, payment institutions, and the National Postal Office.
- Wallet: a payment method made available to the customer by the institution, which allows for the storage of electronic money and the execution of payment operations via mobile phone, potentially including different technologies.
- Default Wallet: the wallet, among those available to a customer, on which funds received from a transfer or a payment to accepting merchants are automatically deposited.
- Mobile Payment: any payment transaction carried out from a mobile phone that results in a debit or credit movement on a Wallet, whether on a card, a bank account, a postal account, or a payment account.

Mobile payment transactions include, in particular, operations following - Off-us transfer: Transactions carried out between users of mobile payment methods domiciled with two different institutions.
- Strong authentication: Two-factor authentication that combines the use of two elements from the following three categories: something you know (password, PIN), something you possess (computer, mobile phone), something you are (fingerprint, iris, voice...).
- User/client: "Mobile payment services user": a natural or legal person who uses a mobile payment service as a payer or a beneficiary, or both.
- Issuer: The institution that provides its client with payment methods to initiate mobile payment transactions.
- Acquirer: The institution that provides its client with services for acquiring mobile payment transactions.
- SGMT: Large amount transfer system managed by the Central Bank of Tunisia.

Paragraph 3: Technical and Security Rules

Article 26** - Mobile payment services are interoperable.
Issuing and acquiring institutions must implement the necessary technical prerequisites, particularly for interfacing with the mobile switch, to enable transaction interoperability.
Membership in the mobile switch is ensured according to the homologation process defined by the manager of this switch and approved by the Central Bank of Tunisia, before the operational deployment of the mobile payment service.

Article 31 - The establishment and the manager of the mobile switch are required to take the necessary measures to ensure the security of the network and operational systems, and the establishment of a network and payment channels protected against fraud, piracy, and any other form of unauthorized use.
They must design and implement a cybersecurity program that addresses the various aspects of establishing an internal capability for the prevention, detection, and response to cyber incidents. The program must be aligned with international best practices and enable collaboration between them.

Article 32 - The establishment must identify and assess the security risks of mobile payment services and must continuously monitor these risks.
It must conduct periodic tests of security procedures and systems.

Article 33 - In order to protect the confidentiality and integrity of mobile payment user data, the establishment must:

- Define access rules and have access control systems that manage authorization identification, authentication, access approval, and entity accountability through login credentials.
- Restrict physical access to systems and limit access to customer data to authorized personnel.

Article 34 - The establishment is required to comply, at a minimum, with the following rules:

- Transactions can only be initiated after the prior steps of user authentication.
- Repeated entry of incorrect authentication information triggers a supplementary authentication mechanism or a block of the payment method. **Paragraph 4: Surveillance Reporting Rules**

Decides:

Article 1: Subject
The purpose of this circular is to define the conditions for granting financial assistance by the Central Bank of Tunisia to banks and financial institutions, as provided for by Articles 19, 20, and 21 of Law No. 2016-35 of April 25, 2016, relating to the Statutes of the Central Bank of Tu ** Article 6: Applicable Interest Rate**
The interest rate applicable to financial assistance operations shall be equal to the lending facility rate plus a margin of at least 250 basis points.

**

Article 7: Duration of Financial Assistance**
Financial assistance is granted for a period not exceeding three months. However, the Central Bank of Tunisia may, if applicable, renew this assistance a maximum of three times, provided that the total duration of such assistance does not exceed 12 months and that the bank or financial institution meets, at the time of the renewal request, the eligibility conditions set out in

Article 2 of this circular.

**

Article 8: Eligible Assets and Guarantees**
The Central Bank of Tunisia may accept, within the framework of financial assistance, any asset or guarantee approved by its Board of Directors, by applying adequate haircuts set out in a bilateral agreement between the Central Bank of Tunisia and the bank or financial institution, as referred to in

Article 9 of this circular.

**

Article 9: Financial Assistance Agreement**
Before benefiting from financial assistance, the bank or financial institution must conclude an agreement with the Central Bank of Tunisia, which shall notably specify:
the obligations of the parties, the terms and conditions for providing liquidity, the categories of assets to be presented as collateral, the terms of their transfer, as well as the haircut rates to be applied to these assets.

**

Article 10: Supervision by the Central Bank of Tunisia**
In order to ensure the reliability of the information provided on the collateral created and the proper execution of the liquidity and/or solvency recovery plan provided for in Article 4 of this circular, the Central Bank of Tunisia may, at any time, conduct specific on-site audits. FOURTH PART

Article 1: A loan granted at an excessive interest rate is constituted by any conventional loan granted at an **overall effective interest rate** which exceeds, at the time it is granted, by more than one-fifth¹ the average effective rate practiced during the preceding semester by banks and financial institutions for operations of the same nature.

The Central Bank of Tunisia determines the operations that are subject to the same excessive interest rate.

Sales operations with payment facilities are assimilated to conventional loans and are subject to the provisions of this law.

Article 2: For the determination of the **overall effective interest rate** of the loan, account shall be taken, in addition to interest, of all fees, commissions, or remuneration of any kind, direct or indirect, incurred in the granting of the loan, except for those exempted by decree.

The methods for calculating the **overall effective interest rate** and the average effective rate, as well as their publication mode, are fixed by decree.

Article 3: The **overall effective interest rate** provided for by

Article 2 of this law must be mentioned in any writing establishing a loan agreement governed by this law.

In the event that the said rate is not mentioned, the average effective interest rate practiced during the preceding semester will be taken into account, and the lender shall be liable to a fine ranging from five hundred to three thousand dinars.

Article 4: In case of the application of an excessive interest rate, the sums unduly received by the lender shall be returned to the borrower, increased by interest calculated at the legal rate provided for by Article 1100 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts, from the date of their receipt.

The period rate is calculated actuarially, based on a unit period corresponding to the periodicity of payments made by the borrower.

It ensures, according to the compound interest method, equality between, on the one hand, the sums lent and, on the other hand, all payments due by the borrower for this loan, in capital, interest, fees, commissions, or remuneration of any direct or indirect nature involved in granting credit, these elements being, where applicable, estimated. The period rate is obtained by applying the following formula:

These overdrafts give rise to the collection of interest and commissions provided for by the bank for current account advances.

CHAPTER 4
TERM ACCOUNTS AND BONDS AND OTHER FINANCIAL PRODUCTS Article 141: Banks are authorized to open term accounts, to issue registered cash bonds, as well as any other financial product. **

Article 20:** Interest payable in arrears on term accounts, treasury bills, or any other financial product shall be calculated on the basis of a 365-day year using the following formula:

I = ctn/36500

where:
I = amount of interest
c = principal amount invested
t = interest rate for the investment period
n = exact number of days, from the day after opening or subscription up to and including the maturity date.

When the investment period is less than one year, the interest is payable in a single installment at maturity.

When the investment period is more than one year, interest is payable at the end of each one-year period and at maturity for the remaining fraction of a year.

Interest payable in advance on treasury bills or any other financial product shall be calculated according to the rational interest method (or discount calculation) using the following formula:

I = ctn/36500 + tn

where:
I = amount of interest
c = principal amount invested
t = interest rate for the investment period
n = exact number of days, from the day after subscription up to and including the maturity date.

Article 1: General Provisions**
This circular sets out the conditions for implementing the monetary policy of the Central Bank of Tunisia.
Adherence to the conditions for implementing monetary policy as provided for in Annexes II, III, and IV of this circular is required for any counterparty to access monetary policy operations. Adherence is confirmed by the signature of the adherence form which is the subject of Annex I of this circular.
The practical arrangements and procedures for executing monetary policy operations are described in the Operations Manual, which is the subject of Annex II of this circular.
The provision of liquidity by the Central Bank of Tunisia is conditional upon the mobilization of appropriate collateral in its favor, in the form of negotiable assets and/or non-negotiable assets that meet the eligibility criteria as set by the Central Bank of Tunisia. The rules governing the mobilization of negotiable assets and non-negotiable assets are set out respectively in Annexes III and IV of this circular.

**

Article 2: Eligible Counterparties**
The following conditions aim to allow a wide range of counterparties to access monetary policy operations according to uniform prudential and operational eligibility criteria.
Eligible counterparties for monetary policy operations are banks within the meaning of Law No. 2016-48 of July 11, 2016, relating to banks and financial institutions, and which cumulatively meet the following conditions:
- They must be financially sound, in accordance with the assessment made by the Central Bank of Tunisia, particularly based on capital and liquidity ratios, regularly communicated by the banks; and
- They meet the operational criteria set by the Central Bank.

Article 5: Categories of Operations Initiated by the Central Bank of Tunisia

Operations initiated by the Central Bank of Tunisia consist of four categories of operations defined as follows:

- **Main Refinancing Operations:** These operations constitute the main tool for providing liquidity by the Central Bank of Tunisia. They play a key role in steering interest rates and signal the orientation of monetary policy. The minimum interest rate applied to main refinancing operations is the key rate of the Central Bank of Tunisia. This is set by the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Tunisia in a manner consistent with the ultimate objective of price stability.

- **Longer-Term Refinancing Operations:** The purpose of these operations is to provide additional liquidity for maturities longer than that of main refinancing operations.

- **Fine-Tuning Operations:** These operations are carried out on a case-by-case basis to correct the effect of unforeseen fluctuations in banking liquidity on interest rates. They have a duration shorter than that of main refinancing operations.

- **Structural Operations:** These operations aim to manage a situation of durable liquidity deficit or surplus.

Article 6: Instruments for Executing Operations Initiated by the Central Bank of Tunisia

Main refinancing operations and longer-term refinancing operations are exclusively carried out by means of repurchase agreements in the form of secured loans or reverse repurchase agreements as defined in Article 2 of the Monetary Policy Operations Manual, which is the subject of Annex II of this circular.

Fine-tuning operations may be carried out by means of repurchase agreements, foreign exchange swaps for policy purposes. Here is the English translation of TITLE IV: ELIGIBLE ASSETS

Article 15: Definition of Eligible Assets
In order to protect the balance sheet of the Central Bank of Tunisia against credit risk, refinancing operations are carried out on the basis of appropriate collateral.
To this end, the Central Bank of Tunisia accepts negotiable assets, including public and private negotiable debt securities, and non-negotiable assets representing bank claims on companies and individuals, as collateral for refinancing operations, in accordance with the criteria established within the framework of this circular.

Article 17: Eligibility Criteria for Non-Negotiable Assets
Non-negotiable assets accepted as collateral for refinancing operations must meet the following eligibility criteria:
- be bank claims denominated in Tunisian dinars and representing a debtor's commitments to a counterparty Article 17 bis - Eligible Assets in Exceptional Circumstances
In exceptional circumstances, the Central Bank of Tunisia may accept, as collateral for refinancing operations, negotiable and non-negotiable assets that do not meet the eligibility criteria set out in Articles 16 and 17 of this circular and Articles 51 and 52 of its Appendix II.

Article 1**

**Subject and scope**

1. This Monetary Policy Operations Manual sets out the practical arrangements for the implementation of the monetary policy of the Central Bank of Tunisia (hereinafter referred to as the Central Bank), as defined by Chapter One of Title 2 of the Law Governing the Statutes of the Central Bank.

The scope of this Manual does not include measures relating to the exercise of the Central Bank's powers outside of monetary policy: in particular, the scope of this Manual does not include measures relating to the oversight of payment systems and methods, such as intraday credit (Chapter 3 of Title 2 of the Law Governing the Statutes of the Central Bank), financial stability, such as financial assistance (Chapter 4 of Title 2 of the Law Governing the Statutes of the Central Bank), and foreign exchange policy and reserve management (Chapter 5 of Title 2 of the Law Governing the Statutes of the Central Bank). 2.

2. The Central Bank shall take all appropriate measures to implement its monetary policy operations in accordance with the principles, tools, instruments, conditions, criteria, and procedures set out in this Manual. 3. The Central Bank reserves the right to request from, and obtain from, counterparties any relevant information necessary for the accomplishment of its missions and the achievement of its objectives within the framework of monetary policy operations. This right is without prejudice to any other existing specific right of the Central Bank to request information relating to monetary policy operations.

The Marginal Lending Facility

Article 17

Characteristics of the Marginal Lending Facility

1. Counterparties may use the marginal lending facility to obtain twenty-four-hour liquidity from the Central Bank, through a repurchase agreement in the form of a secured loan or repo, at a predetermined interest rate by using eligible assets as collateral.

2. There is no limit to the amount of liquidity that can be provided under the marginal lending facility, as long as the obligation to provide appropriate collateral in accordance with paragraph 3 is met.

3. Assets presented by counterparties must be previously deposited with the Central Bank in the case of private claims or delivered at the time of application for access to the marginal lending facility in the case of negotiable securities. Failure to comply with this access condition shall result in penalties in accordance with

Article 69 of this Manual.

Article 18

Conditions of Access to the Marginal Lending Facility

1. Counterparties meeting the eligibility criteria for counterparties and having an account with the Central Bank of Tunisia may access the marginal lending facility.

2. Access to the marginal lending facility is limited to days when the SGMT is operational. On days when securities settlement systems are not operational, access to the marginal lending facility is granted based on eligible assets that have already been previously deposited with the Central Bank.

3. To access the marginal lending facility, the counterparty must submit a request to the Central Bank. The Central Bank processes the request on the same day within the SGMT, provided that it receives the request no later than the provisional closing time of the SGMT. The deadline for submitting the request for access to the facil CHAPTER 2
The Deposit Facility

Article 20
Characteristics of the Deposit Facility

1. Counterparties may use the deposit facility to make overnight deposits with the Central Bank; a predetermined interest rate being applied to these deposits.

2. The Central Bank provides no collateral in exchange for the deposits.

3. There is no limit to the amount a counterparty can deposit under this facility.

Article 21
Conditions for Access to the Deposit Facility

1. Counterparties meeting the eligibility criteria for counterparties may access the deposit facility. Access to the deposit facility is limited to days when the TARGET system is operational.

2. To gain access to the deposit facility, the counterparty must submit a request to the Central Bank. The Central Bank processes the request on the same day within the TARGET system, provided it receives the request no later than the provisional closing time of TARGET. The deadline for submitting a request to access the deposit facility is extended by an additional fifteen minutes on the last business day of a reserve maintenance period. The request indicates the amount to be deposited under this facility.

Article 22
Duration and Interest Rate of the Deposit Facility

1. Deposits made under the deposit facility are for twenty-four hours. Deposits held under the deposit facility mature on the following day when the TARGET system is operational, at the opening of this system.

2. The interest rate applicable to the deposit is announced in advance by the Central Bank and is calculated in the form of a simple interest rate according to the "actual number of days/360" convention.

3. Interest on deposits is payable on the maturity of the deposit.

Article 36**

**Adjudication during multi-rate tender procedures concerning foreign exchange swaps intended to provide liquidity**

In a multi-rate foreign exchange swap tender procedure intended to provide liquidity, counterparties' bids are awarded as follows:

a) The list of submissions is established in descending order of forward/backwardation rates, taking into account the sign of the quotation;
b) The sign of the quotation depends on the sign of the interest rate differential between the foreign currency and the dinar. For the swap maturity b) The sign of the quotation depends on the sign of the interest rate differential between the currency and the dinar. For the swap maturity:

i.

If the currency's interest rate is higher than the corresponding interest rate for the dinar, the forward/backwardation rate is negative, meaning the dinar is quoted in forward against the currency; and
ii. If the currency's interest rate is lower than the corresponding interest rate for the dinar, the forward/backwardation rate is positive, meaning the dinar is quoted in backwardation against the currency;

c) Bids with the lowest forward/backwardation rates are satisfied first; subsequent, higher bids are then accepted until the total amount of dinars to be repurchased is exhausted.

d) If, at the highest accepted forward/backwardation rate (i.e., the marginal forward/backwardation rate), the aggregate amount of bids exceeds the residual amount to be awarded, the latter is awarded pro rata to the bids, based on the ratio between the residual amount to be awarded and the total amount of bids at the marginal forward/backwardation rate.

e) The amount awarded to each counterparty is rounded to the nearest million dinars.

b) to the rights of holders of debt securities of the same issuer.

**

Article 55**

**Absence of Business Relationships between the Counterparty and the Issuer or Debtor**

1. Counterparties submitting eligible assets must ensure that these assets are not issued or guaranteed by themselves.

2. They must also ensure that they have no business relationship with the issuer or debtor, as defined by the prevailing regulations.

**

Article 56 (new)** (Amended by Circular to Banks No. 2018-08 of October 5, 2018)

**Allocation of Collateral for Refinancing Operations between Tradable and Non-Tradable Assets**

Counterparties must ensure, at all times, that the allocation of collateral for refinancing operations between tradable and non-tradable assets complies with the quotas published by the Central Bank of Tunisia on its CAER system and its website.

Article 57**

Article 59**

**Mobilization of Tradable Assets**

1. Tradable assets can be mobilized through secured lending techniques or repurchase agreements.

2. Within the framework of the agreement forming the subject of Annex III of this circular, between the Central Bank, the counterparty, and Tunisie Clearing, it is possible for counterparties to generate a message through the CAER system, which will be sent to Tunisie Clearing, in order to transfer the tradable assets to the Central Bank's securities account held with Tunisie Clearing. The asset will become available for use as collateral immediately after confirmation by Tunisie Clearing of the transfer to the benefit of the Central Bank.

3. The transmission to the Central Bank by counterparties of instructions to transfer tradable assets via the CAER system replaces sending matched instructions by both parties to Tunisie Clearing, significantly simplifying and accelerating the collateral mobilization process.

4. Mobilization messages can be generated from the beginning of the day until the provisional closing time of the SGMT. Orders sent too late after the system closes and not processed during that business day will be rejected by the system.

**

Article 60**

**Demobilization of Tradable Assets**

The demobilization of tradable assets provided for collateral purposes can only be initiated by the Central Bank via a return instruction to Tunisie Clearing after the full reimbursement of the amount due by the counterparty, in principal and interest.

At the end of each transaction, the assets assigned to that transaction for collateral purposes are demobilized, and the counterparty must resubmit the assets if it plans to participate in a subsequent transaction. If the situation does not allow for the demobilization of assets, the Central Bank may use a netting method. **

Article 63**

**Method of Mobilization of Non-Negotiable Assets**

1. Counterparties may mobilize bank claims by means of assignment of bank claims deeds. These assignment deeds shall result in the delivery to the Central Bank of slips entitled "assignment deeds," the model of which is annexed to the mobilization agreement, referencing Law No. 2000-92 of October 31, 2000, relating to deeds of assignment or pledge of professional claims and the mobilization of related credit.

2. The delivery of the said slips may be carried out by ordinary mail, fax, SWIFT, messaging, or by any computer file that leaves a written trace and presents a sufficient degree of reliability and security for both parties. The absence of confirmation of receipt of a slip shall not affect the validity of the assignment deed in any way.

**

Article 64**

**Control of Non-Negotiable Assets**

1. The Central Bank may at any time take all necessary measures, including on-site inspections, to verify the information provided concerning claims lodged for collateral.

2. Under the mobilization agreement for non-negotiable assets, which is the subject of Annex IV of this circular, the Central Bank may conduct checks and investigations to ascertain the actual existence of the bank claims lodged as collateral.

3. The Central Bank requires, at least quarterly, written confirmation from each counterparty, whereby the latter certifies:

a) that the bank claims actually exist;
b) that the bank claims comply with the applied eligibility criteria;
c) that the bank claim in question is not simultaneously being used as collateral for the benefit of a third party;
d) that it undertakes to inform the Central Bank, no later than the following business day, of any event affecting **PART FOUR**

Article 67**

**Penalties for breaches concerning mandatory reserves**

Any shortfall compared to the amount required for the mandatory reserve shall result in the collection by the Central Bank of interest calculated over the reserve formation period at the rate of the standing lending facility plus 2.5 percentage points.

** Article 68**

**Measures taken in case of breaches of certain operational rules**

1. In accordance with the contractual provisions applied by the Central Bank, measures shall be taken against counterparties who breach any of the following obligations:

    a) With regard to repurchase agreements and foreign exchange swaps for monetary policy purposes, the obligations to adequately guarantee and settle the amount awarded to the counterparty throughout the duration of a specific operation, in accordance with

Article 68, paragraph 1, point a) or b), as applicable.

2. Any suspension imposed by the Central Bank under paragraph 1 applies to any monetary policy operation initiated by the Central Bank thereafter.

3. The suspension period imposed under paragraph 1 is determined in accordance with Annex II.4.

4. If a counterparty fails to comply with an obligation referred to in

Article 68, paragraph 1, point c).

5. In exceptional cases, the Central Bank may suspend a counterparty's access, for a period of three months, to all future monetary policy operations of the Central Bank in the event of a breach of any of the obligations provided for in Article 68, paragraph 1. In such a case, the Central Bank shall take into account the seriousness of the case and, in particular, the amounts involved as well as the frequency and duration of the breach.

6. The suspension period imposed by the Central Bank under this article applies in **PART FIVE**
**DISCRETIONARY MEASURES**

**

Article 71**

Discretionary measures taken under the precautionary principle or following a case of default

1. Under the precautionary principle, the Central Bank may take any of the following discretionary measures:

a) Suspend, limit, or prohibit a counterparty's access to operations initiated by the Central Bank or to standing facilities;

b) Refuse assets pledged as collateral for central bank credit operations by a given counterparty, limit their use, or apply additional haircuts to them, based on any information deemed relevant by the Central Bank, particularly if the counterparty's credit quality is closely correlated with the credit quality of the pledged assets.

2. Where a measure initiated by the Central Bank, as described in paragraph 1, is based on prudential information, the Central Bank shall use such information to the extent strictly necessary for the performance of its monetary policy tasks.

3. In the event of a default, the Central Bank may suspend, limit, or prohibit access to operations initiated by the Central Bank or to the Central Bank's standing facilities for counterparties in default.

4. All discretionary measures taken under paragraphs 1 and 3 shall be applied in a proportionate and non-discriminatory manner and shall be duly justified by the Central Bank. SIXTH PART, FINAL PROVISIONS

Article 72. Regulation in matters of fighting against money laundering and terrorism financing

The counterparties to the Monetary Policy operations of the Central Bank are deemed to be aware of all the obligations imposed on them by the regulation in matters of fighting against money laundering and terrorism financing, and they comply with these obligations.
