SUBJECT: Procedures for granting, controlling, and refinancing credits. TITLE ONE
PRELIMINARY PROVISIONS
Article 1: Short, medium, and long-term credits are no longer subject to prior authorization and refinancing approval formalities.

Article 2: Banks must comply with the credit granting standards set by this circular.2
They must also ensure that the support provided is the most appropriate in form, volume, and duration to the real needs of the clientele.

Article 2bis:
Repealed by circular n°2007-25 of 19/11/2007

Article 3: The Central Bank of Tunisia controls the credits dispensed by banks in accordance with the procedures outlined in Title 3.2.
These credits become due upon the completion of campaigns, the durations of which are set out in Annex II.

Article 6: Olive Oil Start-up Credits.

These contributions are granted to olive oil producers to cover manufacturing costs and the settlement of oils purchased from producers while awaiting the formation of stacks by the ONH (National Olive Oil Office).

The credit amount is limited to financing quantities of oil equivalent to the storage capacity of the oil mill, without exceeding 15% of crushing forecasts. It is calculated on the basis of the reference prices specified in Annex III.

The due date for this credit is set at June 30th of each year.

Article 7: Advances on Goods.

These credits are granted to cover the cash flow needs of businesses arising from holding stocks of agricultural products in their natural state, packaged, or processed, pending their gradual sale.

The credit amount is equal to:

*   80% of the value of the peak stock identified from the projected stock variation statement for preserves, dates, almonds, seafood products, olive oils held by collectors, and olive pomace oils;
*   100% of the value of the peak stock of olive oils held by the ONH;
*   100% of the value of the projected collection for cereals, legumes, and wines.

The calculation of the credit amount and the stock valuation are carried out on the basis of the reference prices specified in Annex III.

Article 7 bis: Credits financing the acquisition, transport, and storage of dry fodder and bran. **

Article 10: Commercial Discount on Exports and Mobilization of Claims Arising Abroad.**

This credit is intended to mobilize claims arising abroad.

The amount of this facility is determined based on export turnover and the payment terms granted, provided that the maturity of the drafts does not exceed 360 days.⁶

**

Article 11: Pre-financing of Public Procurement.**

This type of facility is intended to cover expenses incurred by the start-up work of contracts concluded with the Administration.

The amount of credit allocated must not exceed 10% of the value of new contracts, after deduction of advances from the Administration.

Repayment of this credit will be made by a deduction of at least 10% from each interim payment for services rendered.

**

Article 12: Advances on Administrative Claims**

This facility is intended to finance claims arising from the Administration.

The amount of credit must not exceed 80% of the amount of the duly established claim.

** Article 13: Commercial Discount on Tunisia.**

This facility is intended to mobilize credit sales of products to be resold as is or after transformation.

The amount of this facility is determined based on credit sales turnover and the payment terms granted, provided that the maturity of the drafts does not exceed 3 months.

**

Article 14: Non-Mobilizable Credit**

This type of facility is intended to meet temporary cash flow needs arising from mismatches between revenue and expenditure flows.

The amount of this credit generally ranges between 15 days and one month of turnover.

Article 15:** Medium-term credits are generally granted

Working capital must not exceed 10% of the investment amount.

Article 18 bis7: Medium-term credit financing privatization.

This credit is intended to finance the purchase of a controlling stake or assets of a public enterprise as part of the privatization program and is granted directly to the acquirers.

The credit, the amount of which must not exceed 70% of the operation's cost, must be repaid from the acquirers' own revenues and not by the privatized company.

Article 19: Medium-term consolidation, recovery, and restructuring credits.

These credits are intended for:

- consolidating short-term credits to restore the balance of the financial structure in accordance with the provisions of Article 18 above.
- restructuring the production apparatus, notably through the acquisition of new technologies to improve productivity, quality, and competitiveness.
- facilitating the takeover and revival of companies in difficulty.

Article 20 (new) 8: Medium-term export credits.

This support is intended to finance receivables from abroad with settlement terms exceeding one year, resulting from authorized export transactions within the framework of circular n° 86-12 of May 5, 1986, concerning the financial settlement of exports and the repatriation of their proceeds.

The amount of the The portion of the credit whose duration must not exceed 3 years is limited to 70% of the repair costs.

Article 23 bis (new)11: Medium-term credit financing the acquisition and breeding of purebred heifers born in Tunisia.
This support is intended to finance the acquisition and breeding of purebred heifers born in Tunisia and covers 80% of the acquisition cost of the heifer and breeding expenses.
The credit, whose duration is fixed at 27 months, must be disbursed in accordance with the scale set out in the attached Appendix IV bis and repaid in a single installment.

Article 24: Medium-term credit for production.
These supports are intended to finance the credit sale of capital goods or services to investors.
However, for solar water heaters and pumping wind turbines, the final buyer can be any natural or legal person.
The amount of credit is fixed according to the volume of credit sales and the payment period granted to final buyers.
The credit portion is limited to 80% of the credit sales amount.
For solar water heaters and pumping wind turbines, this portion is increased to 90% of the total amount of equipment and installation costs.
The beneficiaries of these credits must pass on to the final buyers the interest rate and duration conditions applied to them by the banks.
The list of goods or services eligible for financing is provided in Appendix V.

Article 25: Medium-term credit for the acquisition of transport equipment.
These credits are • For projects with an investment exceeding fifty thousand dinars:

▪ At least 10% equity for the investment tranche equal to ten thousand dinars;
▪ At least 20% equity for the investment tranche greater than ten thousand dinars and less than or equal to fifty thousand dinars;
▪ At least 40% equity for the investment tranche greater than fifty thousand dinars and less than or equal to one hundred thousand dinars.

Promoters belonging to needy families registered in the national poverty register or categories with specific needs who cannot provide evidence of the cash personal contribution required for the financing of their projects, benefit from a repayable grant representing 100% of the equity.

The amortization schedules for these loans must provide for annual or more frequent payments of amounts towards the principal and interest calculated according to the constant annuity formula; the interest rate being the rate equivalent to the chosen repayment period.

The first installment must be due no earlier than three months and no later than one year after the project's operational start date.

This form of assistance is intended to finance the opening or expansion of medical, veterinary, or radiology practices, pharmacies, medical analysis laboratories, and accounting expertise firms, audit firms, or even study or engineering offices.

The Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia,

Considering Law n°2016 -35 of April 25, 2016 establishing the status of the Central Bank of Tunisia; Considering Law n°2016 -48 of July 11, 2016 relating to banks and financial institutions; Considering Circular n°87 -47 of the Central Bank of Tunisia of December 23, 1987 on the modalities for granting, controlling, and refinancing of credits, as amended and supplemented by subsequent texts; Considering Circular n°91 -24 of the Central Bank of Tunisia of December 17, 1991 relating to the division, coverage of risks, and monitoring of commitments, as amended and supplemented by subsequent texts;

Considering Circular n°2017 -02 of the Central Bank of Tunisia of March 10, 2017 relating to the implementation of monetary policy by the Central Bank of Tunisia,
Considering the opinion of the Compliance Control Committee n° 12 -2019 of December 18, 2019,

Decides:

Article One - Banks and financial institutions may proceed with the rescheduling of principal and interest payment deadlines for credits granted to oil producers and olive oil exporters who have encountered difficulties in repaying their debts during the 2017/2018 and 2018/2019 campaigns.

The rescheduling shall be done on a case-by-case basis and for a duration that takes into account the repayment capacity of each beneficiary. Banks and financial institutions may grant new financing to beneficiaries of rescheduled credits for the 2019/2020 campaign.

Article 2 - Banks and financial institutions that have proceeded with rescheduling and granting new financing within the meaning of Article One of this circular may, during the year 2019, maintain the classification determined at f Article 3 - Banks and financial institutions must, when calculating collective provisions, assign the oil producers sector and the olive oil export sector to specific categories within the reference methodology for calculating these provisions, as provided for in Annex 3 of the Circular of the Central Bank of Tunisia No. 91-24 of December 17, 1991, while applying the following minimum provisioning rates:

| Sectors                   | Minimum Provision Rate |
| :------------------------ | :--------------------- |
| Oil Producers             | 35%                    |
| Olive Oil Exporters       | 30%                    |

Article 4 - Banks and financial institutions are required to communicate monthly to the Central Bank of Tunisia, via the data exchange system, the list of companies that have benefited from treatment measures, indicating the nature of the measure, in accordance with the table that forms the annex to this circular.

Article 5 - This circular comes into force as of the date of its publication. **Annex to Circular to Banks and Credit Institutions No. 2019-12 of December 18, 2019**

**Margin Management**

**1.

Determination of the value difference of a delivery pension convention with margin and the net balance of each party:**

**1.1.** On each valuation date, the calculation agent shall determine, for each delivery pension convention with margin outstanding on that date, the positive or negative difference between:

(i) the value of the securities delivered under a repurchase agreement, adjusted by the initial safety margin (if any); and

(ii) the sale price of the said securities increased by the accrued interest thereon, calculated at the rate of the delivery pension convention, from the date of sale (inclusive) to the valuation date under consideration (exclusive).

**1.2.** Once this difference has been determined, the calculation agent shall calculate for each party the value difference of each outstanding delivery pension convention with margin, which shall be equal to:

(i) for any delivery pension convention for which the party concerned is the seller, to the difference between the two amounts referred to above, and of the same sign as this difference;

(ii) for any delivery pension convention for which the party concerned is the buyer, to the difference between the two amounts referred to above, but with the opposite sign.

**1.3.** Once the value difference of each delivery pension convention with margin has been determined, the calculation agent shall determine the net balance of the value differences of each party (hereinafter referred to as the "net balance"), which shall be equal to the algebraic sum of the value differences of that party for each of the outstanding delivery pension conventions with margin.

**2.

Provision or retrocession of margin based on the net balance:**

CIRCULAR TO BANKS NO.

2018-12 OF NOVEMBER 28, 2018

**Subject: Interbank Market in Dinars**

Having regard to Law No. 2016-35 of April 25, 2016, fixing the statute of the Central Bank of Tunisia,

Having regard to Law No. 2016-48 of July 11, 2016, relating to banks and financial institutions,

Having regard to Law No. 2012-24 of December 24, 2012, relating to the repurchase agreement,

Having regard to Circular to Credit Institutions No. 2005-09 of July 14, 2005, relating to the organization of the money market, as amended and supplemented by subsequent texts,

Having regard to Circular to Credit Institutions and Authorized Intermediaries No. 2008-07 of March 13, 2008, relating to the use of the "SED" data exchange system,

Having regard to the Circular of the Central Bank of Tunisia No. 2013-05 of April 30, 2013, concerning a framework agreement for repurchase agreements,

Having regard to Circular to Banks No. 2017-02 of March 10, 2017, relating to the implementation of monetary policy by the Central Bank of Tunisia,

Having regard to the deliberation of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Tunisia dated June 13, 2018,

Having regard to Opinion No. 10-2018 of the Control and Compliance Committee dated November 16, 2018, as provided for by

Article 42 of Law No. 2016-35 of April 25, 2016, fixing the statute of the Central Bank of Tunisia,

**Decides:**

**TITLE ONE: SUBJECT, SCOPE AND DEFINITIONS**

** Article 1: Subject and Scope**
The purpose of this circular is to define the conditions, procedures, and processes for liquidity exchange within the interbank market in dinars. It applies to banks as defined by Law No. 2016-48 of July 11, 2016, relating to banks and financial institutions.

**

Article 2: Definitions**
"Contributing Bank": a bank that is part of the panel of contributors to TUNIBOR.
"Underlying Contributions to TUNIBOR": "SGMT," the Tunisian large-value payment system, enabling gross real-time settlement of payments in dinar.

"Trading System," a secure and reliable system for the electronic trading of interbank transactions.

"Reference Interest Rates," interest rates calculated and published daily by the Central Bank of Tunisia, applying a formula to underlying data from interbank transactions or contributions made by the panel of TUNIBOR contributors.

"TM," the average overnight interest rate on the interbank market.

"Unsecured Interbank Transaction," an interbank transaction without collateral.

"Interbank Transaction," an exchange of liquidity concluded between two banks in the form of an unsecured transaction or a repurchase agreement.

"TUNIBOR," abbreviation for 'Tunisian interbank offered rate,' representing the average interest rate at which contributing banks are willing to grant each other unsecured loans for each of the maturities ranging from one week to twelve months: one week, two weeks, one month, two months, three months, six months, nine months, and twelve months.

TITLE II: QUOTING, TRADING, AND REPORTING OF INTERBANK TRANSACTIONS

Article 3: Obligation to Display Quotations

Banks are required to continuously display their indicative bid and ask conditions for liquidity in dinar for maturities ranging from overnight to one year. This obligation also applies to banks engaged in operations consistent with the principles of Islamic finance as provided for by current regulations, particularly Articles 11 to 16 of Law No. 2016-48 of July 11, 2016, relating to banks and financial institutions.

The display of rate quotations must be carried out through contribution pages broadcast over secure information networks. **

Article 7: Negotiation of Interbank Transactions**
Regardless of the form that the exchange of liquidity in dinars takes on the interbank market, banks are
required to use a trading system that guarantees the traceability and security of transactions, such as
Reuters or Bloomberg.
The Central Bank of Tunisia may remotely access real-time data on interbank transactions
carried out via the said trading system without prior authorization from the
banks.

**

Article 8: Declarations of Interbank Transactions by Banks**
Banks are required to declare to the Central Bank of Tunisia, for each category indicated in Article 6 of this circular, interbank transactions carried out per session, in accordance with
the IT recording structure published on the Data Exchange System (SED).
During the double-session period, two declaration sessions are set for no later than 10:30 AM and 2:00 PM.
For the single-session period, one declaration session is set for no later than 10:30 AM. In case of malfunction
of the Data Exchange System (SED), banks may use fax or, if applicable, any other
communication system that leaves a written record.
Banks must also communicate to the Central Bank of Tunisia, no later than 15 minutes after
the provisional closing of the Tunisia Large Value Payment System (SGMT), a summary of all
interbank transactions for the day, specifying, for each category, the amounts, rates, and durations
processed.

**

Article 9: Information Communicated by the Central Bank of Tunisia**
At the end of each session provided for in Article 8 of this circular, the Central Bank of Tunisia
communicates to the banks a file, for each category of operations, summarizing all
transactions declared, broken down by amount, rate, and duration. **

Article 11: Calculation Methodology for the Overnight Average Interest Rate (TM)**

The overnight average interest rate (TM) is calculated as a weighted average of the overnight lending rates of all interbank unsecured transactions, transmitted at the end of the day to the Central Bank of Tunisia under the conditions set out in Article 8 of this circular. This rate is rounded to the nearest basis point. The Central Bank of Tunisia reserves the right to eliminate outlier rates that do not reflect market conditions.

**

Article 12: Publication of the TM**

The overnight average interest rate (TM) is published at the end of each day by the Central Bank of Tunisia on the data exchange system (SED), and no later than the following day on its website and on the Reuters and Bloomberg platforms.

** Article 13: Panel of TUNIBOR Contributors**

The panel of TUNIBOR contributors comprises the most active banks in the dinar money market that meet the eligibility criteria for counterparties in monetary policy operations as provided for in

Article 2 of Circular No. 2017-02 of March 10, 2017, concerning the implementation of monetary policy by the Central Bank of Tunisia.
To this end, the Central Bank of Tunisia ranks banks at least once a year based on the volume of activity carried out in the various segments of the dinar money market (interbank market, negotiable debt securities market, and refinancing with the Central Bank of Tunisia).
The Central Bank of Tunisia regularly publishes and updates the list of TUNIBOR contributing banks on its website and on the Reuters and Bloomberg platforms.

**

Article 14: Obligations Incumbent on Contributing Banks**

Each contributing bank is required to update its quotations daily before 10:45 AM. The Central Bank of Tunisia ensures that at least half of the banks in the panel of contributors have communicated their lending rates for the 8 maturities before 10:45 AM. If this quorum is not met, the Central Bank of Tunisia may postpone the fixing time for TUNIBOR and informs the market accordingly.

The methodology for calculating TUNIBOR may be modified by the Central Bank of Tunisia, after consulting the banks, to better reflect market realities.

**

Article 16: Publication of TUNIBOR**

TUNIBOR is published every working day at 11:00 AM on the website of the Central Bank of Tunisia and on the Reuters and Bloomberg platforms.

**TITLE IV: FINAL PROVISIONS**

** Article 17: Measures taken in case of default**

The obligations provided for in this circular, incumbent upon the banks, constitute conditions for the implementation of monetary policy within the meaning of circular no. 2017-02 of March 10, 2017, relating to the implementation of monetary policy by the Central Bank of Tunisia. Failure to comply with any of these obligations is subject to the measures provided for in the said circular against the counterparties.

**

Article 18: Repeal**

Title One, as well as the provisions of the first dash of

Article 3, Article 18, and the first paragraph of

Article 20 of circular no. 2005-09 of July 14, 2005, relating to the organization of the money market, are hereby repealed.

Article 5: Credit institutions and non-resident banks supervised on a consolidated basis must ensure that the internal control systems implemented within the companies operating in the financial services sector that they exclusively control are coherent and compatible with each other in order to allow risks to be understood and monitored on a consolidated basis.

They also ensure that the aforementioned internal control systems are adapted to the organization of the group as well as to the nature of the activity of the controlled entities.

TITLE I
INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEM FOR OPERATIONS AND PROCEDURES

Article 6: The internal control system for operations and procedures must enable credit institutions and non-resident banks to:

a) Verify that the operations carried out by the credit institution or the non-resident bank, as well as the internal organization and procedures, comply with current legislative and regulatory provisions, professional and ethical standards and practices, and guidelines Credit institutions and non-resident banks must permanently have an internal audit structure that is independent of operational entities and adapted to their size and the nature of their operations. To this end, they appoint an internal audit manager responsible for ensuring the consistency and effectiveness of the missions mentioned in point b of

Article 7 of this circular, and whose identity and curriculum vitae are communicated to the Central Bank of Tunisia.

When the size of the credit institution does not justify entrusting the responsibilities of permanent and periodic control to different persons, these responsibilities may be entrusted either to a single person, or to the management body which ensures, under the control of the Board of Directors or the Supervisory Board, the coordination of all the mechanisms that contribute to the exercise of this mission.

Article 9: The Board of Directors or the Supervisory Board shall be informed by the management body of the appointment of the persons responsible for the permanent and periodic controls mentioned in Article 8 of this circular. These responsible persons shall report on the performance of their duties to the management body. When the latter or the Board of Directors or the Supervisory Board deems it necessary, they shall also report directly to the Board of Directors or the Supervisory Board or, where applicable, to the permanent internal audit committee.

Article 10: Credit institutions and non-resident banks must ensure that the number and qualification of the persons mentioned in Article 7, as well as the means made available to them, particularly risk monitoring tools and analysis methods, are adapted to their activities and size. **

Article 14:** Credit institutions and non-resident banks shall determine the level of IT security deemed adequate with regard to technological standards and the requirements of their businesses. They shall ensure their information system is adapted to their level of activity and the nature of their risks.

The control of information systems must notably ensure:

a) that the security level is periodically assessed and that, where necessary, corrective actions are taken in a timely manner;
b) that IT backup procedures are available. These procedures must be tested periodically to ensure their proper functioning.

Information and documentation supporting the analysis and execution of programs must be stored under conditions offering maximum security against risks of deterioration, manipulation, or theft.

Article 211:** Credit institutions and non-resident banks shall define reporting procedures at least quarterly to the management body and, where applicable, to the risk monitoring and oversight structures¹ on compliance with risk limits, particularly when overall limits are likely to be reached. Adapted summary statements for monitoring their operations shall be drawn up to inform the management body, the risk monitoring and oversight structure¹, the Board of Directors or the Supervisory Board, and, where applicable, the audit committee.

Article 42: Settlement risk is understood as the risk of a default or difficulties occurring during the period necessary for the settlement of the transaction, which prevent the counterparty of a credit institution or a non-resident bank from delivering the agreed financial instruments or funds to it, while the said credit institution or the said non-resident bank has already fulfilled its commitments to the said counterparty.

Credit institutions and non-resident banks must implement procedures to know their current and future exposure to settlement risk as they conclude new transactions and as unsettled transactions progress through the different phases of the settlement process.

**SUBJECT: Terms of Reference for the Audit of Accounts.**

The Circular of the Central Bank of Tunisia n°91-24 dated December 17, 1991, defined, in its

Article 14, the objectives of the supervisory mission of statutory auditors (or auditors) of banks. To this end, statutory auditors (or auditors) must expressly provide, within their reports, their conclusions on:

*   The internal control systems implemented by the bank,
*   The accounting principles applied to various operations and the justification of accounts,
*   Credit policies, debt recovery, and the monitoring of commitments,
*   The valuation of assets included on or off the balance sheet,
*   The accounting for income from credit operations and provisions made for the coverage of risks.

In addition, statutory auditors (or auditors) must issue independent opinions and detailed reports relating to the following annual financial statements:

*   Balance sheet as of the end of the year,
*   Income statement for the financial year ending at the end of the same year,
*   Profit and loss account for the same financial year,
*   Cash flow statement for the same financial year. These reports and opinions must be prepared in accordance with the standards of the Order of Chartered Accountants of Tunisia, as well as the recommendations of the International Accounting Standards Committee (IASC) and those of the IFAC.

The reports to be provided by statutory auditors (or auditors) to the Central Bank of Tunisia must contain the following documents, including a sufficient number of details and annexes to support the conclusions and opinions reached by the auditors:

1°) Financial statements 9°) An assessment of foreign exchange risk. The statutory auditors (or auditors) must determine the extent of actual and potential foreign exchange risk losses and evaluate the adequacy of information systems in identifying foreign exchange risks and the accounting procedures used to reflect them.

10°) An assessment of interest rate risk and liquidity management (assets and liabilities); the statutory auditors (or auditors) must report on any significant risk related to changes in interest or liquidity rates to assess management's ability to manage loss risks.

11°) an opinion on the adequacy of capital. To the extent that capital is inadequate to support current and future operations, the auditor shall recommend the amount of additional capital required. SCOPE AND TERMS OF THE AUDIT

When the financial statements do not reflect the true and fair view of the bank's or financial institution's situation, the statutory auditors (or auditors) must detail and quantify the necessary adjustments. Emphasis should be placed on: (a) the adequacy of loss provisions and the necessary adjustments to bring valuation provisions to adequate levels; (b) adjustments to profit and loss accounts relating to recognized income from assets in classes 2, 3, and 4; (c) adjustments to profit and loss accounts for accrued and unpaid interest that has been capitalized, renegotiated, or refinanced; and (d) extraordinary or non-recurring income.

9°) Identify, quantify, and assess credit concentrations, with an emphasis on credit granted to: (a) insiders of the institution and their related interests (shareholders, directors, and executives); (b) parties related to the bank, including subsidiaries and affiliates; and (c) major economic sectors. The Central Bank of Tunisia requires banks to classify all their assets, regardless of their form, whether they appear on the balance sheet or off-balance sheet, and whether they are denominated in dinars or foreign currencies. Provisions constituted must also be made specifically for any asset classified as equal to or greater than 50 thousand dinars or 0.5% of net own funds.

The valuation must cover at least 80% of the total balance sheet and off-balance sheet assets, and in particular:

a) All assets in dispute, doubtful, or litigious, as well as those subject to reservations of interest or that have experienced a payment incident of any kind.

b) All renegotiated loans and advances.

c) All credit facilities granted to shareholders holding more than 5% of the bank's capital, to directors, and to the bank's management.

d) All ordinary assets exceeding 100 thousand dinars, and particularly credit facilities (loans, participations, and others) granted to beneficiaries affiliated with the same group as defined by

Article 2 of BCT Circular No. 91-24 of December 17, 1991.

e) Seized or repossessed real estate, conditional commitments and guarantees, and miscellaneous assets must also be valued. When assessing the quality of assets, emphasis must be placed on the borrower's ability to generate liquid funds to repay their debts. Guarantees obtained should only be considered of secondary importance, especially when they consist of goodwill or operational fixed assets.

Article 2:**
This circular applies to banks and financial institutions within the meaning of Law No. 2016-48, with the exception of payment institutions.
Hereinafter referred to as "the establishments".
Branches of banks established in Tunisia before the promulgation of the aforementioned Law No. 2016-48 and having their registered office abroad are excluded from the scope of this circular. However, these branches are required to submit to the Central Bank of Tunisia an annual report, particularly concerning the governance framework applied by the parent company to the branch, as well as the risk management and compliance policy and strategy. This report must be approved by the parent company's management body.

**

Article 3:**
For the purposes of this circular, the following shall be understood as:

**Risk Appetite:** the overall level and type of risk an institution is willing to assume to achieve its strategic objectives and business plan.

**Governance Framework:** the set of rules governing the relationships between, on the one hand, governance bodies, namely: the management body, the executive body, and the committees, and on the other hand, stakeholders. The governance framework defines, in particular, the powers and responsibilities of the different governance bodies as well as the decision-making mechanisms within the institution.

**Committees:** audit, risk, and nomination and remuneration committees as referred to in Articles 49, 50, and 51 of Law No.

2016-48.

**Conflicts of Interest:** a situation where the personal interests of a member of the management body or executive body or staff, or those of persons with whom they have a close family tie, or financial and strategic interests, are not compatible with the interests of the institution.

**Risk Culture:** the set of norms, **Stakeholders:** they refer to all individuals who are in direct contact with an establishment's activities and who can influence or be influenced by the achievement of the establishment's objectives. In particular, stakeholders include shareholders, depositors, users of banking services, creditors, public authorities, staff, management, and competitors.

**Non-compliance risk:** the risk of an establishment being exposed to reputational damage, financial losses, or sanctions due to non-adherence to legal and regulatory provisions, standards, and practices applicable to its activities, or non-compliance with the establishment's internal policy or code of ethics.

**

Article 4:**
The governance framework of establishments must adhere to the following principles:

**The principle of proportionality:** the governance framework must be adapted to the size of the establishment, its systemic nature as defined in Article 69 of Law No. 2016-48, its financial situation as defined in Articles 100, 101, and 102 of the same law, its risk profile, as well as the nature and complexity of its activities and operations.
This principle must be applied without prejudice to current legal and regulatory provisions.

**The principle of balance of powers:** the governance framework must establish a balance of powers through the implementation of an appropriate system of powers and counter-powers, responsibility, and accountability.

**The principle of equitable treatment of shareholders:** this is particularly reflected in:
- the timely and regular obtaining of relevant and significant information about the establishment,
- participation and voting at general meetings,
- facilitating the effective participation of shareholders in major governance-related decisions. **Section II: Specific Responsibilities**

**

Article 6:**

The administrative body shall decide on the development strategy and the intervention policies of the establishment. To this end, it shall be responsible for:
- Formalizing growth and profitability objectives, consistent with the risk appetite policy and the preservation of the financial soundness of the establishment.
- Regularly reviewing the relevance of these objectives, particularly in light of changes in the banking and finance sectors, as well as regulatory, economic, and environmental developments.

In this capacity, it must ensure that human, financial, and technical resources are permanently aligned with the established strategy and intervention policies.

**

Article 7:**

The administrative body shall establish, in consultation with the management body, a risk appetite policy that:
- Determines the overall and individual level, by type of risk, that the establishment is prepared to assume to achieve its business plan.
- Defines exposure limits by type of risk.
- Defines the own funds and liquidity policy, consistent with the volume and nature of the risk and in compliance with current legal and regulatory requirements.

The risk appetite policy shall be disseminated to all relevant departments of the establishment and shall become part of the establishment's risk culture.
The administrative body shall ensure the effective implementation of the risk appetite policy and its compliance.

**

Article 8:**

The administrative body shall establish a governance framework for the establishment in accordance with current legal and regulatory provisions and the principles set forth in the code of ethics referred to in

Article 13 of this circular.
This framework shall define, in accordance with the statutes of the **

Article 10:**

The administrative body shall establish a remuneration and appointment policy for its members, committees, the Sharia Compliance Control Committee, the management body, and the senior officers of key functions and the auditor of Islamic banking operations, in line with the organization and performance of the institution.

The remuneration policy shall adhere to the following elements:
- be consistent with the development strategy, the financial soundness of the institution, and its long-term interests,
- be designed to establish practices that curb incentives for excessive risk-taking,
- clearly, formally, and based on objective criteria, establish the remuneration scheme and its components, and
- partially or totally revise variable remuneration when the institution records unfavorable financial performance or incurs losses, or in cases of actions leading to significant losses for the institution, or in cases of failure to meet its obligations.

The administrative body is required to submit a report to the Central Bank of Tunisia detailing the remuneration practices of the members of the management body and the senior officers of key functions.

**

Article 11:**

The administrative body shall appoint from among its peers the members of the committees referred to in Articles 49, 50, and 51 of Law No. 2016-48.

It shall appoint:
- the senior officers of the internal audit, risk, and compliance control structures, upon the proposal of the management body, and
- the head of the Islamic banking operations audit structure in accordance with the first paragraph of

Article 58 of this circular.

The administrative body shall propose to the institution's general assembly the members of the Sharia Compliance Control Committee. To this end, the administrative body shall establish documented policies concerning how these rules are to be respected. These policies must include, in particular:

- the principles of responsible professional conduct, including in particular the performance of duties with integrity, loyalty, competence, and the required diligence, and the avoidance of conflicts of interest,
- the principles to ensure that users of banking services are heard, well-informed, and that commercial conduct is in their interest, and
- the rules of conduct ensuring the protection of personal data and respect for professional secrecy.

Article 14:

The administrative body is responsible for:

- establishing the basic principles of the compliance policy that the institution must adhere to in the conduct of its activities and supervising its implementation,
- ensuring the establishment of an effective and independent compliance control function by the management body,
- regularly monitoring the activity of the body responsible for compliance control, ensuring its proper functioning and the adequacy of its resources, and
- evaluating, at least annually, the institution's management of non-compliance risk.

Article 15:

The administrative body shall ensure the establishment of a culture of responsible finance. As such, it shall work to integrate the principles of social and environmental responsibility into the institution's strategy.
The actions taken within the framework of the institution's social and environmental responsibility shall be recorded in its annual report, which shall include, in particular, the funded projects and their environmental and social impacts.

Article 16:

The administrative body shall establish a whistleblowing policy and adequate procedures allowing employees to report, in complete confid The board of directors ensures that shareholders are informed, in the management report, of the evaluation of the performance of the board of directors and its committees, and, where applicable, of the follow-up to this evaluation. This evaluation must be carried out in accordance with the methodology provided for in

Article 42, paragraph 4 of this circular.

CHAPTER II
ON THE COMPOSITION AND FUNCTIONING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS

Section I: On the composition and qualification of members Article 18:

The composition of the board of directors and the qualifications of its members must be adapted to the development strategy of the institution, its size, the nature of its business, and the complexity of its operations, as well as to its risk profile.

The board of directors must reflect a diversity of skills enabling it to effectively fulfill its responsibilities.

The institution ensures the implementation of a policy aimed at establishing gender diversity on the board of directors and communicating on this aspect in the report intended for the public as provided for in

Article 69 of this circular.

Article 19:

The board of directors must include at least two independent members and one member representing small shareholders within the meaning of the financial market regulations for an institution listed on the Tunis Stock Exchange.

Article 20:

Without prejudice to the provisions of

Article 47 of Law No. 2016-48 and Article 237 of the Commercial Companies Code, any person who:

- does not hold, themselves, their spouse, their ascendants and first-degree descendants, a direct or indirect stake in the capital of the institution,
- has not held a management position or has not been a member **

Article 21:**
The independent director's compliance with the criteria set out in

Article 20 of this circular is reviewed annually by the institution's nomination and remuneration committee. The conclusions of this review are brought to the attention of the administrative body.

** Article 22:**
The independent director must, during the exercise of their mandate, promptly inform the administrative body in case of non-compliance with the conditions and criteria relating to their eligibility.

**

Article 23:**
The members of the administrative body must individually possess appropriate skills in one or more of the following areas, including: banking operations, payment systems, strategic planning, governance, internal control and risk management, information systems, financial analysis, and accounting.

** Article 24:**
The institution's administrative body requires from any candidate who is to be appointed as a member of its body or to the management body, a sworn declaration to verify the existence or absence of situations of conflict of interest. This declaration must indicate:
- whether they hold positions in the administrative or management bodies of other companies, as well as operations carried out or in progress with companies linked to the institution or its subsidiaries by the entities within which they exercise these functions, and
- the existence of family ties with principal individual shareholders and members of the administrative and management bodies.

The members of the administrative body must also, during their mandates, keep the administrative body informed before accepting any invitation to sit on another administrative body or to assume a management function in an economic undertaking.

Article 27:**

All members of the administrative body must:

*   attend the meetings of the administrative body diligently according to the conditions to be established in the governance code.
*   actively contribute to the work of the administrative body.
*   ensure that the agenda for the administrative body's meetings covers all important matters.
*   devote the necessary time to properly fulfill their obligations.

**

Article 28:**

The administrative body must implement a continuous skill enhancement program for all its members so that they can fully carry out their duties.

**CHAPTER III: ROLE OF THE CHAIRMAN OF THE ADMINISTRATIVE BODY**

** Article 29:**

The chairman of the administrative body is required to:

*   ensure that the administrative body properly fulfills its responsibilities in an effective and independent manner.
*   ensure that the committees carry out their assigned responsibilities and report the results of their work to the administrative body.
*   oversee the performance evaluation process of the administrative body, the committees, and the members of said body.

**

Article 30:**

The chairman of the administrative body prepares, coordinates, and directs the work of said body. They are responsible in particular for:

*   establishing the agenda for the administrative body's meetings in consultation with the management body and other governance structures.
*   ensuring the regularity of the administrative body's meetings.
*   communicating requests, comments, and any decisions of the administrative body to the management body.
*   identifying important matters from the management body to be submitted to the administrative body or one of its committees.
*   leading discussions during the administrative body's meetings. possess professional experience, particularly in the banking and/or financial sector, and must have the necessary personal qualities to carry out its duties, namely leadership, communication skills, listening skills, and conflict management.
The chairman of the administrative body devotes adequate time to the exercise of their functions.

Article 33:
The chairman of the administrative body must ensure the preparation of the reports referred to in Article 69 of this circular.

Article 34:
The administrative body shall establish a permanent secretariat placed under the direct authority of the chairman of the administrative body, which is responsible for, among other things:

- the distribution to each member of the agenda, as well as the documents and information necessary for the accomplishment of their mission, within a sufficient timeframe to allow each member to adequately prepare the items on the agenda.
- the drafting of the minutes.
The chairman of the administrative body shall ensure that the minutes of the meetings faithfully and accurately record the discussions, the questions raised by the attending members, any reservations expressed, and the decisions taken.

TITLE III: COMMITTEES EMANATING FROM THE ADMINISTRATIVE BODY
CHAPTER ONE: GENERAL PRINCIPLES

Article 37:**

Every committee shall convene upon the convocation of its president at least quarterly and whenever it deems it useful, and at least every two months for institutions subject to the provisions of Articles 101 and 102 of Law No. 2016-48, as well as for those of a systemic nature within the meaning of Article 69 of Law No.

2016-48.

The committee may involve any person whose presence is deemed useful, without them taking part in the vote. The committee may also convene a member of the governing body to participate in its meetings in order to provide clarification on certain matters. The committee may not validly deliberate without the presence of three of its members. In the event of the president's inability to attend, the presidency shall be entrusted to one of the committee members chosen by their peers. Decisions shall be taken by a majority of the members present. In the event of a tie in votes, the president's vote shall be decisive.

In the event of a tie in votes, the president's vote shall be decisive. Minutes shall be drawn up for each committee meeting, signed by all members of the committee, and which shall record in detail the deliberations, decisions, and recommendations, as well as any dissenting opinions and the follow-up to the implementation of decisions from previous meetings. Every committee must establish a charter, approved by the administrative body, defining its responsibilities, its composition, its operating rules, and its relationships with the administrative body and the operational structures of the institution.

The Audit Committee and the Risk Committee must establish a framework for coordination and collaboration in order to facilitate decision-making at the level of the administrative body. The Risk Committee is required to submit its meeting minutes to the Audit Committee in a timely manner.

**CHAPTER II: THE AUDIT COMMITTEE**

**

Article 38:**

The Audit Committee is responsible for assisting the administrative body in the areas of financial information. ** Article 39:**

The chairperson of the audit committee must possess academic and professional qualifications and solid expertise in one of the fields of finance, accounting, and audit.
The members of the audit committee must demonstrate experience in one of the fields of finance, accounting, and audit, which is adapted to the complexity of the institution's activity and its risk profile.

The secretariat of the committee shall be provided by the unit responsible for the internal audit function.

**CHAPTER III: THE RISK COMMITTEE**

**

Article 40:**

The risk committee's mission is to assist the administrative body in fulfilling its responsibilities relating to the oversight of the institution's risk management framework.

Without prejudice to the provisions of

Article 50 of Law No. 2016-48, the risk committee is responsible for assisting the administrative body, particularly in:

- the design and updating of a risk management policy and the setting of exposure limits and operational ceilings,
- the approval of risk measurement and monitoring systems,
- the control of the management body's compliance with the risk appetite policy,
- the analysis and monitoring of the institution's exposure to risks, particularly credit, market, liquidity, and operational risks,
- the assessment of the provisioning policy and the permanent adequacy of own funds in relation to the institution's risk profile,
- the examination of risks arising from the strategic decisions of the administrative body,
- the adoption of corrective actions for better effectiveness of the risk management framework,
- the approval of business continuity plans, and
- the appointment of the head of the risk management function.

It must ensure that the risk management structure is - the design of the succession policy for members of the administrative body, committees, the management body, key function heads, as well as the Islamic banking operations auditor and members of the Islamic banking standards compliance control committee,
- the appointment of members of the administrative body and committees, as well as the management body and control functions, and
- the design of the methodology for evaluating the work of the administrative body and its committees.

Article 43:

The Nomination and Remuneration Committee must develop and maintain a clear, transparent, and rigorous process for identifying, selecting, appointing, and evaluating members of the administrative body and its committees, the management body, and control function heads.

The selection process must ensure that candidates:

- possess the necessary qualifications, skills, and experience,
- meet integrity criteria and enjoy a good reputation, and
- devote sufficient time to properly exercise their responsibilities.

The Nomination and Remuneration Committee must identify and submit to the administrative body any situations of conflict of interest arising from the appointment process.

The committee's secretariat will be provided by the department responsible for human resource management.

Article 44:

For financial institutions that have not established a Nomination and Remuneration Committee, the obligations set out in this chapter shall systematically devolve upon the administrative body.

TITLE IV: ON THE MANAGEMENT BODY Article 45:

Without prejudice to the powers vested in it by current laws, the management body is responsible for the day-to-day management of the institution's activities and ensures the effective steering of the realization process. **

Article 46:**

The management body must immediately alert the administrative body of any event that could:

*   Impact the financial situation and risk profile of the establishment,
*   Cause a malfunction of the internal control system and increase the risks of non-compliance,
*   Compromise the continuity of critical activities.

** Article 47:**

Members of the management body must possess the experience, skills, and integrity necessary for managing the establishment's activities. They must receive regular training to deepen their skills and stay updated on knowledge and developments in their areas of responsibility.

**TITLE V: CONTROL FUNCTIONS**

**

Article 48:**

The administrative body must ensure that the internal audit, risk management, and compliance control functions referred to in Article 53 of Law No. 2016-48 have formalized procedures and the human, technical, and financial resources that enable them to carry out their missions effectively, with complete independence and objectivity.

The head of the risk management function and the head of the internal audit function must not hold their respective mandates concurrently with other functions or responsibilities within the establishment.

The administrative body must hold meetings at least annually with the heads of the control functions to monitor their work and be informed about major developments that could affect the establishment's risk profile.

**CHAPTER ONE: RISK MANAGEMENT FUNCTION**

**

Article 49:**

The risk management function is responsible, among other things, for the following:

*   Identifying the main risks and developing a risk map of the establishment and assessing the levels of exposure to these risks,
*   Preparing the risk management policy - regularly assess the risk governance framework, including in particular:

  * the effectiveness and functioning of the risk management and compliance control functions,
  * the quality, reliability, and frequency of risk reports submitted to the supervisory and management bodies, and
  * the effectiveness of the institution's internal control system.

- inform the supervisory and management bodies of any shortcomings identified during its assignments in order to take appropriate corrective measures.

The internal audit function must have access to all data, records, and premises of the institution.

The internal audit function must communicate any malfunctions related to non-compliance risk, identified during its control missions, to the heads of the compliance control function and the risk management function.

**CHAPTER 3: THE COMPLIANCE CONTROL FUNCTION**

**

Article 51:**

The compliance control function must act as an advisor to the supervisory and management bodies on matters related to compliance with current legal and regulatory provisions and keep them informed of changes in this regard. In carrying out its duties, the compliance control function is independent of the management body.

To this end, this function must, in particular:

- carry out a regulatory monitoring mission,
- establish a mapping of non-compliance risks,
- ensure that the institution has formalized procedures and internal control rules for areas directly falling under the compliance control function,
- regularly verify compliance with policy and procedures in compliance matters and recommend corrective measures as appropriate.

Article 53:

The administration organ of the consolidated entity shall, in the exercise of its responsibilities:

- establish a governance framework for each subsidiary, consistent with the group's framework and suitable for the size and complexity of its activities,
- approve the group's development strategy and clear policies for implementation,
- define the global risk policy of the group and its subsidiaries,
- approve clear policies and strategies regarding the creation of new legal structures and entities, ensuring coherence with the group's policies and interests,
- implement appropriate processes and controls to detect and manage potential conflicts of interest within the group, primarily arising from intra-group transactions,
- ensure the adequacy of internal control, compliance, and risk management tools for each subsidiary and their consistency with the group's system,
- ensure the adequacy of information systems, the existence of robust audit trails, and appropriate controls for risk identification, measurement, management, and limitation at the consolidated level, and
- verify that effective systems exist for facilitating communication between different entities, managing risks for various subsidiaries or group entities, and enabling effective group supervision.

Article 54:

The administration organ shall:

- ensure that the consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with IFRS and that they give a true and fair view of the consolidated entity' ** Article 57:**

The committee for the supervision of compliance with Islamic banking standards meets at the convocation of its president, at least twice a year, and whenever deemed useful.
The committee for the supervision of compliance with Islamic banking standards may call upon any person whose presence is deemed useful, without voting rights.
It cannot deliberate without the presence of at least three of its members.
In case of the president's absence, the presidency will be entrusted to one of the members of the committee for the supervision of compliance with Islamic banking standards, chosen by his peers.
Minutes shall be kept for each meeting of the committee for the supervision of compliance with Islamic banking standards.
Decisions within this committee are made by a majority of the votes of the members. In case of a tie in votes, the vote of the presiding officer shall be decisive.
The secretariat of the committee for the supervision of compliance with Islamic banking standards shall be provided by the auditor of Islamic banking operations.

**CHAPTER 2: THE AUDITOR OF ISLAMIC BANKING OPERATIONS**

**

Article 58:**

The auditor of Islamic banking operations shall be appointed by the administrative body upon proposal of the management body and after opinion from the committee for the supervision of compliance with Islamic banking standards.
He shall be responsible in particular for:
- ensuring the compliance of transactions, financial services and products, as well as contracts and financing granted, with the opinions and proposals of the committee for the supervision of compliance with Islamic banking standards,
- reporting any irregularity noted to the committee for the supervision of compliance with Islamic banking standards, the administrative body, and the management body,
- carrying out the annual audit plan and submitting audit reports to the committee for the supervision of compliance with Islamic banking standards,
- submitting an annual report on his work to the committee for the supervision of compliance with Islamic banking standards. CHAPTER 4: OBLIGATIONS OF THE MANAGEMENT BODY

Article 60:

In order to enable the Sharia compliance control committee to fulfill its missions, the management body is required to:

- provide the Sharia compliance control committee with adequate human and logistical resources, and the necessary documents and/or information,
- provide all clarifications requested by the Sharia compliance control committee during the execution of its work,
- submit, in advance, to the Sharia compliance control committee all new products, contracts, and transactions that the institution intends to use in the future, for review and approval,
- organize periodic meetings between the Sharia compliance control committee and operational structures, and
- organize training for operational structures related to Sharia banking compliance.

The management body is also required to:

- formalize the procedures describing the Sharia banking standards to be respected by operational structures, and in particular those relating to transactions, financial services, and contracts, and
- implement a control system allowing for the early detection of situations of non-compliance with Sharia banking standards.

Article 61:

The management body must ensure the application of the principles referred to in

Article 59 of this circular and establish the adequate procedures and means necessary for this purpose.

The Central Bank of Tunisia organizes meetings with independent directors to inquire about their role in the governance of the institution.

Article 68:**
The administrative body shall ensure the establishment and updating of an information disclosure mechanism for stakeholders, which must ensure the timely communication of reliable information. - the institution's risk profile, particularly the level of exposure by type of risk, by geographical area, by sector, and by main beneficiaries,
- the composition of own funds and their adequacy in relation to the risk profile,
- the provisioning policy for risk coverage, and
- the shareholding structure, particularly the main shareholders, their representation on the administrative body, and voting rights.

The capital requirement for market risks must cover the following risks:

  * Debt securities risk or interest rate risk, as defined below in Section II of this chapter.

Article 20
In the context of this circular, the trading portfolio, as opposed to the banking portfolio, consists of positions in financial instruments held with the intention of trading or for the purpose of hedging other elements of the trading portfolio.
To be included in the trading portfolio, financial instruments must be free of clauses limiting their negotiability or the establishment of hedging.
By financial instrument, we mean any contract that creates a financial asset for one party and a financial liability or an equity instrument for another party. Financial instruments include both spot financial instruments and derivative instruments.
Positions held for trading purposes are those taken with the intention of being disposed of in the short term and/or with the intention of benefiting from short-term favorable price movements or locking in arbitrage profits.
They include proprietary positions, positions related to client business activities, and positions related to market-making activities within the meaning of Circular No. 2016-01.

Article 23**

Supervised institutions must ensure that transfers of instruments between the trading book and the banking book are limited. These operations must only be carried out in exceptional circumstances.

Any reallocation between the trading book and the banking book must be justified, documented, deemed compliant with the policies of the supervised institution, and brought to the attention of the Central Bank of Tunisia.

Under no circumstances may the transfer of instruments result in a reduction of capital requirements.

**

Article 24**

The position risk concerning a debt or equity security or a derivative instrument on such a security is broken down into two elements:

a) General risk, meaning the risk of a price change caused by a fluctuation in interest rate levels in the case of debt securities or derivatives on such securities, or by a general movement in the stock market in the case of equity securities or derivatives on such securities.

b) Specific risk, meaning the risk of a price change influenced by factors related to the issuer of the underlying security or instrument.

The capital requirement relating to general risk is determined by applying a coefficient of 8% to the overall net position, for each national market, and then summing the requirements thus calculated.

The capital requirement relating to specific risk is determined by applying a coefficient of 8% to the overall gross position, for each national market, and then summing the requirements thus calculated.

**

Article 40**
Positions on instruments that are already subject to a deduction from capital are exempt from a capital requirement for specific risk.

**Section IV: Capital Requirements for Foreign Exchange Risk**

**

Article 41**
For the purpose of calculating capital requirements for foreign exchange risk, the overall net position in foreign currencies is determined as follows:

a) Subject institutions calculate their net open position in each currency. This position is the algebraic sum of the positive and negative items listed below:

i) the items taken into account are the following:
*   **Net spot position:** all assets minus all liabilities, including accrued interest not yet due in the currency considered.
*   **Net forward position:** all amounts to be received minus all amounts to be paid under forward foreign exchange transactions.
*   Irrevocable guarantees and similar instruments that are certain to be called and likely to be irrecoverable.
*   The net delta equivalent of the total portfolio of currency options. Positions thus obtained may be offset against positions of opposite sign in identical currencies.

ii) the items excluded are the following:
*   Transactions where the foreign exchange risk is borne by the State or by a foreign exchange risk guarantee mechanism;
*   Durable and structural assets, such as equity and fixed-income securities. **Section V: Capital Requirements for Settlement-Delivery Risk**

Article 44**

Article 45**
In the case of transactions in debt securities, equity securities, and currencies that are not settled after the scheduled delivery date within a settlement-delivery system ensuring simultaneous exchange, the obligated institutions calculate the price difference to which they are exposed. This price difference corresponds to the difference between the agreed settlement price for the debt security, equity security, or currency concerned and its current market value. Article 51**
The risks incurred on the same beneficiary must not exceed 25% of the net own funds of the subject institution.
Borrowers affiliated with the same group are considered as the "same beneficiary." The term "group" is attributed to two or more legal entities having interconnections between them such as:
- joint management;

Article 52**
The total amount of risks incurred on persons linked to the subject institution within the meaning of Article 43 of Law No. 2016-48 concerning banks and financial institutions must not exceed 75% of the net own funds of the subject institution.

**Decides:**

**Chapter One: General Provisions**

** Article 1** - The present circular aims to reduce the level of non-performing loans in the balance sheets of banks and financial institutions through the establishment of a prevention and resolution framework.
The rules established by the present circular constitute minimum requirements to be respected by banks and financial institutions.

**

Article 2** - For the purposes of the present circular, the term:
Non-performing loans: refers to loans **Business Group:** With reference to

2021-05.

**Share of Gross Non-Performing Exposures in the Institution's Total Exposures (in %):** Exposures classified as 2, 3, and 4 / Total Exposures.

**Share of Gross Non-Performing Exposures in the Institution's Total Exposures, taking into account Exposures Transferred to Debt Recovery Companies (in %):** (Institution's Classified Exposures 2, 3, and 4 + Exposures Transferred to Recovery Subsidiaries) / (Institution's Total Exposures + Exposures Transferred to Recovery Subsidiaries)

**Prevention:** The early and proactive management of claims for which the risk of becoming non-performing is high.

**Resolution:** The curative treatment aimed at reducing the level of existing non-performing claims within the institution.

**Debt Restructuring:** Any agreement relating to the modification of the terms of the initial credit contract to enable the institution to recover its claims (rescheduling, consolidation, conversion, partial or total write-off, granting of new credits, etc.).

**Debt Recovery Companies:** Companies within the meaning of Law No.

98-4 of February 2, 1998, relating to debt recovery companies, as amended by subsequent texts.

**Early Warning System:** All procedures and tools that allow for the rapid identification of claims likely to become non-performing. - approve the mechanism provided for by

Article 3 of this circular, review it at least once a year and revise it if necessary, taking into account achievements, the evolution of the institution's situation and the economic and regulatory environment; and
- monitor the application of the mechanism provided for by Article 3 of this circular by regularly tracking quantitative and qualitative performance indicators for the prevention and resolution of non-performing loans.
The Risk Committee is required to assist the administrative body in the design of the non-performing loan prevention and resolution mechanism and in monitoring its implementation.

Chapter 2
On the Non-Performing Loan Prevention Mechanism

Article 6 - Institutions must segment their loan portfolio in order to form homogeneous groups of assets to which similar treatments can be applied.
The segmentation criteria are determined based on the specifics of the portfolio and must be reviewed periodically to verify the homogeneity of the groups in terms of their reaction to credit risk factors.

Article 7 - Throughout the entire lifecycle of the loan, the esta - **Financial Expense Coverage Ratio:** EBITDA / Financial Expenses.
- **Leverage Ratio:** Debt / EBITDA.

To assess the debtor's viability, the institution must establish thresholds for the chosen analytical indicators, taking into account, where applicable, sector-specific characteristics.

This assessment must consider, where applicable, the financial situation of the business group to which the company belongs, based in particular on certified consolidated financial statements.

For individuals and professionals not subject to the obligation to prepare financial statements under current legislation, the analysis of their viability must at least take into account their repayment capacity and their history of settling their commitments.

**

Article 8** - Institutions must implement an early warning system for potential debtor difficulties, on an individual basis and for business groups, in order to act and take corrective measures before the situation becomes compromised.

To this end, institutions must define, for each portfolio segment, a set of quantitative and qualitative indicators enabling them to detect, in a timely manner, signs of difficulties in the debtor's financial situation, operations, and actions.

The early warning system must take into account both recent information and relevant forward-looking data, on an individual basis and at the business group level.

**

Article 9** - The institution must establish, by referring in particular to the internal counterparty rating system, a "watch list" of debtors, including at least claims classified as 1 within the meaning of the aforementioned Circular No. 91-24 and restructured claims. The institution must clearly and formally set the criteria and duration for inclusion on this list. **

Article 11 - The development of a non-performing loan resolution strategy requires, beforehand, the preparation of an internal report assessing the institution's internal and external operational environment. This is for the purpose of identifying potential obstacles and deciding on the necessary actions to be implemented.**

**This report must be validated by the administrative body and include at least the following elements:**

*   the factors that led to the accumulation of non-performing loans, for significant segments;
*   the nature of the resolution measures implemented in the past and their limitations;
*   the assessment of the institution's operational capabilities (credit policies, recovery policies, restructuring policies, loan monitoring system, organization and resources, etc.); and
*   the identification of aspects that need to be improved to achieve the objectives of reducing non-performing loans.

**

Article 12 - The non-performing loan resolution strategy referred to in

Article 10 of this circular must, in particular:**

*   include quantitative target objectives for reducing non-performing loans in terms of share, volume, number and age. These objectives must be broken down, particularly by time horizon, by portfolio segment and by implementation measure;
*   be consistent with the institution's risk management and capital planning policies;
*   include policies for balance sheet clean-up, loan sales, and management of assets acquired through loan recovery; and
*   be translated into an operational implementation plan that defines, according to a precise timetable, the various actions to be taken to achieve the target objectives for reducing non-performing loans, and the investments and resources required for this purpose (information system, organization, staff, etc.).

Ar **

Article 15** - Establishments must define a formalized and transparent process for managing assets that have come into their possession under the recovery terms permitted by current legislation. This process must enable the establishment to ensure the protection of these assets and their disposal within a reasonable timeframe, maximizing their sale value.

**

Article 16** - The establishments referred to in

Article 10 of this circular must establish, within their organization, an operational unit, a "workout unit," tasked exclusively with the resolution of non-performing loans, under the following conditions:
*   to be separate from the structures responsible for granting credit and to have a different hierarchical reporting line from these structures;
*   to have a sufficiently high hierarchical reporting line granting it specific resolution powers under a dedicated delegation scheme;
*   to be adapted to the volume and specificities of the non-performing loan portfolio and the envisaged resolution measures; and
*   to permanently have adequate resources in terms of staffing, skills, and information systems.
The resolution unit must submit quarterly reports on its activity to the risk committee.

**Chapter 4**
**Application of the Non-Performing Loan Prevention and Resolution Framework for Large Exposures and Co-Financed Debtors**

**

Article 17** - In the context of applying this circular, establishments must ensure they consult and coordinate their actions during the prevention and resolution phases for large exposures and for restructuring operations of co-financed debtors' commitments.
"Large exposures" are understood to mean debtors or business groups whose total exposure to the financial system exceeds 100 million dinars.

**

Article 18** - Save **

Article 19** - For large exposures, the lead arranger is required to demand an annual report on the governance, activity, performance, liquidity, and solvency of the debtor and, where applicable, on the relationships between entities within the business group. This report must be reviewed by a chartered accountant registered with the Tunisian Order of Chartered Accountants. This report must also be demanded if the requested financing is likely to increase the overall exposure of the debtor or the business group beyond 100 million dinars.

The lead arranger is also responsible to the Central Bank of Tunisia for:

*   Communicating the report referred to in the first paragraph of this article to it;
*   Communicating to it, no later than June 30th of each year, an assessment note by the institution concerning the governance and economic and financial situation, as well as the due diligence measures taken to control the risks for each of the debtors concerned; and
*   Informing it without delay of any event likely to affect the viability of the debtors concerned and of any related restructuring operations.

**Chapter 5: Miscellaneous Provisions**

**

Article 20** - Institutions must adapt their internal control system to ensure compliance with the requirements of this circular and the proper functioning of the systems put in place.

The internal audit structure is required to evaluate, at least once every two years, the processes for the prevention and resolution of non-performing loans.

SUBJECT: Centralization of banking risks. The purpose of this circular is to remind banks of certain provisions governing the reporting of banking risks and to establish a new reconciliation statement of credits reported to the Risk Centralization with those appearing on the monthly financial statements. I - DISCREPANCIES BETWEEN THE DATA OF THE RISK CENTRALIZATION AND THOSE OF THE MONTHLY FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

By circular n° 77-97 of November 29, 1977, banks were invited to adopt exactly the same accounting methods for credits and other commitments for both their financial statements and their risk reporting, in order to avoid any discrepancies between the total credits reported for risks and that shown on the financial statements. However, despite this invitation, sometimes significant discrepancies have been noted for certain banks between the figures for risks and those on the financial statements. Therefore, banks are requested to take all necessary measures to avoid the recurrence of these discrepancies as soon as possible. To this end, banks are requested to follow the following prescriptions:

1°) Credits must be reported before due date both to the Risk Centralization and on the monthly financial statements. 2°) Advances on term accounts and cash vouchers are not reportable to the Risk Centralization.

3°) Discounted bills for collection and bills rediscounted at the BCT must be reported to the Risk Centralization under the headings of their original portfolio: bills of exchange on Tunisia, bills of exchange on foreign countries, other export credits, etc.

4°) Credits and advances to personnel must be accounted for under the heading "A06200 sundry debtors" of **III - COMMUNICATION OF BANKING RISKS ON A MEDIUM THAT CAN BE PROCESSED DIRECTLY BY COMPUTER**

Some banks continue to communicate their risks to the BCT (Central Bank of Tunisia) on individual statements whose manual processing greatly burdens the work of extracting and entering information and causes significant loss of time before the various analytical reports of the Central Risk Register can be drawn up.

In order to facilitate and accelerate the processing of data from the Central Risk Register, the aforementioned banks are requested to implement, as soon as possible, a system for communicating risks on a medium that can be processed directly by computer, and preferably on magnetic tapes.

**IV - UPDATING THE RECONCILIATION STATEMENT BETWEEN CREDITS DECLARED TO THE CENTRAL RISK REGISTER AND THOSE APPEARING ON THE MONTHLY ACCOUNTING SITUATION**

By circular no.

68-11 of March 22, 1968, banks were invited to attach to their accounting situations a statement reconciling the credits declared to the Central Risk Register with those appearing on the aforementioned situation. However, this statement is now outdated, notably by the latest revision of the monthly accounting situation, and no longer allows for a precise understanding of the exact origin of discrepancies that may appear between the statistics for different categories of banking risks and the corresponding data appearing on the monthly accounting situation.
The aforementioned statement is therefore cancelled and replaced by model "A15" attached to the present circular.
