SECTION 1
OF THE PAYMENT OF CHEQUES FOR AN AMOUNT
LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO 20 DINARS

Article 374 of the Commercial Code places upon the drawee bank the obligation to pay cheques for an amount less than or equal to 20 dinars for which the provision is either absent or insufficient, to the exclusion of cheques drawn on foreign currency accounts or convertible dinar accounts.

This payment obligation is subject to strict conditions that must be met; thus:

*   the amount of the cheque must be less than or equal to 20 dinars;
*   it must be presented for payment less than one month after the expiry of the presentation period provided for in

Article 372 of the Commercial Code; and
*   the cheque must be drawn on a form issued by the drawee bank after the entry into force of Law n° 96-28 of April 3, 1996. Indeed, being based on a legal presumption of an irrevocable credit opening in favor of the account holder upon the delivery of cheque forms, the obligation to pay cheques for an amount less than or equal to 20 dinars does not apply to forms issued before the entry into force of the aforementioned law.

The drawee bank that refuses to pay a cheque for an amount equal to or less than 20 dinars due to the absence or insufficiency of provision must justify, at the time of refusal, that the form used was issued before the entry into force date of the aforementioned law. For cheques for an amount less than or equal to twenty dinars that it pays, the drawee bank must not:

*   issue a certificate of non-payment;

Article 1 - The present organic law aims to prevent and combat terrorism and money laundering. It also supports international efforts in this field, in accordance with international standards, and within the framework of international, regional, and bilateral conventions ratified by the Republic of Tunisia.

Art. 2 - Public authorities responsible for applying the present law must respect constitutional guarantees and international, regional, and bilateral conventions ratified by the Republic of Tunisia, in the domain of human rights, the protection of refugees, and international humanitarian law.

Art. 3 - For the purposes of the present law, the following terms are understood as:
* Conspiracy: any plot formed for any duration, and regardless of the number of its members, with the aim of committing one of the offenses provided for by the present law, without it being necessary for a structural organization or a determined and official distribution of their roles or the continuity of their membership in this plot to exist.
* Organization: a structured group composed of three or more persons, formed for any duration and operating in concert, with the aim of committing one of the offenses provided for by the present law on national territory or abroad.
* Transnational offense: an offense is considered transnational in the following cases:
- if it is committed on national territory and in one or more other foreign states,
- if it is committed on the territory "In the event of a forced landing, the aircraft is always considered to be in flight until the competent authorities take charge of the aircraft, passengers, and cargo.
* Aircraft in service: An aircraft is considered to be in service as soon as the aerodrome personnel and crew members begin its preparation for flight and until twenty-four hours after any landing.

In all cases, the state of service includes the entire period during which the aircraft is in flight.
* Persons enjoying international protection: The persons mentioned below, when they are in a foreign State:
    1. A Head of State or a member of a body acting as Head of State under the constitution of the State concerned, as well as their accompanying family members. 2. A Head of Government or a Minister of Foreign Affairs, as well as their accompanying family members. 3.

Any representative or official of a State, or an official or person accredited to an intergovernmental organization, as well as their accompanying family members, in cases where they are entitled to special protection in accordance with international law.
* Fixed platforms located on the continental shelf: An artificial island or an installation or structure fixed to the seabed permanently for the purpose of exploration or exploitation of resources or for other economic purposes.
* Property (new) (repealed and replaced by Organic Law No. 2019-9 of January 23, 2019): Assets and property of any nature, corporeal or incorporeal, tangible or intangible, movable or immovable, regardless of the means of their acquisition, including securities, documents, and legal instruments, in whatever form, including electronic and digital, that prove ownership of such property or the existence of a right over it." *   **Legal structures (added by Organic Law 2019-9 of January 23, 2019):** refers to direct special-purpose funds and other similar legal arrangements, including any transaction whereby a person transfers funds, rights, or current or future guarantees in favor of a person called a trustee, who holds them separately from their own assets, to manage and administer them on behalf of one or more beneficiaries.

*   **Entities responsible for supervising the persons listed in

Article 107 of this Law (Added by Organic Law 2019-9 of January 23, 2019):** the Central Bank of Tunisia, the Microfinance Control Authority, the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Commerce, the Ministry in charge of Communication Technologies and the Digital Economy, the General Committee of Insurance, the Financial Market Council, and self-regulatory bodies or supervisory authorities for specific professions and non-financial activities.

*   **Bearer negotiable instruments (Added by Organic Law 2019-9 of January 23, 2019):** bearer monetary instruments in documentary form such as traveler's checks, negotiable instruments such as checks

drafts, promissory notes, payment orders either for their bearer or on their behalf, without restriction, or issued on behalf of a fictitious beneficiary or in a format allowing the transfer of the right to receive it, or signed incomplete instruments on which the beneficiary's name has been omitted.

*   **Risk-based approach (Added by Organic Law 2019-9 of January 23, 2019):** measures and procedures aimed at identifying, assessing, understanding, and mitigating the risks of money laundering and terrorist financing.

2- Any installation or means of transport used to produce, store, process, transport, use,

Art. 4 - The provisions of the Penal Code, the Code of Criminal Procedure, the Code of Military Justice, as well as
special texts relating to certain offenses and related procedures, are applicable to

This does not preclude the imposition of all or part of the complementary penalties provided for by law.

Art. 7** - A legal entity shall be prosecuted if the commission of terrorist offenses provided for by this law represents the true reason for its creation, or if they were committed on its behalf or if it has obtained advantages or revenues therefrom, or if it is established that it provides support, in whatever form, to persons, organizations, or activities related to terrorist offenses provided for by this law.
The legal entity shall be punished by a fine equal to the value of the assets obtained from the terrorist crimes. The amount of the fine may in no case be less than five times the amount of the fine payable by natural persons.
The court shall also order the prohibition of the legal entity from carrying out its activity for a maximum period of five years or order its dissolution.

Section 3
Judicial Police Officers

Art. 38 - Judicial police officers within the jurisdiction of the Tunis Court of First Instance, authorized to
establish terrorist offenses, exercise their functions throughout the territory of the Republic,
notwithstanding territorial jurisdiction rules. Military judicial police officers exercise their
functions relating to the establishment of terrorist offenses.

Art. 39 - Judicial police officers are required to notify, without delay, the public prosecutor to whom they
report, of terrorist offenses of which they have become aware. They may not detain a suspect for a period exceeding five days.
They must also notify, without delay, the relevant authorities if the suspect is a member of the armed forces,
internal security forces personnel, or customs officers.
Public prosecutors at the courts of first instance are required to transmit,
immediately, the above-mentioned notifications to the public prosecutor at the Tunis Court of First Instance for... It also includes representatives of the public prosecutor's office, investigating judges, indictment chamber judges, a juvenile judge, and judges sitting in the Juvenile Court at first instance and on appeal, competent in matters relating to children.
The judges of the judicial pole for combating terrorism are selected based on their training and experience in cases relating to terrorist offenses.

Subsection 1 - On the Public Prosecutor's Office

Art. 41 - The Public Prosecutor at the Court of First Instance of Tunis is solely competent to initiate and exercise public action relating to terrorist offenses provided for by the present law and related offenses.
He is assisted by substitutes of at least second grade, among those who have been appointed to the judicial pole for combating terrorism.
The Public Prosecutors at Courts of First Instance other than Tunis are authorized to conduct urgent preliminary investigations with a view to establishing the offense, gathering evidence thereof, and seeking its perpetrators. They receive voluntary reports, complaints, minutes, and related reports, summarily question the accused upon their appearance, and decide to place them at the disposal of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of First Instance of Tunis with the reports, the minutes drawn up, and the exhibits.
The Public Prosecutor at the Court of First Instance of Tunis is solely authorized to extend the duration of police custody twice for the same period provided for by

Article 39 of the present law, by a reasoned order, including the factual and legal grounds justifying it.
The Public Prosecutor at the Court of First Instance of Tunis must notify, without delay, the Attorney General at the Court of Appeal of Tunis of all terrorist offenses.

Art. 44 - The investigating judge is required to proceed with the confiscation of weapons, ammunition, explosives and other materials, tools, equipment, and documents that serve or are used to commit the offense or to facilitate its commission.
He must also proceed with the confiscation of objects the manufacture, possession, use, or marketing of which constitutes an offense.
An inventory shall be made, as far as possible, in the presence of the accused, or of the person in whose possession the seized items were found. The investigating judge shall draw up minutes thereof, including a description of the seized items, their characteristics, and all useful information, specifying the date of seizure and the case number.

Art. 45 - The investigating judge may, either ex officio or upon request from the public prosecutor's office, order the freezing of the accused's movable or immovable assets and financial assets, determine the arrangements for their management, or order, if necessary, their sequestration.
He must ensure that the accused is provided with a portion of his assets that allows for the coverage of his necessary needs and those of his family, including housing.

He may also order, even ex officio, the lifting of the aforementioned measures.

The investigating judge shall rule on the request for the lifting of measures within a period of four days from the date of its submission.

The order of the investigating judge on the lifting or the total or partial refusal to lift these measures may be appealed to the indictment chamber by the public prosecutor, the accused, or their lawyer within four days from the date of communication for the public prosecutor, and from the date of notification for the others.

An appeal by the public prosecutor suspends the execution of the order.

In case of appeal, the investigating judge shall transmit the case file to the indictment chamber as soon as possible. .

Art. 47 - If the witness has failed to meet the requirements of testimony, the investigating judge shall draw up an independent report which shall be transmitted to the public prosecutor to assess the advisability of bringing the witness before the competent court through a direct summons procedure, without the need to request an investigation.

Art. 48 - The witness who fails to meet the requirements of testimony in one of the terrorist offenses shall be punished by three to six months' imprisonment and a fine of one hundred to two thousand dinars.
Sub-section 3 - Trial Courts Art. 49 - The Court of First Instance of Tunis, through the judges appointed to the Judicial Pole for the Fight against Terrorism, shall have exclusive jurisdiction, to the exclusion of all other judicial or military courts, to hear terrorist offenses provided for by this Law and related offenses if they are committed:
- on national territory,
- on board a civilian or military aircraft that has landed on the territory of the Republic and the perpetrator is on board,
- on board a civilian aircraft leased without a crew to an operator whose principal place of business or permanent residence is on Tunisian territory,
- against a civilian vessel flying the flag of the Tunisian State, at the time of the commission of the offense, or against a Tunisian military vessel.

Art. 50 - The provisions of the first, second, and third paragraphs of

Article 45 and the provisions of Article 46 of this Law shall apply to trial courts.

Art. 51 - The court shall order the confiscation of assets that were used to commit or facilitate the commission of the offense, or if it has been proven that they directly or indirectly result from the offense, even if they have been transferred to other estates, whether they remain in their current state or have been converted into other assets, without prejudice to the rights of third parties acquired in good faith.
If the effective seizure has not

Art. 52 - The court may order the confiscation of all or part of the movable or immovable property and financial assets of the convicted person, if it is established that the purpose of their use is the financing of persons, organizations, or activities related to terrorist offenses.

Art. 53 - The sentence is enforceable in cases of terrorist offenses notwithstanding an opposition to a judgment rendered in absentia.

If a death sentence has been rendered in absentia, the person who opposes the judgment shall be imprisoned and the sentence shall only be enforceable after the judgment becomes irrevocable. (Added by Law 2019-9 of January 23, 2019)

Section 5
Special Investigative Techniques

Sub-section 1 - Interception of Communications

Art. 54 - (repealed and replaced by Organic Law No. 2019-9 of January 23, 2019)
In cases where the needs of the investigation require it, the Public Prosecutor or the investigating judge of the judicial pole for combating terrorism may resort to the interception of suspects' communications, by virtue of a written and reasoned decision. In the same cases, upon a reasoned report from judicial police officers empowered to ascertain terrorist offenses, the interception of suspects' communications may also take place, by virtue of a written and reasoned decision from the Public Prosecutor or the investigating judge of the judicial pole for combating terrorism.
Traffic data constitute data that can identify the type of service, the source of the communication, its destination, the transmission network, the time, date, volume, and duration of the communication.

The decision of the Public Prosecutor or the investigating judge must include all elements allowing for the identification of the communications subject to the interception request, as well as the acts that justify the recourse to interception and its duration.

The duration of the intercep

Art. 55 - The authority responsible for carrying out the interception must accomplish its mission in coordination with the public prosecutor or the investigating judge, as appropriate, and under their control, and inform them by any means leaving a written trace of the progress of the interception operation, in order to allow them to take the necessary steps for the proper conduct of the investigation.
Correspondence and reports relating to the interception operation shall be recorded in a separate and special file which shall be attached to the main file before any decision to open an investigation or close the investigation is taken.

Art. 56 - At the end of its work, the body responsible for carrying out the interception shall draw up a descriptive report of the arrangements made, the operations carried out and the results, to which shall be mandatorily attached the data that could be collected, reproduced or recorded, as well as the data allowing them to be stored, consulted or deciphered and useful for the manifestation of the truth.
If the data collected from the interception does not lead to criminal prosecution, it shall benefit from the protection provisions, in accordance with the legislation in force in the field of personal data protection.
Sub-section 2 - Infiltration

Art. 57 - (new) (Repealed and replaced by organic law no. 2019-09 of January 23, 2019)
In cases where the necessity of the investigation requires it, direct or digital infiltration may take place through a police officer using a false identity or through an informant certified by judicial police officers authorized to ascertain terrorist offenses.
In the same cases, upon a reasoned report from the judicial police officer, direct or digital infiltration may also take place, through a police officer using a false identity or through an informant certifi The penalty is increased to twelve years' imprisonment and a fine of twenty thousand dinars if the revelation results in the infiltrator, their spouse, their children, or their parents suffering blows and injuries or any other form of violence provided for by Articles 218 and 319 of the Penal Code.

The penalty is fifteen years' imprisonment and a fine of twenty-five thousand dinars if the revelation causes bodily harm not covered by Articles 218 and 319 of the Penal Code.

When this revelation results in the death of the infiltrator or one of the persons referred to in the preceding paragraph, the penalty is increased to twenty years' imprisonment and a fine of thirty thousand dinars, without prejudice to the application of more severe penalties relating to voluntary homicide.
Art. 59 - The infiltrator is not criminally liable when they carry out, without bad faith, the acts necessary for the infiltration operation.

Art. 60 - The judicial police officer in charge must supervise the infiltration operation and submit reports to the Public Prosecutor or the investigating judge when necessity demands it, or if a request has been made to them, and upon completion of the infiltration operation.
Only the final report is recorded in the case file.

Sub-section 3 – Audiovisual Surveillance

61 – (Repealed and replaced by Organic Law No. 2019-9 of January 23, 2019)
In cases where the needs of the investigation so require, the Public Prosecutor or the investigating judge of the judicial pole for the fight against terrorism may, as the case may be, order, by means of a written and reasoned decision, authorized judicial police officers to establish terrorist offenses provided for by this law, to set up a technical device in the personal affairs of suspects, in private or public places, premises, or vehicles, in order to capture, record, transmit, and save. .
premises, or private or public vehicles concerned by audiovisual surveillance, the acts justifying it, as well as its duration.

The duration of audiovisual surveillance may not exceed two months from the date of the decision, renewable only once for the same duration and by a reasoned decision. The decision provided for in this article may be withdrawn at any time. The public prosecutor, the investigating judge, or judicial police officers, as the case may be, may be assisted by any authorized agent and expert in order to proceed with the installation of technical devices.

Correspondence, reports, and recordings relating to the audiovisual surveillance operation are recorded in a separate and special file which is attached to the main file before any decision to open an investigation or close the instruction is taken. At the end of its work, the body responsible for audiovisual surveillance prepares a report describing the arrangements made, the operations carried out, their location, date, time, and outcome, to which are obligatorily attached any audiovisual recordings that have been collected and which are useful for establishing the truth.

If the data collected from audiovisual surveillance does not lead to criminal prosecution, it benefits from the protection provisions, in accordance with current legislation in the field of personal data protection. Subsection 4 – Common provisions for special investigation techniques Art. 62 – Anyone who intentionally discloses any information relating to interception, infiltration, audiovisual surveillance operations, or the data collected therein, shall be punished by ten years' imprisonment, without prejudice to, in the case .

Art. 64 - (new) (Repealed and replaced by Organic Law No. 2019-9 of January 23, 2019):
Anyone who, outside the cases authorized by law and without observing legal requirements, intentionally engages in the interception of communications and correspondence, audiovisual surveillance, or infiltration, shall be punished by five years' imprisonment and a fine of five thousand dinars.
Attempt is punishable.

Art. 65 - The means of evidence collected during an operation of infiltration, interception, or audiovisual surveillance may only be invoked to the extent that they prove the offenses concerned by the investigation or any other terrorist offense.

The means that have no relation to the investigation shall be destroyed as soon as a final judgment of conviction or acquittal is pronounced.

In all cases, all means, whether they have a relation to the investigation or not, shall be destroyed in the event of a final judgment of acquittal.

In the event of a final judgment of conviction, the means that have a relation to the investigation shall be kept in the court archives for the legal duration.

All means shall be destroyed in the case of the prescription of public prosecution or in the case of a final decision to dismiss the case without further proceedings.

The destruction operation shall be carried out in the presence of a representative of the Public Prosecutor's Office.
A record shall be drawn up in all cases.

**Section 7**
**Protection Mechanisms**

Art. 71 - **Necessary measures are taken for the protection of persons entrusted by law with the detection and repression of terrorist offenses provided for by this law, including magistrates, judicial police officers, military judicial police officers, customs officers, and public authority agents.**

**Protection measures are also applicable to legal auxiliaries, undercover agents, informants, victims, witnesses, and any person who has committed to reporting an offense to the competent authorities, in any capacity whatsoever.**

**The aforementioned measures are extended, where applicable, to the members** They may proceed to interrogate the suspect and to hear any person whose testimony they deem useful, by using adequate audiovisual communication means without requiring their personal appearance.

Appropriate measures are then taken to preserve the anonymity of the persons heard. In exceptional cases and in the presence of real danger that may result from public hearings, the judicial authority in charge may decide, on its own initiative, at the request of the public prosecutor's representative or at the request of any interested party, to hold hearings in camera. In this case, it is forbidden to disseminate information about the pleadings or decisions that may infringe upon the privacy or reputation of the victims, without prejudice to other guarantees provided for by special texts.
Anyone who infringes the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall be punished by one year's imprisonment and a fine of one thousand dinars.

Art. 74 - The persons referred to in the third paragraph of the preceding article may, if called upon to make statements to judicial police officers, the investigating judge, or any other judicial authority, elect domicile with the Public Prosecutor at the Court of First Instance of Tunis.

Their identity and the address of their actual domicile shall then be recorded in a confidential, numbered, and initialed register kept for this purpose by the Public Prosecutor at the Court of First Instance of Tunis.

Art. 75 - In cases of imminent danger, and if circumstances so require, it shall be possible to record all data that identifies victims, witnesses, and any other person who has undertaken, in any capacity whatsoever, to report the offense to the competent authorities, in independent minutes recorded in a file kept separately from the initial case file.

The judicial authority seized can order the lifting of the aforementioned measures and reveal the identity of the concerned person, if it appears that the request is well-founded, and that there is no danger to fear for their life and property, or for the life or property of their family members. The investigating judge rules on the request to lift the measures within a maximum period of four days from the date the request is submitted. The Public Prosecutor notifies the decision to reveal their identity to the concerned person and receives their response.

The decision to lift or reject the lifting of the measures can be appealed before the indictment chamber, either by the Public Prosecutor, or at the request of the person whose identity has been revealed. It may also be subject to appeal by the suspect, their lawyer, or the civil party, within a period of ten days, from the date of its communication for the Public Prosecutor and from the date of notification for the others. An appeal by the Public Prosecutor suspends the execution of the decision. In case of appeal, the investigating judge immediately forwards the case file to the indictment chamber.

The indictment chamber rules on the appeal request within a period of eight days from the date of receipt of the file. The decision rendered by the indictment chamber to lift the measure or to confirm it is not subject to appeal.

Art. 77 - In no case may the protective measures infringe upon the right of the accused or their lawyer, or the civil party or their representative, to consult the minutes and other documents in the file.

Art. 78 - Anyone who endangers the life or property of persons benefiting from protection or those of their family members shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years and a fine of five thousand to fifty thousand dinars. **Section 8**
**Assistance to Victims of Terrorism**

** Art. 79** - Victims shall benefit from free care and treatment in public health facilities. The National Commission for the Fight Against Terrorism shall ensure that necessary medical assistance is provided to victims in order to guarantee the physical and psychological rehabilitation of those who need it, in coordination with the relevant services and structures.

The Commission shall ensure that necessary social assistance is provided to victims in order to facilitate their social reintegration, in coordination with the relevant services and organizations.

The age, sex, and specific needs of the victims shall be taken into consideration in the implementation of these measures.

**

Art. 80** - The National Commission for the Fight Against Terrorism shall ensure that victims are informed of the provisions governing judicial and administrative procedures that allow them to regularize their situation and obtain appropriate compensation for the damages suffered.

The Commission shall also ensure the follow-up of their cases with public authorities and provide them with assistance, where necessary, to overcome obstacles hindering their access to their rights.

**

Art. 81** - Legal aid shall be granted automatically to victims of terrorism if they request it to initiate civil or criminal judicial proceedings concerning them.

** Art. 82** - The State undertakes to compensate victims of terrorism or their beneficiaries.

The conditions for the application of this article shall be set by government decree.

**Section 9**
**Terrorist Offenses Committed Outside the National Territory**

**

Art. 83** - The Court of First Instance of Tunis, through the judges appointed to the Judicial Pole for the Fight Against Terrorism, shall have jurisdiction to hear terrorist offenses provided for by this law and related offenses committed outside the national territory. ** Art. 85** - The Public Prosecutor at the Court of First Instance of Tunis is solely competent to initiate and exercise criminal proceedings for terrorist offenses provided for by this law and related offenses committed outside the national territory.

**

Art. 86** - Criminal proceedings cannot be initiated against the perpetrators of terrorist offenses provided for by this law and related offenses if they prove that these offenses have acquired the force of res judicata abroad, that they have served any sentence pronounced, or that such sentence has expired or is covered by amnesty.

**Section 10** - On Extradition

**

Art. 87** - Terrorist offenses shall in no case be considered political offenses that do not give rise to extradition.
Offenses of financing terrorism shall in no case be considered fiscal offenses that do not give rise to extradition.

** Art. 88** - Terrorist offenses provided for by this law shall give rise to extradition in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, if they are committed outside the territory of the Republic against a foreigner, or against foreign interests by a foreigner or stateless person present on Tunisian territory.
Extradition shall only be granted if the competent Tunisian authorities receive a legal request from a State competent under its domestic legislation.
Extradition cannot be granted if there are real reasons to believe that the person subject to the extradition request risks torture or that this request is intended to prosecute or punish him/her on account of his/her race, color, origin, religion, sex, nationality, or political opinions.

CHAPTER II
On the Fight Against Money Laundering and its Repression

Art. 92 - (Repealed and replaced by Organic Law No. 2019-9 of January 23, 2019)
Money laundering is considered any intentional act that aims, by any means, to falsely justify the illicit origin of movable or immovable property or income derived directly or indirectly from any crime or misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment of three years or more, as well as any offense sanctioned under the customs code.

Also constituting money laundering is any intentional act aimed at the placement, acquisition, possession, use, deposit, concealment, disguise, management, integration, and safekeeping of proceeds derived directly or indirectly from the offenses provided for in the preceding paragraph, or the attempt, complicity, incitement, facilitation, or contribution to its commission.
The offense of money laundering is independent of the predicate offense for its materiality. It is
proven by the existence of presumptions and sufficient evidence regarding the illegal origin of the assets subject to laundering.

The provisions of the preceding paragraphs shall apply even if the offense - in case of recidivism,
- by the person who benefits from the facilities provided by the exercise of their function or professional or social activity,
- by an organized group or an agreement.
The amount of the fine may be increased to an amount equal to the value of the money laundered.

Art. 95 - When the imprisonment penalty incurred for the principal offense from which the laundered money originates is greater than that provided for the offense stipulated in Articles 93 and 94 of this law, the perpetrator of the money laundering offense shall be punished with the penalties incurred for the principal offense, if it is established that they were aware of it.

Only the aggravating circumstances attached to the principal offense that the perpetrator of the money laundering offense was aware of shall be taken into consideration for the determination of the penalty incurred.

Art. 96 - The penalties provided for in the preceding articles are extended, as appropriate, to the directors of legal persons, their representatives, their agents, their partners, and their statutory auditors whose personal responsibility is established.

This does not prevent prosecution against the said legal persons, if it is established that the laundering operations were carried out for their benefit, or that they resulted in income for them, or that the laundering operations constitute their object. They shall consequently incur a fine equal to five times the value of the fine provided for natural persons. The fine may be increased to an amount equal to the value of the money laundered.

This also does not prevent the extension of disciplinary and administrative sanctions provided for, to the said legal persons in accordance with the legislation in force applicable to them, including the prohibition of carrying out their activity for a determined period or their dissolution.

Art. 97 - The judicial authority in charge shall order the seizure of .
professional or social relationships that provided them with the means used to commit one or more money laundering operations, for a period not exceeding five years.

The court may place the perpetrators of money laundering offenses under administrative surveillance for a period of five years.

This does not prevent the court from imposing all or part of the other additional penalties provided for by law.

CHAPTER ONE
General Provisions

Article 1 - The purpose of this law is to organize "Crowdfunding" to provide the necessary financing for projects and companies in order to promote investment, entrepreneurship, creativity, and innovation.

Art. 2 - For the purposes of this law, the following are understood:
- "Crowdfunding": the method of financing that relies on raising funds from the public via an internet platform dedicated to this purpose in order to finance projects or companies through investment in securities, loans, donations, or endowments.
- "Crowdfunding" Service Provider: a company specializing in "Crowdfunding" activity, through the creation and administration of online platforms connecting the public with companies and projects whose promoters wish to obtain financing.

The "Crowdfunding" Service Provider is an internet platform operator within the meaning of current legislation.
- "Crowdfunding" Platform: a website or mobile application made available to users for the purpose of connecting the public with the company and the project to benefit from "Crowdfunding" services.
- Contributor: any natural or legal person, resident or non-resident, who contributes to the financing of a company or project through "Crowdfunding".
- Project Promoter: any natural or legal person wishing to obtain financing through "Crowdfunding".
- The project: each for-profit initiative that the project promoter presents to obtain financing through "Crowdfunding".

The project presented on the "Crowdfunding" internet platform must be carried out in Tunisia.
- Regulatory Authorities: the Financial Market Council, the Central Bank of Tunisia, and the Microfinance Control Authority.

Article 1 - The purpose of this decree-law is to regulate the creation of credit information companies and the exercise of their activities, and to set the rules for credit information exchange in order to improve their quality, with a view to contributing to the enhancement of financial inclusion.

Art. 2 - Credit information companies shall be governed, with regard to their creation and the exercise of their activities, by the provisions of this decree-law and the legislation relating to the protection of personal data.

Art. 3 - For the purposes of this decree-law, the following shall be understood as:

- Credit information: information relating to the financial commitments of natural and legal persons, concerning the amounts of debts, their due dates, defaults, and all information inherent to them.

- Credit information companies: companies whose activity consists of processing credit information on natural and legal persons, with a view to assessing their ability to honor their financial commitments and offering related services under the conditions set by this decree-law.

- Credit report: A report issued by a credit information company on paper or electronic medium containing credit information of the concerned person and information on their ability to honor their financial commitments.

- Information providers: The parties and organizations mentioned in

Article 12 of this decree-law having a contractual relationship with the credit information company through a credit information supply agreement.

- Authority: The National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data, established by Organic Law No.

2004-63 of July 27, 2004, on the protection of personal data.

- **Payment System**: Refers to the set of instruments, procedures, rules, technical platforms, and networks that enable the processing, clearing, settlement, and transfer of funds between participants based on a contractual commitment with the system operator.
- **Securities Settlement System**: Refers to the complete set of pre-defined institutional arrangements and multilateral rules that enable the confirmation, clearing, and settlement of securities transactions between participants

notably based on the delivery versus payment mechanism.
- **Clearing**: The act of reducing obligations between participants in a clearing arrangement to a single net balance, thereby reducing the number and amount of payments required to settle a set of transactions.
- **Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS)**: A continuous settlement mechanism, without netting, for fund transfer orders, securities, or other obligations between participants on a case-by-case basis

upon receipt.
- **Deferred Net Settlement (DNS)**: A net settlement mechanism that settles obligations between participants on a net cleared basis at the end of a pre-defined settlement cycle.
- **Delivery Versus Payment (DvP) Mechanism**: A securities settlement mechanism that links the transfer of securities and the transfer of funds in such a way as to ensure that the delivery of securities occurs if, and only if, the corresponding payment takes place.

2. Quantification of Risk Exposure
Quantifying risk involves calculating the exposure and simulating the financial effects on the result. Determining the amount of exposure, compared to the company's budget, must integrate the analysis of the intrinsic characteristics of the... **Formulating Risk Perception**

The optimal risk profile of an economic operator balances the benefits of protection against the costs of hedging. The economic operator is therefore called upon to determine their own risk tolerance thresholds and to choose the proportions to cover.

Three possibilities are available in this regard:

*   **Systematic Hedging:** This method consists of automatically hedging as soon as a commitment or asset that could constitute a source of risk appears. This attitude is particularly adopted in cases where the quantification of damage reveals very high amounts, leading to significant losses in the economic operator's profit or margin that could compromise their viability.

*   **Partial Hedging:** This corresponds to setting well-defined limits and criteria for hedging.

Since hedging strategies can be expensive for the economic operator, they could therefore tolerate an uncovered portion of the risk and opt for partial, but more effective, protection (limited, for example, to a certain percentage of the exposure). This approach allows for a more attractive risk/return profile at a reasonable cost.

*   **No Hedging:** For an economic operator, not hedging could represent a rational decision in a specific context, but it must result from a thorough examination of the risks incurred.

Thus, as part of the process of developing a risk management policy, the economic operator must align their risk tolerance with the objectives sought by hedging.

**a. Derivatives Markets**

The Decision-Making Process**
The Hedging Policy must clearly define the decision-making process, which is generally based on two key bodies, pillars of the risk governance structure, namely the Board of Directors or its equivalent management body, and the Steering Committee.

**a. The Board of Directors or Equivalent Management Body**
The "Hedging Policy" document must be approved by the Board of Directors or its equivalent management body.

**b. The Steering Committee**
The Steering Committee is responsible for the implementation of the Hedging Policy, the validation, and the supervision of the risk management strategy.

It is necessary to establish a clear delegation of responsibilities from the Steering Committee within a framework document that also sets out the composition of the Committee. The Committee must include departments whose involvement allows for a good assessment of the level of risk exposure, preferably the Finance and Treasury Department, the Procurement Department, the Commercial Department, and the Department responsible for Risk Management. The Committee reports to the Board of Directors or the equivalent management body on a periodic basis.

The Steering Committee must ensure that market risk analysis and management activities are carried out by personnel possessing the required technical knowledge and experience in the field of financial risks and hedging instruments. A continuous and targeted training policy for human resources involved in risk management is essential to ensure good know-how and to keep pace with rapid market developments. It is also important to equip the structures involved in risk management with appropriate technical means for monitoring markets and evaluating hedging instruments.

Article 16:** A Market Maker is required to provide a firm two-way spot quotation for EUR/TND and USD/TND currency pairs if requested by another Authorized Intermediary.

The maximum spread between the bid and ask prices displayed by the Market Maker is 30 pips maximum, for a maximum currency amount (EUR or USD) of 3 million.

The Market Maker is not required to comply with the provisions of this article for quotation requests concerning currency amounts (EUR or USD) less than 0.5 million, and for all other currencies regardless of the amount.

The Market Maker must execute at least 5% of the interbank spot foreign exchange market volume on average over a year.

**

Article 17:** The internal limits for a Market Maker's foreign exchange positions must be at least equal to two-thirds of the limits provided by current regulations.

The total of daily limits per counterparty granted to other Authorized Intermediaries for spot foreign exchange transactions must be at least equal to 200 million dinars.

The Market Maker is exempt from the quotation obligations stipulated in

**No.

87-25 OF JULY 17, 1987**

**SUBJECT: Granting of Sub-Delegate Status for Currency Exchange and Conditions for Exercising Sub-Delegation.**

The purpose of this circular is, on the one hand, to authorize sub-delegates to carry out manual currency exchange by purchasing foreign currency against dinars, and on the other hand, to introduce relaxations regarding the conditions for granting and exercising sub-delegation, particularly by eliminating the prior authorization of the Central Bank of Tunisia for the granting of sub-delegate status.

It repeals and replaces Circular No.

85-31 and Note No. 85-66 of September 4, 1985.

**I - GENERAL PROVISIONS**

** Article 1:** Apart from Approved Intermediaries and customs offices authorized for this purpose, only persons who have previously obtained a sub-delegation from an Approved Intermediary may accept foreign banknotes and traveler's checks carried by non-resident Tunisian or foreign travelers.

**

Article 2:** Individuals or legal entities, including hotels, travel agencies, and craft product sales shops, who, due to the nature of their activity, are likely to receive means of payment expressed in foreign currency from non-resident travelers, are authorized to receive sub-delegations.

** Article 3:** Sub-delegation authorizes its holder to:

1°) Accept the settlement of purchases or services by non-residents through the transfer of foreign currency.

2°) Carry out manual currency exchange by purchasing foreign currency against the delivery of dinars.

Sub-delegates are in no case authorized to issue foreign currency.

CIRCULAR TO LICENSED INTERMEDIARY BANKS N°2008-04 OF MARCH 03, 2008

Subject: Carrying out manual foreign exchange activity

Article 1: Licensed intermediary banks may, in accordance with current legislation, carry out manual foreign exchange activity within specialized agencies called "bureaux de change" (exchange offices).
Article 2: The opening of exchange offices is subject to the conditions set out in Annex n°1 of this circular. These conditions constitute minimum requirements.

Article 3: Licensed intermediary banks must declare to the Central Bank of Tunisia, according to the models provided in Annexes n°2 and n°3 of this circular, any operation of opening or closing an exchange office at least fifteen (15) working days in advance of the date of opening or closing.

It is prohibited to use the premises, subject to closure, for carrying out any operation with customers.
Article 4: The provisions of the preceding article apply to any operation of temporary or definitive transfer of an exchange office.

Article 5: Bank branches and exchange offices, established in the zones determined in Annex n°4 of this circular, must provide foreign exchange services outside ordinary working hours, including during public holidays, in accordance with on-call schedules among them which determine, in particular, the hours during which these services must be provided.
The Central Bank of Tunisia shall set the said schedule and inform bank branches and exchange offices of it.

Article 6: Exchange offices must display to the public, using visible electronic displays, the exchange rates in dinars applied to the sale and purchase operations with customers of foreign banknotes and traveler's checks. **APPENDIX N°1 TO CIRCULAR TO APPROVED INTERMEDIARY BANKS N°2008-04**

**CONDITIONS FOR OPENING FOREIGN EXCHANGE OFFICES**

Approved intermediary banks must comply with the following conditions when opening a foreign exchange office:

**

Article 1:** The foreign exchange office premises must be visible and identifiable to the public.

To this end, the term "foreign exchange office" must be displayed on the facade of the foreign exchange office.

** Article 2:** Approved intermediary banks must take all security measures relating to the protection of persons and the premises of the foreign exchange office.

They must ensure that the premises are permanently connected to the police station by means of a special telephone line.

**

Article 3:** Approved intermediary banks must have a procedures manual relating to the security of foreign exchange office premises, specifically describing police alert procedures in case of justified concerns or aggression. The procedures manual must be made available to the agents of the foreign exchange office.

Approved intermediary banks must also implement training programs for these agents.

**

Article 4:** The foreign exchange office must be permanently connected to the bank's headquarters by all means of communication and data exchange. ANNEX 2 TO CIRCULAR 2008-04 TO APPROVED INTERMEDIARY BANKS

**No.

2002-17 of August 5, 2002**

**SUBJECT: Verification of the identity of travel check holders.**

It has been brought to my attention that certain authorized intermediaries and sub-delegates of exchange have cashed travel checks for foreign tourists by referring, for the verification of these tourists' identity, to passports other than those used for entry into Tunisia.

Consequently, and to avoid the risks of fraud that could be committed by travelers holding travel checks, such as the presentation of forged travel checks for payment, authorized intermediaries are required to refer, for the purpose of verifying the identity of these persons, to passports bearing the entry stamp into Tunisia and to inform the sub-delegates of exchange carrying out exchange operations on their behalf of these provisions. 93-48 of May 1993, commitments in matters of current operations and the resulting transfers are free. The present circular aims to establish the conditions and modalities for Intermediaries Agreed to carry out transfers related to current operations concerning international transport and to define the applicable rules regarding transport operators' revenues and expenses.

FIRST TITLE
MARITIME TRANSPORT
FIRST CHAPTER
REGULATIONS ON CHARTERING OF NON-RESIDENT SHIPS

The rules resulting from chartering contracts of non-resident ships, including, if applicable, advances and commissions in favor of non-resident brokers, are carried out by Intermediaries Agreed in accordance with the indications of the Ministry in charge of Merchant Navy, as stated in the reserved form*.

FIRST CHAPTER 2
REVENUES OF NON-RESIDENT MARITIME COMPANIES ON PASSENGER, BAGGAGE, AND V 3) Consignators shall open on their account books, in the name of each non-resident shipowner, a Non-resident Shipowner Account intended to record the receipts and expenses effectively received or incurred during Tunisian port calls of vessels whose consignment they have been entrusted with. The Non-resident Shipowner Account shall be kept in such a way that all receipts and expenses related to a single port call can be traced at any moment.

Exporters and transitors must repay the amount of these advances within a maximum period of 3 months from the date they were made to the consignator of the ships.

- advances for port charges of the non-resident shipowner's vessels;

These advances are settled to the consignators either A) Repayment of the debtor's balance
When the cleared balance on the account at the date of the arrest is a debt for the ship's owner, the amount of this debt must be repaid no later than one month after the date of the arrest of the account, unless it is covered, before the expiration of this period, by the registration of other receipts to the credit of the account.

B) Settlements among ship owners' agents representing the same non-resident shipowner

Without prejudice to the preceding provisions, ship owners' agents representing the same non-resident shipowner may, upon instructions from the latter, proceed with compensation between the debtor balances and the creditor balances of the said shipowner.

SECTION 2
REVENUES AND EXPENSES OF RESIDENT SHIPOWNERS

1°) Resident shipowners must be represented in every country of destination of their ships, except where they have their own offices of representation, by one or more agents (ship owners' agents or any other agent to whom the ship consignment may be entrusted) charged with collecting receipts and engaging expenses of call for the said ships in one of the ports of that country.

2°) The expenses of any call of ships of a resident shipowner can be settled through receipts collected by the same representative for that call or 2) Repatriation of the creditor's balance

When the cleared balance is in favor of the resident shipowner, the amount of this balance should be repatriated no later than one month after the date of the position's arrest, unless it is used before the expiration of this delay to cover other port expenses.

3) Settlements between the foreign representatives of a resident shipowner

Without prejudice to the preceding provisions, the representatives of a resident shipowner in the same foreign country may, upon instructions from the latter, proceed with compensation between the debtor balances and the creditor balances of their respective positions regarding said shipowner.

CHAPTER 4
COMMON EXPLOITATION OF SHIPS BY RESIDENT AND NON-RESIDENT SHIPOWNERS

1) In the context of the common exploitation of ships with non-resident shipowners, resident shipowners may make settlements in favor of these last ones, either in the form of profit distribution or of their contribution to the exploitation charges. The result of the exploitation must be settled at least once a year.

The result of the exploitation must be settled at least once a year. Transfers related to these settlements are made by the Designated Intermediaries, upon presentation:
- of the association contract subject to approval by the Ministry in charge of Merchant Marine,
- and of a signed and certified statement conforming to the accounting records by the resident A) Credit Operations

These advances to the credit account are recorded upon presentation of all relevant documents justifying the importation of currencies (credit memos, banking statements, etc.).

PARAGRAPH 2
SETTLEMENT OF NON-RESIDENT TIR ACCOUNT

Representatives in Tunisia of non-resident road transport operators must settle the balance of any open TIR Non-resident account on their books no later than three months following its opening or the last date it was settled. They may transfer the credit balance 3) Resident road transporters must keep a record of all receipts collected and expenses incurred by their representatives abroad. This record shall be kept in such a way that all receipts and expenses related to a single journey can be traced at any moment.

PARAGRAPH 1
JOURNEY RECEIPTS AND EXPENSES

A) Journey receipts

The journey receipts of resident road transporters' vehicles abroad are composed of:
- transport charges and accessory receipts;
- advances made by resident road transporters to their representatives abroad for travel expenses.

The transfers under these regulations are carried out by Authorized Intermediaries, upon presentation of:
- of the common exploitation agreement, as prescribed by the transport terrestrial ministry,
- and of a signed and certified statement by the railway transport company resident, indicating the collected receipts and incurred expenses by each transport company, the operating result and its distribution. 2°) The amounts due to railway transport companies residents by non-resident railway transport companies, in regard to the distribution of the net operating result, must be repatriated no later than one month following their due date.

CHAPTER 3
INTERNATIONAL TRANSPORT OF PASSENGERS AND GOODS BY RAIL
SECTION 1
REGULATIONS BETWEEN MAGHREB RAILWAY TRANSPORT COMPANIES

The transfers under these regulations, in favor of one of the Maghreb railway transport companies, by the Tunisian National Railways, are carried out by Authorized Intermediaries, upon presentation of an extract duly certified by this last one from the companies' accounts established by the Maghreb Central Compensation Bureau, indicating the compensated amounts, the resulting balances, and the payable amount.

SECTION 2
TRANSFER OF REVENUES OF FOREIGN RAILWAY TRANSPORT COMPANIES OTHER Title IV
OPERATIONS RELATED TO INTERNATIONAL TRANSPORT OPERATIONS

A) Presentations of invoices or any other document in lieu, as specified by the resident operator for the operations subject to Annex 2 of the present circular.

B) Presentations of the following documents for each of the following operations:
- Refunds (payments made to a non-resident charger in reimbursement of the freight charges they incurred for the transportation of merchandise, provided the freight charges are individually identified in relation to the total transport cost borne by the foreign trade operator).
* A signed and certified receipt by the non-resident charger's representative (shipper, shipper's agent, international road transport company, warehouse keeper or any other person authorized by the Ministry in charge of merchant shipping or land transport) indicating the identity of the non-resident charger and the foreign trade operator, the commission amounts received, and the amount to be transferred.
- Monthly advances in foreign currency to the resident crew's salaries.
* A certified statement by the shipping company or airline, indicating the identities of the beneficiaries, their qualifications, the amount of the advance granted, and the payee's identity.

The delivery of funds in cash or by check gives rise, in all cases, to the beneficiary being issued an authorization for foreign exchange withdrawal in two copies, one of which must be kept by the beneficiary and the other handed over to customs services. In the case where funds are being transferred, in the name of the ship's crew, to the ship's captain, the authorization for foreign exchange withdrawal delivered to the captain must indicate the names of all ship's crew members benefiting from the transfer in this capacity.

Prior to the execution of the first transfer in relation to one of the operations outlined in this circular, Approved Intermediaries must be provided with:

- A copy of the agreement issued to the principal party for the practice of their activity in Tunisia as an air transport company or an international road transport company for goods or a copy of the professional card issued to the principal party and specifying their authorization to practice their activity in Tunisia as an owner, freight forwarder, or shipper of vessels;
- An attestation from the principal party indicating the persons authorized to sign transfer orders and statements, accompanied by samples of their signatures,
- And for transfer orders placed by representatives in Tunisia of a shipowner, an international road transport company, or a non-resident freight forwarder, a company certificate.

TITLE VII 
INFORMATION FROM THE BANQUE CENTRALE DE TUNISIE 

The procedure for informing the Banque Centrale de Tunisie by Authorized Intermediaries will continue to be governed by the applicable texts, in particular by Note 86-42 to Authorized Intermediaries of December 31, 1986.
All contrary provisions or those creating overlap with the present circular are repealed. The present circular takes effect from the date of its notification.

OBJECT: Scholarship transfers for the benefit of students abroad. The following circular sets out the conditions and modalities for Intermediaries Agreed to carry out scholarship transfers for Tunisian or foreign students pursuing their studies abroad. I - BENEFICIARIES OF SCHOLARSHIP TRANSFERS

Eligible for scholarship transfers:
- any non-bachelor student and any student holding a bachelor's degree or equivalent;
- students holding a university degree;
- handicapped students enrolled in specialized institutions. II - SCHOLARSHIP ALLOCATIONS

A) INSTALLATION ALLOWANCE

The installation allowance transfer is made as an annual allocation of a maximum amount of four thousand dinars (4000DT). The transfer of this allocation can be made in one lump sum or in installments during the considered academic year. B) SEJOUR ALLOWANCE

The maximum amount of the allocation that can be transferred abroad for living expenses during the academic year or school year is set at [an amount in dinars].

The submission of one or both of these two documents is not required from the student registering with a faculty, a grand school or any other higher education institution abroad, starting from at least the second year of studies offered by the concerned university establishment, regardless of whether the student has previously compiled a scholarship transfer file.

- for the disability card. (The 4th dash has been removed by circular no.

2°) The original and a photocopy:
- either of the certificate of enrollment attesting that the interested party is regularly enrolled abroad for the current school year or university year at an secondary, superior or specialized institution for the disabled.
- Or for students benefiting from a scholarship or university loan, of the scholarship or loan grant certificate.

In case the interested party is not a bachelor, he must provide a declaration on honor signed and legalized stating that he does not benefit from a scholarship or, if applicable, the scholarship amount.

In the case of opening the file based on one of these last two pieces, the student is obliged to complete it no later than three months after the start of the academic year 4) Transfers for registration and study fees are made either by wire transfer or by checks payable to the order of the foreign education institution. 5) Delivery of currency in cash or checks results in the beneficiary receiving an "authorization for foreign exchange withdrawal" in two copies from the Approved Intermediary, one of which must be kept by the interested party.

IV - RELATIONS WITH THE TUNISIAN CENTRAL BANK -

- A report, established according to the model in annex (B), of foreign currency transfers for tuition fees made during the previous month. 3) In case of a change of domiciliation, the previous Approved Intermediary will inform the Tunisian Central Bank of the closure of the file and provide a copy of the required certification (as per paragraph III-A).

OBJECT: Tourist Allocation Article 1: The following circulatory sets out the conditions and modalities for implementation by Intermediaries Approved for transfers regarding the tourist allocation.

SECTION 1
BENEFICIARIES OF THE ALLOCATION

Article 2: Eligible for the delivery of the tourist allocation are:

3) Tunisians who were non-residents according to the regulations on changes and have returned definitively to Tunisia, regardless of the duration of their stay in Tunisia after said return.

The definitive return can be proven by any official document (consular attestation, document attesting the benefit of a customs duty exemption for household goods or vehicles…).

SECTION II
AMOUNT OF THE ALLOCATION

Article 3: The amount of the tourist allocation is set at the sum of six thousand dinars

Article 11: The traveler must keep the formule "A" for proof of the origin of the currency or checks they possess before leaving Tunisia, presented to customs. c) remove formule "B" and keep it available for the Central Bank of Tunisia for control purposes.

Subject: Procedures for the delivery of tourist allocations by Approved Intermediaries.

It has come to my attention that certain Approved Intermediaries do not take the necessary precautions when granting tourist allocations by delivering currencies to persons other than the passport holders. Therefore, the attention of Approved Intermediaries is drawn to the fact that any applicant for a tourist allocation must present himself in person at the bank counter with his passport and sign the forms A, B and C referred to in the annexes 1, 2, 3 and 4 of Circular No. 2007-04 of February 9, 2007 on the tourist allocation, in the presence of the counter clerk.

The Approved Intermediary must also keep in accessible files, in addition to form B intended for him, copies of the two pages of the passport bearing the traveler's identity and the object of the tourist allocation granted. 1 Annexes 2, 3 and 4 of Circular No. 2007-04 of February 9, 2007 on the tourist allocation have been abolished and replaced by the CIRCULAR TO INTERMEDIARIES

Intermediary bank: any bank that receives and transmits an electronic funds transfer in a payment coverage series or chain, on behalf of the order giver's institution and the beneficiary's institution or another intermediary bank. Electronic funds transfer: any operation performed electronically, through a national or foreign financial institution, on behalf of an order giver, to make funds available to a beneficiary through another financial institution. The order giver and beneficiary may be the same person. Batch transfer: a set of several individual electronic funds transfers grouped for transmission.

Unique operation reference number: a combination of letters, numbers, or symbols defined according to the payment and settlement or messaging systems used to execute the electronic funds transfer and ensuring traceability of the transaction to the order giver and beneficiary. Order giver: any person authorizing a funds transfer from an account or, in the absence of an account, issuing a funds transfer order. Beneficiary: the intended recipient of the funds transfer. Qualified transfer: any cross-border transfer of funds exceeding the countervalue of 1000 dinars.

Title I: Vigilance Measures and Client/Operation Diligences
Chapter I: General Vigilance Measures

Article 3:

Six main points, notably the calibration of alert levels in relation to risk profiles; and:

The subject establishment may, for the purpose of identifying money laundering and terrorist financing risks, rely on precise data related to its activity as well as information from the national risk assessment and reports published by international organizations. The results of the risk assessment must be documented in a report called the "Risk Evaluation Report for Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing of the Subject Establishment". This report must break down the risk matrix by country, geographical zone, client type, product type, and distribution channel.

Article 7:

Article 10:
Subject institutions with foreign subsidiaries or branches must ensure that these entities take appropriate measures to protect against the risk of being used for money laundering and terrorist financing and are equipped with a vigilance mechanism at least equivalent to that provided for in this circular.

These subsidiaries and branches must communicate to the parent company, as necessary, the local applicable measures in host countries that oppose the implementation of all or part of the requirements set out in this circular.

When the obligations set out in this circular are not fully or partially implemented by the subsidiary or branch, the parent company must take all necessary measures to ensure compliance with these obligations.

Article 11:
Establishments subject to this consolidated financial group must implement programs to combat money laundering and terrorist financing adapted to all their branches and subsidiaries in which they hold a majority participation. These programs include:
(a) policies and procedures for sharing required information for vigilance regarding clientele and risk management of money laundering and terrorist financing;
(b) making available information from branches and subsidiaries regarding clients, accounts, and operations when necessary for anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing efforts, to compliance and audit functions at group level; and
(c) satisfactory guarantees in terms of confidentiality and use of exchanged information.

Article 12:
Establishments subject to this provision must exercise continuous vigilance throughout the business relationship. They must ensure that operations and assets placed with persons with whom they have a relationship are consistent with their knowledge of the client, their commercial activities, their risk profile, and, where applicable, the origin of the funds. Establishments subject to this provision must, therefore, ensure, through regular control, the updating and relevance of the documents, data or information collected during the customer due diligence process. Request for additional information from the client to ensure they are not suspicious as per the present circular.

Chapter II: Reinforced Vigilance Measures

Article 15:
Established entities must exercise enhanced vigilance for identifying clients not residing in Tunisia. They must require, for instance, a reference letter delivered by their bank in their country of residence.

Established entities shall apply in addition to the measures provided in Chapter I of Title I, for clients acting as principal or beneficiary of enhanced due diligence measures, when:
- the client is a resident of countries identified by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) communiqués as countries not applying or not adequately applying the international anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing norms; and
- the transaction is carried out using new technologies of information and communication.

Article 18:
Established entities are obliged, in their business dealings and transactions with natural and legal persons from countries identified by the FATF as countries not applying or not adequately applying the international anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing norms, to apply proportionate counter-measures, notably:
- to systematically declare suspicious transactions;
- to apply enhanced due diligence measures.

Article 14:
Prohibition of using third parties established in the concerned country to perform certain elements of the vigilance process regarding the client.

Article 20:
Establishments subject to this Regulation shall implement a system enabling the identification and assessment of risks related to the use of new technologies for money laundering or terrorist financing purposes. To this end, they shall be equipped with risk management systems allowing for the identification and assessment of money laundering or terrorist financing risks arising:
- from the development of new products and services, including new distribution channels; and
- from the use of new or emerging technologies in connection with new or existing products.

The risk assessment referred to in the first subparagraph of this Article shall be carried out before the launch of new products or services or before the use of new or emerging technologies. Establishments subject to this Regulation shall take appropriate measures to manage and mitigate these risks as well as those specific risks linked to business relationships and transactions not involving the physical presence of the parties.

Article 21:
Establishments subject to this Regulation shall apply enhanced due diligence to any transaction or operation:
- which appears to have no relation to the client’s business;
- for which the documents or information indicating its purpose have not been provided; or
- which involves high-risk countries or high-risk sectors. 15

Establishments subject to examination shall review the framework in which operations or transactions requiring enhanced vigilance are carried out and shall record the results of this examination in writing and make them available to the Central Bank of Tunisia and the auditors.

Chapter III : Specific Vigilance Measures Regarding Electronic Funds Transfer Operations

Article 22 :
The vigilance measures provided for in this chapter apply to all electronic funds transfer operations, regardless of currency, that are initiated or received by a bank or financial institution. They do not apply, however, to the following transfers:
a) made using credit or debit cards for the purchase of goods or services, provided that the card number accompanies all transfers resulting from the operation;
b) made on behalf of a public administration for the payment of taxes, fines, or other deductions; and
c) for which the issuer and beneficiary are both banks or financial institutions acting on their own behalf.

Section I : Diligences to be Observed by the Ordering Establishment

Article 23:
The establishment subject to the orderer shall ensure that international transfers contain the following exact and complete information about the orderer:
a) the name and first name of the orderer. a) the name and surname of the beneficiary; and
b) the beneficiary's bank or postal account number or, in the absence of an account, a unique operation reference number enabling traceability of the transaction.

International transfers not qualifying as funds transfers must contain the name and surname of the order giver and the beneficiary, as well as each party's account number or unique operation reference number. The order giver's establishment may not verify the accuracy of these details, except in cases of suspected money laundering or terrorism financing.

Article 24:

The order giver's establishment verifies the accuracy of the information specified in

Article 23 of this circular before issuing a qualified international transfer, based on documents, data, or reliable information from a source.

The verification referred to in the first paragraph of this article is considered to have been completed.

Article 25:
The issuer of the order must refuse to execute any international fund transfers if the required information is incomplete or missing.

Article 26:
When multiple cross-border electronic transfers originating from the same orderer are transmitted in batches to beneficiaries, they may be exempted from the obligations regarding orderer information under article 23 of this circular, provided they contain the orderer's account number or unique operation reference number and the batch includes complete and accurate information on the orderer, as well as complete information on the beneficiaries. The entire trail of these information must be reconstructable in the receiving country.

Article 27:
Domestic fund transfers must include the information specified in

article 23 of this circular, except when this information can be made available:
a) by the beneficiary's institution or the Central Bank of Tunisia through any other means within 3 business days following receipt by the orderer's institution, or
b) by judicial authorities upon request.

In such cases, the orderer's institution only includes the account number or a unique operation reference number enabling the reconstruction of the transfer trail. Section II: Obligations for Intermediary Banks

Article 28:
An intermediary bank must ensure that all information about the order giver and beneficiary accompanying an electronic transfer remain attached. When technical ordering constraints prevent the required information about the order giver or beneficiary from being transmitted with the corresponding electronic transfer, the intermediary bank is required to keep the received information from the order giver's bank or another intermediary bank for at least ten years.

Article 29:
An intermediary bank must implement appropriate procedures to detect if, in the messaging or payment and settlement system used to execute the funds transfer, the fields intended to contain the order giver and beneficiary information have been filled in using unauthorized characters or elements, according to the system's conventions.

Article 30:
An intermediary bank must have policies and procedures based on risk assessment to decide whether to execute, suspend, request additional information, or reject funds transfers where required information about the order giver and beneficiary is missing or incomplete, or the fields concerning these informations have not been filled in using authorized characters or elements.
