Title IV 
Of the governance of banks and financial institutions

Article 40 - Banks and financial institutions are required to establish an effective governance system, capable of guaranteeing their sustainability and preserving the interests of depositors, creditors, and shareholders. The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the organizational conditions for governance. 
Chapter I 
Of governance policies Article 41 - Banks and financial institutions are required to establish an internal control system adapted to the nature and size of their activities and which guarantees the effectiveness of operations, the protection of assets, and the control of risks in the context of compliance with the laws and regulations governing their activities. This system must include in particular: 
- a procedural system governing operations and their control in order to guarantee their security,   
- an administrative and accounting organization that guarantees the reliability of financial information, 
- a system for identifying, monitoring, and controlling risks, 
- a system for archiving operations and data.

Article 42 - Without prejudice to the provisions of Organic Law No. 2015-26 of August 7, 2015, relating to the fight against terrorism and the repression of money laundering, banks and financial institutions are required to adopt rules for good management of money laundering and terrorism financing risks, including an internal control system to avoid the use of the bank or the financial institution.
For the purpose of financial and economic illicit activities financing. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the conditions for the application of this article.

Art. 43 - Banks and financial institutions are required to adopt a policy aimed at effective conflict of interest management. The Central Bank of Tunisia sets, for this purpose, rules governing transactions with persons having links with the bank or financial institution, within the meaning of this law, and in particular the limits of financing granted.

A person having links with the bank or financial institution is considered to be: 
- any shareholder whose participation exceeds, directly or indirectly, 5% of the bank's or financial institution's capital, 
- any spouse, ascendant, and descendant of a natural person whose participation exceeds, directly or indirectly, 5% of the bank's or financial institution's capital, 
- any company in which the bank or financial institution holds a capital participation proportion that enables it to control or significantly influence its activity, 
- the chairman of the board of directors of a bank or financial institution, the general manager, members of the board of directors, deputy general managers, members of the supervisory board, members of the executive board, members of the compliance committee with Islamic banking standards, and auditors, as well as the spouses of the aforementioned persons, their ascendants, and descendants, 
- any company of which one of the above-mentioned persons is the owner, associate, delegated proxy, or director, or a member of its board of directors, executive board, or supervisory board.
Art. 44 - Banks and financial institutions are required to adopt a remuneration policy for their executives that is adequate to the fundamental indicators of solidity, solvency, and profitability.

Article 45 - Banks and financial institutions are required to adopt a financial disclosure policy regarding their activities, financial indicators, and internal governance and control rules. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the financial disclosure rules. 
Chapter II 
On the rules organizing the governance structures of banks and financial institutions

Article 46 - Banks and financial institutions managed by a board of directors must separate the function of chairman of the board of directors and the function of general manager. 
It is prohibited for the general manager and the deputy general manager of a bank or financial institution to be a member of the board of directors of that bank or financial institution. 
By way of exception, a financial institution may, after approval from the Central Bank of Tunisia, granted considering the nature of the institution and the volume of its activity, combine the functions of chairman of the board of directors and general manager.

Article 47 - The board of directors or the supervisory board of a bank or financial institution must have at least two independent members from the shareholders and one member representing small shareholders within the meaning of the legislation and regulation related to the financial market, with regard to institutions listed on the Tunis Stock Exchange. 
The term of office of independent members and the member representing small shareholders may be renewed only once. 
Is considered an independent member, within the meaning of this law, any person having no ties with the said bank or institution or with its shareholders or managers that could compromise the independence of their decisions or lead to a situation of actual or potential conflict of interest. 
Are considered small shareholders, the public within the meaning of the legislation organizing the financial market. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the criteria determining the quality of independence.
Article 48 - The board of directors or the supervisory board defines the strategy of the bank or financial institution and ensures its execution.

It monitors all significant changes affecting the activity of the bank or financial institution, in a manner that preserves the interests of depositors, shareholders, all stakeholders, and in general, the long-term interests of the bank or financial institution.

The board of directors or the supervisory board is responsible, in particular, for: 
- controlling the degree of involvement of the management of the bank or financial institution in the implementation of the governance system and evaluating
This device in a periodic manner as to its adaptation to significant changes that have occurred at the bank or financial institution, particularly in terms of business size, complexity of operations, market evolution, and organizational requirements, 
- to establish, in consultation with the general management or board of directors, a risk appetite strategy that takes into account the competitive and regulatory environment as well as the bank's or financial institution's ability to master risks,  
- to appoint the general management or board of directors, 
- to close the financial statements and prepare the annual report of the bank or financial institution, 
- to establish models for measuring the adequacy of own funds in relation to the volume and nature of risks, liquidity management policies, compliance requirements with laws and texts governing activity, and the internal control system, and ensure their implementation, 
- to appoint the head of the internal audit structure, on proposal from the general management or board of directors.
The board of directors or supervisory board must provide all financial, human, and logistical resources and procedures capable of enabling it to effectively fulfill its mission.

Art. 49 - The bank or financial institution must create an audit committee emanating from the board of directors or supervisory board that assists it in establishing an effective internal control system and will be responsible, in particular: 
- for monitoring the proper functioning of internal control, proposing corrective measures, and ensuring their implementation, 
- for reviewing the main internal control reports and financial information before their transmission to the Central Bank of Tunisia, 
- for providing its opinion to the board of directors or supervisory board on the annual report and financial statements. - to propose the appointment of one or more auditors and to provide its opinion on the control programs and their results.

Art. 50 - The bank or financial institution must create a risk committee emanating from the board of directors or the supervisory board that assists it, in particular, in establishing a risk management strategy and will be responsible, in particular: 
- for providing its opinion to the board of directors or the supervisory board on the identification, measurement, and control of risks, 
- for periodically evaluating the risk management policy and its implementation,  
- for monitoring the activity of the body responsible for risk management.

Art. 51 - Every bank must create a nomination and remuneration committee emanating from the board of directors or the supervisory board that assists it, in particular, in designing and monitoring policies: 
- for nomination and remuneration, 
- for replacing executives and senior managers and recruitment, 
- for managing conflict of interest situations.

Art. 52 – Each of the committees provided for in Articles 49, 50, and 51 of this law must be composed of three members from among the members of the board of directors or the supervisory board. 
The audit committee and the risk committee are chaired by an independent member within the meaning of Article 47 of this law. 
It is prohibited to accumulate the status of member in the audit committee and in the risk committee. 
Financial institutions may, if the volume of their activity and the nature of their operations justify it and with the agreement of the Central Bank of Tunisia, combine the audit committee and the risk committee into a single committee.

Art. 53 - The bank or financial institution must create within its organizational chart internal audit functions, risk management, and compliance control. These functions must be independent of the operational and support bodies. 
The secretariat of the audit committee and the risk committee is ensured by the internal audit body and the risk management body. The bank or financial institution must notify, without delay, the Central Bank of Tunisia of any appointment or change that occurs at the level of the main officials responsible for audit, risk management, and compliance control.

Art. 54 - The bank or financial institution approved in accordance with this law to carry out Islamic banking operations as provided for in Chapter I of Title II of this law may create
A committee named "Islamic Banking Standards Compliance Committee" attached to the board of directors or the supervisory board, which is responsible for: 
- ensuring the compliance of Islamic banking operations with the standards defined in this area, 
- issuing an opinion on the compliance of products, contract models, and operational procedures of the activity with Islamic banking standards, 
- examining any issue raised by a bank or financial institution related to Islamic banking operations.

The Islamic Banking Standards Compliance Committee consists of at least three members of Tunisian nationality, appointed for a three-year term renewable only once, by the general assembly of the said bank or financial institution. These members are chosen based on their integrity, competence, and experience in the Islamic banking field, as well as the absence of conflict of interest situations with the bank or financial institution. It is also prohibited for any member of this committee to sit on more than one Islamic Banking Standards Compliance Committee.

The bank or financial institution is required to notify, without delay, the Central Bank of Tunisia of any appointment of members of the Islamic Banking Standards Compliance Committee. The Islamic Banking Standards Compliance Committee may request the bank or financial institution to provide it with the documents and clarifications it deems necessary to fulfill its mission. The Islamic Banking Standards Compliance Committee prepares an annual report on the results of its activities, which will be submitted to the board of directors or the supervisory board.
A copy of this report is sent to the Central Bank of Tunisia and the general assembly, at least one month before the date of its meeting.

The bank or financial institution is required, after consultation with the compliance control committee for Islamic banking standards, to appoint an auditor of Islamic banking operations who will be responsible for ensuring the compliance of transactions with the opinions and proposals of the committee as approved by the board of directors or the supervisory board. The auditor of Islamic banking operations will serve as the secretary of the said committee. The members of the compliance control committee for Islamic banking standards are required to maintain professional secrecy regarding the information they have become aware of in the course of their duties and must refrain from using this information, except in cases permitted by law, for purposes other than those required for the execution of their duties, even after they have lost their position, and are subject to the penalties provided for in

Article 254 of the penal code.

Chapter III 
Rules governing members of governance structures

Art. 55 - The bank or financial institution is required to notify the Central Bank of Tunisia within a period not exceeding seven days of any appointment of the president, a member of the board of directors, the supervisory board, the general manager, the deputy general manager, and the president, or a member of the executive board. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia may, taking into account the criteria provided for in

Article 56 of this law, oppose the said appointment within a period of one month from the date of its notification. It is required to provide justification for any decision to oppose. As soon as it is informed of the decision to oppose, the bank or financial institution must suspend the appointment decision.

Art. 56 - In the appointment of the persons provided for in

Article 55 of this law, the bank or financial institution must base its decision, in particular, on the following criteria: 
- integrity and reputation, 
- scientific qualifications, competence, and professional experience, as well as their consistency with the functions entrusted to the person concerned, 
- the absence of prohibitions provided for in

Article 60 of this law. 
The bank or financial institution must also base its decision on the criteria provided for in Article 47 of this law with regard to the appointment of independent members and the member representing minority shareholders.

Art. 57 - The general manager, deputy general manager, or member of the executive board of a bank or financial institution may not hold any of these positions in another bank, financial institution, insurance company, stock brokerage firm, portfolio management company, or investment company.
No one can hold the position of member of the board of directors or supervisory board in two banks. 
No one can hold the position of member of the board of directors or supervisory board in two financial institutions of the same category, within the meaning of this law.
Art. 58 - The general manager, deputy general manager or member of the management board of a bank or financial institution cannot exercise the function of manager of an economic enterprise.

Art. 59 - The chairman of the board of directors, general manager, chairman of the supervisory board or chairman of the management board of resident banks and financial institutions must be of Tunisian nationality. 
The general manager or chairman of the management board of a bank or financial institution must have the status of resident in Tunisia within the meaning of the exchange regulation in force. 
The governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia may, by decision, grant, on an exceptional basis, the status of resident to the persons referred to in the previous paragraph, after consultation with the minister responsible for finance.

Art. 60 - No one can manage, administer, manage, control or commit a bank, financial institution, agency, or branch of a bank or financial institution: 
- if they have been the subject of an irrevocable judgment for forgery, theft, breach of trust, swindling, extortion of funds or values of others, embezzlement committed by a public depositary, corruption or tax evasion, issuing a check without provision, receiving stolen goods obtained through these offenses or infringement of the exchange regulation or legislation related to the fight against money laundering and the financing of terrorism

- if they have been the subject of an irrevocable judgment of bankruptcy, - if they have been a manager or agent of companies condemned under the provisions of the penal code related to bankruptcy, Page 2206 Journal Officiel de la République Tunisienne — 15 juillet 2016 N° 58 - if, under a sanction imposed by the Central Bank of Tunisia or by one of the authorities responsible for controlling the financial market or insurance and reinsurance companies or microfinance institutions, they have been revoked from administrative or management functions of a company subject to the control of the aforementioned authorities

Art. 61 - Members of the board of directors, supervisory board, management board, or general management of a bank or financial institution, their representatives, controllers, and employees are required to respect professional secrecy for the information they have become aware of as a result of their duties and not to use this information, except in cases permitted by law, for purposes other than those required by the execution of the tasks entrusted to them, even after the loss of their positions, and this, under penalty of the sanctions provided for in

Article 254 of the Penal Code.

Art. 62 - Any agreement concluded between the bank or financial institution and persons having links with them within the meaning of Article 43 of this law is subject to the prior authorization of the board of directors or supervisory board and the approval of the general meeting of shareholders. The chairman of the board of directors or the chairman of the supervisory board must submit these agreements to the general meeting of shareholders for approval based on a special report established by the auditor or auditors. The person concerned may not participate in the vote and their shares are not taken into account for the calculation of the quorum and majority. Unapproved agreements remain applicable, however, the harmful effects will be attributed, in case of fraud, to the party to the contract or the board of directors or supervisory board, if it has been established that they were aware of it.

The provisions of this article do not apply to transactions with a value of less than 15 000 TND, and to transactions that are subject to the regulations of the SWIFT network, and to transactions that are subject to the AML, KYC, CDD, EDD, STR, BCT, CTAF, and FATF regulations, and to transactions with PEP. Regarding the agreements related to ordinary operations concluded under normal conditions between the bank or financial institution and its clients.

However, the chairman of the board of directors, the chairman of the supervisory board, the chief executive officer, the chairman of the executive board, the members of the board of directors, the members of the supervisory board, the members of the executive board, and the deputy chief executive officers must inform the board of directors or the supervisory board and the Central Bank of Tunisia of any agreement concluded with the bank or financial institution that falls within the framework of ordinary operations.

The Central Bank of Tunisia may request the bank or financial institution, in the event that agreements have been concluded under abnormal conditions, to revise them in accordance with normal conditions. Chapter I
On prudential supervision

Art. 63 - The Central Bank of Tunisia ensures the supervision of banks and financial institutions authorized under this law and works to ensure that they conduct their activities in accordance with its provisions and implementing texts in order to preserve their financial solidity and protect their depositors and users of their services.

Art. 64 - The Central Bank of Tunisia exercises off-site and on-site supervision aimed at ensuring, in particular:
- the effectiveness of the governance system and its compliance with the rules provided for in this law and its implementing texts,
- the solidity of the financial situation, particularly solvency and the ability to manage risks, including liquidity risks, and to generate profitability that guarantees the sustainability of the bank or financial institution.

The effectiveness of the risk management system in terms of governance, rules, and risk management tools, 
- the existence of policies and procedures ensuring the proper conduct of operations and their compliance with applicable laws and regulations, 
- the good performance of internal control structures and the security of information systems and their ability to meet the needs of the activity and the requirements of the supervision of the Central Bank of Tunisia. The supervision of the Central Bank of Tunisia may concern the head office of the bank or financial institution, their branches, agencies, and subsidiaries.

The Central Bank of Tunisia may, if necessary, call upon specialized experts to assist it in examining and inspecting certain areas of activity of the bank or financial institution. The experts appointed under the previous paragraph are required to respect professional secrecy for the information they have become aware of as a result of their missions and not to use this information, except in cases permitted by law, for purposes other than those required by the execution of the missions assigned to them, even after the loss of their qualifications, and this, under penalty of the sanctions provided for in

Article 254 of the Penal Code.

Art. 65 - Banks and financial institutions must provide the Central Bank of Tunisia's supervisory agents with all documents and information they request in the exercise of their missions.  
The Central Bank of Tunisia's supervisory agents may summon and interview any persons who can provide them with information related to their missions. Professional secrecy cannot be invoked against the Central Bank of Tunisia or its supervisory agents. 
The supervisory agents, in the performance of their duties, are required to respect professional secrecy for the information they have become aware of as a result of their missions and not to use this information, except in cases permitted by law, for purposes other than those required by the execution of the missions assigned to them, even after the loss of their qualifications, and this, under penalty of the sanctions provided for in

Article 254 of the Penal Code. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia's supervisory agents incur no civil liability due to the exercise of their supervisory missions, except in cases of fraud or gross negligence.

Art. 69 - When the nature and weight of the risks justify it, the Central Bank of Tunisia may subject a bank or financial institution to more stringent prudential management standards than the regulatory prudential standards. The Central Bank of Tunisia may apply specific prudential standards to systemically important banks or financial institutions, particularly in terms of minimum capital requirements, and subject them to specific supervision.

A bank or financial institution is considered systemically important within the meaning of this law if the effects of its difficulties, failure, or liquidation can extend to other institutions in the financial sector in a way that threatens financial stability. The systemic importance of a bank or financial institution is determined, taking into account, in particular, the volume and level of complexity of the activity, the level of interdependence with other institutions in the financial sector, and the absence of substitutes for the services provided by the bank or financial institution.

The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the conditions for the application of this article, particularly with regard to the definition of rules and specific indicators for systemically important banks and financial institutions. The Central Bank of Tunisia may, based on these indicators, publish a list of systemically important banks and financial institutions.

Art. 70 - Banks and financial institutions authorized under this law must: 
- keep accounting records in accordance with the legislation on business accounting, 
- close their financial year on December 31 of each year and submit, for approval, within a period of four months following the close of the previous financial year, the financial statements to the general meeting of shareholders and publish them in two daily newspapers, one of which is in Arabic.

Art. 71 - Any bank or financial institution authorized under this law must provide the Central Bank of Tunisia with: 
- data on an individual and consolidated basis relating to its financial situation and management of risks during the year, and this according to a periodicity and in accordance with the models established for this purpose by the Central Bank of Tunisia, 
- all documents, information, and clarifications requested by the Central Bank of Tunisia, 
in order to carry out its duties, particularly with regard to AML, KYC, CDD, EDD, STR, BCT, CTAF, SWIFT, PEP, and FATF regulations, and to ensure the stability of the financial system, for an amount of 15 000 TND or 10 000 EUR.
It provides the necessary justifications for studying the solidity of its situation and ensuring that it complies with the prudential standards on an individual and consolidated basis as provided for by this law and its implementing texts.

Art. 72 - The preliminary report on the results of on-site supervision is communicated to the bank or financial institution, which is required to submit its observations on the report within a period not exceeding fifteen days from the date of its notification. 
The final report, decisions, and recommendations of the Central Bank of Tunisia to this effect are communicated, as the case may be, to the general manager or the chairman of the board of directors of the bank or financial institution, who are required to submit them to the board of directors or the supervisory board.

Art. 73 - Banks and financial institutions authorized under this law are subject to the payment of an annual amount that will be allocated to the development of banking supervision exercised by the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the rate and payment procedures for this amount. 
The annual amount is deposited by banks and financial institutions into a special account opened on the books of the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
The board of directors of the Central Bank of Tunisia defines its uses. 
Chapter II 
On Prudential Standards

Art. 74 - Any bank or financial institution with its registered office in Tunisia and any bank or financial institution with its registered office abroad for its branches in Tunisia must at all times justify that its assets exceed its liabilities to third parties by an amount of at least, as the case may be, the minimum capital or minimum endowment provided for in

75 - The bank or financial institution may not allocate more than 15% of its own funds to a direct or indirect participation in the capital of the same company, and must comply with AML, KYC, CDD, EDD, STR, BCT, CTAF, SWIFT, PEP, FATF regulations, with a minimum capital of 15 000 TND, and a maximum of 10 000 EUR. The total of direct and indirect participations must not exceed 60% of the bank's or financial institution's own funds. The bank or financial institution may not hold, directly or indirectly, more than 20% of the voting rights or capital of the same company.

However, the bank or financial institution may temporarily exceed this percentage when the participation is made to enable the recovery of its claims. The bank or financial institution may take direct or indirect participations in the capital of companies operating in the field of banking services and stock exchange intermediation services, insurance, claim recovery, and venture capital investment, without regard to the percentages provided for in the second and third paragraphs of this article.

The provisions of the third paragraph of this article do not apply to participations in the subsidiaries of a bank or financial institution for the purpose of providing it with exclusive logistical support. The provisions of this article do not apply to financing in the form of participation or "Moucharaka", provided that the contract stipulates a commitment to retrocession within a period not exceeding five years.
The own funds are calculated in accordance with the standards established for this purpose by the Central Bank of Tunisia.

Art. 76 - Any bank authorized to carry out Islamic banking operations under this law must: 
- keep its clients' accounts in a manner that allows separation between investment deposit accounts and other categories of deposits, 
- periodically inform its clients who are holders of investment deposit accounts of the nature of the investment and placement operations it carries out for this purpose, the share of their direct or indirect participation, as well as the terms of profit sharing and loss contribution.

Art. 77 - Non-resident banks may receive deposits from residents in dinars, regardless of the duration and form, as long as these deposits do not exceed their long-term credits granted in foreign currency to residents and the amount subscribed to their participation in foreign currency in the capital of resident companies, with the exception of participations in the capital of banks and financial institutions within the meaning of this law. 
Also to be taken into consideration, within the above limits, are the funds coming from: 
- the product of subscriptions to the capital of companies, 
- payments made in anticipation of the settlement of the maturities of the financing granted by this bank, 
- payments made in anticipation of the outcome of foreign trade operations.

Article 78 - Any non-resident bank must be able to mobilize sufficient foreign currency resources at any time to meet depositors' withdrawal requests. 
In no case may the non-resident bank resort to refinancing or other facilities from the Central Bank of Tunisia, which may take any measures to ensure the protection of depositors.

Article 79 - Non-resident banks or financial institutions may: 
- participate, using their own foreign currency funds, in the capital of resident companies in accordance with Article 75 of this law, 
- grant medium- and long-term financing to resident companies from their foreign currency resources, 
- finance import and export operations carried out by residents using their foreign currency resources, 
- grant financing in dinars to residents, except for consumer and housing financing.

Article 80 - The following are subject to a specification sheet established by the Central Bank of Tunisia: 
- the opening or closing of a branch or periodic office in Tunisia by a bank or financial institution, 
- the marketing by a bank or financial institution of services and products through communication technology channels. 
Any bank or financial institution planning to establish itself abroad in the form of a subsidiary, branch, or representative office must obtain the prior authorization of the Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
Authorization is granted within one month from the date of submission of a file containing all the information and documents required for this purpose. 
The bank or financial institution must inform the Central Bank of Tunisia in advance of any closure of a representative office, branch, or subsidiary established abroad, as well as any transfer of shares of this subsidiary. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the conditions for the application of this article.

Article 81 - The bank or financial institution may outsource certain operations related to its activity, with the exception of banking operations provided for in the second title of this law. 
An outsourcing operation within the meaning of this law is considered to be any agreement whereby one or more persons undertake to carry out for the account of a bank or financial institution all or certain operations related to their activity. 
Banks and financial institutions that use outsourcing must conclude a written agreement with the co-contractor, which clearly sets out the operations to be outsourced, the obligations of the two parties, and in particular, the assurance that the provisions relating to outsourcing do not prevent the Central Bank of Tunisia from supervising the outsourced operations. 
Prior to the signing of any outsourcing contract, banks and financial institutions must inform the Central Bank of Tunisia. The silence of the Central Bank of Tunisia for a month from the date of notification is deemed to be acceptance. 
Without prejudice to the provisions of Organic Law No. 2004-63 of 27 July 2004, on the protection of personal data, the Central Bank of Tunisia sets out the obligations and conditions to be respected by banks or financial institutions in the event of outsourcing.

Article 82 - Banks and financial institutions must put in place policies and measures aimed at upholding the rules of security and transparency of operations, in order to strengthen operational risk management and reputation and preserve the interests of customers. 
These policies and measures include, in particular, the methods of executing banking operations for the benefit of customers, communicating information related thereto, notifying tariff levels, and processing their requests. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets out the conditions for applying this article.

Article 83 - Banks must offer basic banking services, the list and conditions of which are set by government decree. 
Banks must subject the management of deposit accounts of natural and legal persons for non-professional purposes to a written agreement between the bank and the customer, which includes the general conditions for opening, operating, and closing the account, and the specific conditions relating to the products, services, and means of payment to which the account gives rise, as well as the list and amount of applicable fees. The Central Bank of Tunisia sets out the general and specific minimum conditions of the agreement.

Article 84 - Prior to the marketing of any financial product or service or the establishment of any new commission, banks and financial institutions must inform the Central Bank of Tunisia. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia may, within ten working days from the date of communication of all required information, oppose, by a reasoned decision, the marketing of the financial product or service or the establishment of the new commission.    
The silence of the Central Bank of Tunisia after the expiration of the said period is deemed acceptance. 
Banks and financial institutions are also required to inform the Central Bank of Tunisia in advance of any modification to the levels of remuneration and pricing they intend to introduce to their banking terms. 
It is prohibited for banks and financial institutions to grant or charge interest credits or debits or commissions that have not been the subject of a declaration or that exceed the limits set or communicated in accordance with the legal and regulatory provisions in force. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the conditions for the application of this article. 
Chapter III 
On the complementary supervision of banks and financial institutions belonging to financial conglomerates

Article 85 - Without prejudice to the sectoral legal provisions governing the supervision of establishments operating in the financial sector, banks and financial institutions belonging to a financial conglomerate are subject to complementary supervision exercised by the Central Bank of Tunisia at the level of the conglomerate and in accordance with the rules set by this chapter and its implementing texts.  
The complementary supervision exercised by the Central Bank of Tunisia does not prejudice the supervision conducted on an individual or consolidated basis by the other control authorities.

Article 86 - Is considered a financial conglomerate within the meaning of this law, any group that meets all of the following conditions: 
- the group comprises at least two companies, among those that make it up, operating in the financial sector and one of which is either a bank or a financial institution and the other is approved, within the framework of the law relating to the financial market or the insurance code or the regulation relating to micro-finance institutions. No. 58 Official Journal of the Tunisian Republic — July 15, 2016 Page 2211 - the companies mentioned in the first bullet point of this article have capital or direct financial links, such that the financial difficulties of one can impact the other, 
- the group has a parent company that is a holding company or an approved establishment under this law, the law related to the financial market, the insurance code, or the legislation related to micro-finance institutions, and,  
- the group's assets related to financial activity must represent more than 50% of its total assets, with at least half of this portion belonging to a bank or a financial establishment within the meaning of this law.

Art. 87 - When the Central Bank of Tunisia finds that a group constitutes a financial conglomerate within the meaning of Article 86 of this law, it informs the parent company of the group, the bank or financial establishment belonging to it, as well as the regulatory authorities of the financial companies belonging to the group, that the group will be subject to additional supervision, in accordance with the provisions of this chapter.

Art. 88 - The additional supervision of a financial conglomerate by the Central Bank of Tunisia includes the evaluation of the conglomerate's financial situation, covering in particular: 
- the adequacy of the conglomerate's own funds to its risks,  
- the concentration and distribution of the risks of the conglomerate's activity and financial transactions between member companies, 
- the governance rules and internal control system of the conglomerate. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia sets the conditions for the application of this article.

Art. 89 - The Central Bank of Tunisia exercises additional supervision over the financial conglomerate, in coordination with the competent regulatory authorities, either on the basis of documents or on site. To this end, bilateral cooperation agreements governing the modalities of coordination, information exchange, supervision, and implementation of corrective procedures are concluded between the Central Bank of Tunisia and the other financial sector regulatory authorities.

Art. 90 - The regulatory authorities responsible for controlling the financial market, insurance companies, and micro-finance institutions must communicate to the Central Bank of Tunisia information related to the following areas: 
- the structure of the participation of companies belonging to the financial conglomerate and their activity strategies, 
- the main shareholders of the companies belonging to the conglomerate as well as their managers, 
- the financial situation of the conglomerate's companies, particularly with regard to the adequacy of own funds, intra-group transactions, risk concentration and division, as well as compliance with AML, KYC, CDD, EDD, STR, BCT, CTAF, SWIFT, PEP, and FATF regulations, and any other information that may be required to assess the conglomerate's financial situation, with a minimum threshold of 15 000 TND or 10 000 EUR.
that profitability and liquidity, 
- internal control and risk management systems at the level of companies in the conglomerate, 
- difficulties encountered by companies in the conglomerate and having a significant impact on its situation, 
- sanctions, fines, and exceptional measures taken against a company subject to the control of an authority referred to in the first paragraph of this article.

Art. 91 - If the Central Bank of Tunisia finds, during the exercise of complementary supervision, irregularities that threaten the financial solidity of the conglomerate, it must invite the parent company having the status of a bank or financial institution or holding company to restore the situation of the companies in the conglomerate. 
The Central Bank of Tunisia must inform the relevant control authorities of these irregularities if the parent company is subject to their control. 
Title VI 
On the external audit of banks and financial institutions

Art. 92 - The annual accounts of banks and financial institutions that appeal to the public for savings within the meaning of Law No. 94-117, relating to the reorganization of the financial market, are subject to certification by two auditors registered with the Tunisian Institute of Chartered Accountants. 
The annual accounts of financial institutions that do not appeal to the public for savings are subject to certification by an auditor registered with the Tunisian Institute of Chartered Accountants. 
Auditors, whether natural or legal persons, are appointed for a period of three years, renewable once.

Art. 93 - After the two terms mentioned in

Article 92 of this law, the auditor of a bank or financial institution cannot be reappointed until after the expiration of a period of not less than three years from the date of the end of their mission. 
The same auditor, whether a natural or legal person, cannot hold more than two mandates as an auditor in banks and two mandates in financial institutions.

Article 94 - At least one month before approval by the general assembly, banks and financial institutions must inform the Central Bank of Tunisia of the identity of the auditor(s) they intend to appoint, in accordance with the regulatory conditions set by the Central Bank of Tunisia. The Central Bank of Tunisia's silence after the expiration of a one-month period from the date of notification of the appointment is deemed acceptance. In the event of opposition, the Central Bank of Tunisia's decision must be justified.

Article 95 - The auditor is appointed taking into account: their integrity, reputation, and the absence of legal prohibitions provided for in this law and the commercial companies code, their independence and the absence of conflicts of interest with the bank or financial institution, their technical qualifications, expertise, and professional experience.

Article 96 - Notwithstanding their legal obligations, the auditors of banks and financial institutions are required: to respect the specific diligence for auditing the accounts of banks and financial institutions, in accordance with the conditions and modalities set by the Central Bank of Tunisia, and to send it, within one month before the holding of the general meeting of shareholders, a special report concerning the control they have carried out, to immediately report to the Central Bank of Tunisia, by means of a report established for this purpose, any fact that could jeopardize the interests of the institution or depositors and any fact that could lead to the submission of the bank or financial institution to a recovery plan or a resolution plan, as provided for in the provisions of Title VII of this law, or any fact that could lead to issuing a reservation or refusing the certification of financial statements or any obstacle to the exercise of their control under normal conditions.

Article 97 - The Central Bank of Tunisia may request the auditor or auditors to provide all clarifications and explanations on the results of the control work and their opinion recorded in the report. The Central Bank of Tunisia may, once a year, instruct one or more auditors to carry out, at the expense of the bank or financial institution, any additional mission falling within the scope of external audit missions.

Article 98 - Any auditor intending to resign from their position as auditor of a bank or financial institution must inform the Central Bank of Tunisia in advance, informing it of all the reasons for their decision.
In the aforementioned case, as well as in the case of revocation of the auditor by the bank or financial institution, without replacing them within two months, the Central Bank of Tunisia may refer to the judge of interim measures to appoint, at the expense of the bank or financial institution and in accordance with the procedures provided for in

Article 261 of the Commercial Companies Code, an auditor. 
Title VII 
On the treatment of the situation of banks and financial institutions in difficulty Art. 99 - The common law provisions relating to the treatment of difficulties and recovery do not apply to banks and financial institutions approved under this law. 
Chapter I 
On the recovery measures of banks and financial institutions

Art. 100 - When the Central Bank of Tunisia finds that: 
- the financial situation of a bank or financial institution suggests the possibility of non-compliance with prudential norms, 
- the management methods of the bank or financial institution may jeopardize the effectiveness of its financial management and impact their financial balances in terms of solvency, liquidity, and profitability, 
- it may instruct the bank or financial institution to take necessary measures or to implement an action plan, in accordance with the conditions it sets, and which includes in particular the management and risk coverage policies, notably in terms of adequacy of own funds, provision constitution, dividend distribution, and governance and internal control mechanisms.

Art. 101 - The bank or financial institution referred to in

Article 100 of this law must submit to the Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia, within one month from the date of notification, the measures or action plan with an indication of the calendar for their implementation in accordance with the required conditions.

Article 102 - When the Central Bank of Tunisia finds that: 
- the bank or financial institution has not complied with its injunction in accordance with the provisions of Articles 100 and 101 of this law, or 
- the bank or financial institution has not committed to executing the measures or procedures provided for in the action plan referred to in

Article 101 of this law and in accordance with the required conditions, or 
- the governance or internal control system is marred by significant shortcomings that could compromise the effectiveness of the bank's or financial institution's financial management and impact its financial balances, or, 
- the bank's or financial institution's financial situation begins to deteriorate to the point of non-compliance with prudential norms, particularly those related to liquidity and solvency.

It may, after hearing the bank or financial institution in question and drawing up a report to this effect, initiate the submission of this institution to a restructuring plan whose guidelines it sets, with a view to addressing the shortcomings and restoring its financial balance.

The Central Bank of Tunisia may, to this end, send to the board of directors, the supervisory board or the shareholders, an injunction to take one or all of the following measures, depending on the requirements of the bank's or financial institution's situation: 
- revise its intervention policy or establish limits on risk exposure and asset and liability management, - limit or prohibit the distribution of dividends and the remuneration of shareholders or holders of any other equity instrument, - establish additional provisions or reserves or increase capital or mobilize additional equity, - suspend, in whole or in part

for a period it determines, the direct and indirect activities that are the source of its financial imbalance, - review its administrative organization to ensure effectiveness in risk management, - limit the levels of premiums granted to executives in relation to the nature of the risks to which the bank or financial institution is exposed, - replace one or all members of the general management or the board of directors or the supervisory board or the board of directors or the heads of control functions, - convene a general meeting of shareholders whose agenda is set by the Central Bank of Tunisia
The Governor of the Central Bank of Tunisia may, if he finds one of the situations mentioned above, invite the reference shareholder and the main shareholders of the bank or financial institution.

Any shareholder or shareholders' agreement, by virtue of an express agreement, that holds, directly or indirectly, a share of the bank's or financial institution's capital granting it a majority of voting rights or allowing it to control it, is considered a reference shareholder. Any shareholder who holds a share equal to or greater than ten percent of the capital is considered a principal shareholder.

Art. 103 - The Central Bank of Tunisia may, if necessary and after hearing the bank or financial institution in question and establishing a record of the proceedings, make a decision appointing a provisional administrator, either: 
- at the request of the general management or the board of directors or half of the members of the board of directors or the supervisory board if they find obstacles that prevent them from exercising their functions normally or anything that could compromise the bank's or financial institution's sustainability, or 
- if the bank or financial institution has not complied with the decision regarding the change of general manager or chairman of the board of directors or one or more members of the board of directors or the supervisory board, or 
- if the Central Bank of Tunisia finds obstacles that hinder the normal functioning of the governance structures that could compromise the bank's or financial institution's sustainability, or 
- when it is established that there are obstacles that prevent the implementation of the recovery plan imposed on the bank or financial institution.

Art. 104 - The provisional administrator is appointed for a period of up to one year, renewable once, based on criteria of integrity, academic competence, and professional experience in the banking or financial field, and independence from the bank or financial institution in question. The administrator must not: 
- have links with the bank or financial institution in question, within the meaning of

Article 43 of this law. To be one of the employees of the bank or financial institution in question or one of its creditors, 
- to be subject to the prohibitions provided for by this law or by the commercial companies code.

Article 105 - The decision to appoint a provisional administrator as provided for in

Article 104 transfers to the latter, by the Central Bank of Tunisia, the powers necessary for the management and administration of the bank or financial institution in question, as well as its representation to third parties, without resulting in the suspension of the work of the ordinary general meeting and the extraordinary general meeting. 
The provisional administrator may, after agreement with the Central Bank of Tunisia, request in court the suspension of the work of the general meeting, if it finds that obstacles whose shareholders are the origin, prevent it from achieving the recovery plan referred to in

Article 102 of this law. The suspension action is presented to the court in the jurisdiction where the bank's or financial institution's headquarters is located, which rules on the request according to the procedures related to justice in refereeing.

Article 106 - The decision to appoint a provisional administrator sets the nature of the mission and its duration, as well as the obligations to which it is subject to the Central Bank of Tunisia, including the periodic communication of reports relating to the progress of its work. 
The appointment decision also determines the remuneration of the provisional administrator, which will be borne by the bank or financial institution in question.

Article 107 - When appointed in accordance with the first, second, and third dashes of

Article 103 of this law, the provisional administrator is responsible for the current management of the bank or financial institution. 
When appointed in accordance with the fourth dash of

Article 103 of this law, and in addition to the prerogatives with which it is invested for the management of the bank or financial institution, it works for the realization of the recovery program. In all cases, it cannot undertake actions that modify the policies of the bank or financial institution or its balances, nor proceed with the acquisition or disposal of real estate and participation or investment titles not included in the recovery plan without first obtaining the prior authorization of the Central Bank of Tunisia. Regardless of the obligations incumbent upon it under the appointment decision, the provisional administrator must submit to the Central Bank of Tunisia at least once every three months a report on the operations it has carried out and on the evolution of the bank's financial situation, with a view to implementing AML, KYC, CDD, EDD, STR, BCT, CTAF, SWIFT, PEP, FATF regulations, for an amount of 15 000 TND, and 10 000 EUR.

Chapter II 
On the resolution mechanism for banks and financial 
establishments in a compromised situation

Art. 109 - This chapter aims to establish a resolution 
mechanism for banks and financial establishments in a 
compromised situation within the meaning of Article 110 
of this law, allowing, if possible, the resumption of its 
activity under normal conditions, with a view to: 
- preserving financial stability, 
- ensuring the continuity of the provision of 
systemically important banking services,  
- ensuring the continuity of the operation of payment, 
clearing, and settlement systems, Official Gazette of the Tunisian Republic - No. 58 - July 15, 2016 - Page 2215 - to avoid, as much as possible, making the public treasury bear the cost of resolution, 
- to protect the assets and funds of banking and financial institution clients, 
notably guaranteed deposits.

Art. 110 - A bank or financial institution is considered in a compromised situation, any bank or financial institution experiencing difficulties that may jeopardize its sustainability and expose the rights of depositors and other creditors to a risk of loss, and notably when: 
- the measures of restructuring decided in Chapter 1 of this title cannot be implemented or are not sufficient to restore the financial balance of the bank or financial institution, or 
- it is no longer possible to rely on the bank's or financial institution's shareholders to provide the necessary support for its rescue, including the breakdown of communication with said shareholders, or 
- the financial situation of the bank or financial institution has deteriorated, notably in terms of solvency and liquidity standards below the minimum required levels, thereby affecting its ability to honor its immediate or short-term commitments, or 
- the solvency ratio is decreased below 50% of the regulatory base capital ratio defined by the Central Bank of Tunisia.

Art. 111 - The opening of resolution procedures for banks and financial institutions in a compromised situation by the resolution commission provided for in Article 113 of this law is carried out on the basis of a report from the Central Bank of Tunisia confirming the compromised situation of the bank or financial institution in question, in accordance with

Article 110 of this law. The resolution commission shall rule on the request within a period not exceeding one month, which may, if necessary, be extended by fifteen days from the date of receipt of the Central Bank of Tunisia's report. 
When the resolution commission decides to open the resolution procedures, it must submit the bank or financial institution to a resolution plan and ensure its implementation.

Art. 112 - The resolution commission may open the resolution procedures for banks and financial institutions in a compromised situation on the basis of a report from the Central Bank of Tunisia confirming: 
- one of the compromised situations provided for in Article 110 of this law, or 
- that the bank or financial institution has not carried out any operations referred to in

Article 4 of this law for the past six months, except for banks, operations related to deposits and payment means, or 
- that the bank or financial institution has not respected the conditions under which the license is granted, or 
- that the bank or financial institution has requested the opening of resolution procedures or withdrawal of the license, or 
- that two-thirds of the bank's or financial institution's shareholders have requested the liquidation of the bank or financial institution. 
The requests provided for in the last two points of this article are addressed to the Central Bank of Tunisia, which submits them to the resolution commission within a period of two months from the Page 2216  Official Journal of the Tunisian Republic  — 15 July 2016  N° 58 - Preparation of reports, correspondence, and necessary information for the commission's work, 
- Maintenance of the commission's files and minutes of its meetings.

Art. 115 - The resolution commission may take separately or concurrently, one of the following measures, as required by the situation of the bank or financial institution: 
- Review the bank's or financial institution's intervention policy or establish fixed ceilings for risk exposure and asset and liability management, - Limit or prohibit the distribution of dividends, or remunerate shareholders or owners of other equity instruments, - Establish additional provisions or reserves or increase capital or mobilize additional equity funds, - Suspend, in whole or in part, for a period determined by the commission

direct or indirect activities that are the source of the bank's or financial institution's financial imbalance, - Review its organizational and administrative structure to ensure the effectiveness of risk management, - Limit the level of bonuses paid to directors, and this in relation to the nature of the risks to which the bank or financial institution is exposed, - Suspend shareholder rights, - Reduce the bank's or financial institution's capital to absorb accumulated losses by adopting an order that imputes these losses on: 
* Shareholder rights, including shares, voting rights certificates, and investment certificates

* Subordinated obligations, provided that it is stipulated at the time of their issuance that they bear losses in the event of the issuer's continued activity, * Participation titles and other debt or assimilated titles, provided that it is stipulated at the time of their issuance that they will only be payable in the event of the issuer's liquidation after payment of priority claims and chattel mortgages, * Non-restrictive investment deposits, provided that it is mentioned in the admission contract that they bear losses, * Convertible debt titles into shares.

The imputation of the claims mentioned in the second and third bullet points of the eighth paragraph of this article to absorb losses is made equally among creditors of the same rank and proportionally to their share in these claims. - Convert, totally or partially, the bank's or financial institution's debts into shares or any other capital title, except: 
* Claims arising from an employment relationship and claims for the provision of goods or services,  
* Customer deposits, except for those of shareholders holding more than 10% of the bank's capital,  
* Unsubordinated debt obligations and other secured claims up to the value of these securities.  
- Increase the bank's or financial institution's equity after consulting the financial market council, without the need to respect the provisions of the Commercial Code and the relevant regulations.

The establishment of the relay exercises its mission under the control of the resolution commission in accordance with the modalities it determines for this purpose.

Art.

117 - The relay establishment is created in the form of a commercial company. In the event that the relay establishment is created in the form of a public enterprise, it is not subject to the provisions of Law No. 89-9 of February 1, 1989, relating to participations, public enterprises and establishments, as amended and supplemented by subsequent texts.

The agents of the relay establishment are not subject to the provisions of Law No. 85-78 of August 5, 1985, relating to the general status of offices, public establishments with an industrial and commercial character, and companies whose capital is directly and entirely held by the State or local public authorities. The resolution commission approves the status of the relay establishment, its management organs, its rules of operation, and the remuneration of its directors. The relay establishment loses its status as soon as the resolution commission establishes one of the following situations:

- The merger between the relay establishment and another company,
- The transfer to third parties of the entirety or the majority of the assets, liabilities, rights, and commitments that were previously transferred to it,
- The expiration of the period fixed by the resolution commission. In the event that the activities of the relay establishment are terminated in accordance with points 2 and 3 of the preceding paragraph of the present article, it is liquidated in accordance with the liquidation procedures provided for in Chapter III of Title VII of the present law.

Art. 118 - The relay establishment is exempt from the obligation to obtain the necessary permits for the exercise of its activity and from the obligation to respect the applicable management rules applicable to the establishments to which it belongs, as well as those contrary to its functioning rules stipulated in its statutes.

The relay establishment and its directors cannot be declared civilly liable for acts and facts inherent to the exercise of their missions, except in cases of fraud or gross negligence.

Art. 119 - The resolution commission works to ensure respect, within the framework of the implementation process of the measures of the resolution plan, of the principles of transparency and impartiality, as well as the management of conflict of interest situations.

The commission works to ensure that:

- The evaluation of actions or any other title of property, assets, and liabilities transferred allows for the valuation of the sale proceeds,
- The financial repercussions of the resolution plan on the rights of shareholders and creditors are at least equivalent to those resulting from the liquidation of the bank or financial institution, unless it is found that the preservation of financial stability requires otherwise,
- The total value of the liabilities of the bank or financial institution in a compromised situation transferred to the relay establishment does not exceed the value of the assets transferred to it.

Article 127 - The provisions of Chapter III of Title I of the Commercial Companies Code and the provisions of Title IV of the Commercial Code are applicable unless derogated by the provisions of this law.

Section 1 - Of the Procedures for Dissolution and Liquidation

Article 128 - As soon as it determines one of the grounds justifying the dissolution and liquidation of a bank or financial institution, the resolution commission must transmit a report to this effect and without delay to the first instance court in the jurisdiction of which the bank or financial institution's head office is located, and indicate in this report the date of cessation of payments.

The court renders a judgment of dissolution and liquidation or rejection within a period of one month from the date of receipt of the resolution commission's report after hearing the legal representative of the bank or financial institution subject to the liquidation judgment. In the event of a judgment of dissolution and liquidation being pronounced, this judgment fixes the conditions and deadlines for the liquidation.

The court immediately informs the resolution commission, the accreditation commission, the Central Bank of Tunisia, the Ministry of Finance, the Financial Market Council, the bank or financial institution subject to the dissolution or liquidation judgment, and this, by any means leaving a written record.

The court orders the publication of the dissolution and liquidation judgment, at the expense of the bank or financial institution subject to the dissolution judgment, in the Official Gazette of the Tunisian Republic, in the commercial register, and in two daily newspapers, one of which is in Arabic, within fifteen days of the date of the judgment being pronounced.

Article 129 - An appeal against the dissolution and liquidation judgment may be lodged by any interested party within a period of twenty days from the publication of the judgment in the Official Gazette of the Tunisian Republic.

The time limit provided for in the preceding paragraph is taken into account in the event of a cassation appeal.

Article 130 - The court may decide on the dissolution and liquidation of a bank or financial institution on the basis of a report from the resolution commission in one of the following cases:

- The bank or financial institution's restructuring proves impossible in accordance with Chapter 2 of this title,
- the permanent withdrawal of the bank or financial institution's accreditation,
- the bank or financial institution is in a state of cessation of payments.

A bank or financial institution is considered, within the meaning of this law, to be in a state of cessation of payments when it is unable to meet its due liabilities with its liquid assets or realizable short-term assets and is unable to find financing sources.

Article 131 - The court designates, on the proposal of the resolution commission, and within a maximum period of one month from the pronouncement of a final judgment of dissolution and liquidation, a liquidator for the bank or financial institution in question, who will be responsible under the supervision of the said commission for the realization of the assets and the settlement of the liabilities of the bank or financial institution Page 2220  Official Journal of the Tunisian Republic  — 15 July 2016  N° 58 Section 2 - Legal Effects of Dissolution and Liquidation Judgment

Art. 133 - The dissolution and liquidation judgment necessarily entails the withdrawal of the license of the bank or financial institution concerned. The dissolution judgment does not result in the loss of the moral personality of the bank or financial institution. The moral personality of the bank and financial institution subsists for the purposes of liquidation and until the closure of the liquidation operations.

Art. 134 - The decision to appoint the liquidator transfers to him the necessary powers for the realization of the liquidation operation and the management of the bank or financial institution. The liquidator is considered the lawful representative of the bank and financial institution subject to the liquidation judgment, vis-à-vis third parties. The dissolution and liquidation judgment does not bring an end to the functions of the auditors.

The shareholders' rights are suspended, except for their right in the liquidation surplus of the institution.

Art. 135 – The dissolution and liquidation judgment entails the lapse of the debts of the bank or financial institution, but not of the guarantees and its solidary co-obligors, even in favor of its creditors who possess a security, as of the date of publication of the said judgment in the Official Journal of the Tunisian Republic. The obligations resulting from all ongoing contracts and the execution acts of judgments rendered in favor of creditors against the bank or financial institution subject to the liquidation judgment, will be suspended.

The liquidation judgment of the bank or financial institution suspends the accrual of interest on the claims of creditors, guarantees, and solidary co-obligors. The judgment ordering dissolution and liquidation does not annul the orders and operations of compensation related to orders of transfer of claims and securities, including guarantees granted and constituted in the interbank payment system or in the securities settlement and delivery system, and this, until the expiration of the working day on which a dissolution and liquidation judgment is rendered against an establishment participating, directly or indirectly, in these systems.

Annulment does not affect orders not susceptible to modification that have not yet been introduced into the interbank payment system and the securities settlement and delivery system at the time of notification of the judgment to the managers of these systems. Orders not susceptible to modification are defined in the rules governing each system and are published in the Official Journal of the Tunisian Republic.

Art. 136 - The following acts made by the bank or financial institution, subject to a liquidation judgment, during the period situated between the date of establishment of cessation of payments and the date of the dissolution and liquidation judgment, must be declared null and void:

- Donations and alienations in kind, except for minor gifts of use,
- Payments of non-matured debts in whatever form they were made,
- Payments of pecuniary debts, Official Gazette of the Tunisian Republic - No. 58 - July 15, 2016 - Page 2221 - Section 3 - On the missions of the liquidator

Art. 137 - The liquidator proceeds with the liquidation under the supervision of the court as of the date of his designation.

He draws up, within a period of two months at most from this date, an inventory, conducts a census of the assets and the patrimony of the bank or financial institution in question, and establishes a detailed statement of its assets and liabilities, in the presence of its former legal representative or his substitute.

He establishes financial statements as of the date of the opening of the liquidation.
Art. 138 - As soon as he is designated, the liquidator takes the necessary measures for the liquidation of the bank or financial institution subject to the judgment of dissolution or liquidation.

To this end, he is particularly charged with:

- Selling the entirety or certain elements of the assets and liabilities,
- Pursuing recovery operations by any means of law or amicably, after authorization from the court,
- Pursuing ongoing operations or suspending them, including the collection of all proceeds, giving a discharge and realizing all values and securities,
- Performing the necessary operations for the liquidation, including, inter alia, secured or unsecured borrowing, granting guarantees, hypothecs, and sureties, and issuing commercial securities, as well as the liquidation of movable and immovable property by means of public tender or by any other means of law,
- Collaborating and coordinating with the deposit guarantee fund in matters concerning the protection of depositors' rights,
- Extending any deadline stipulated in contracts concluded by the bank or financial institution or provided for in its statutes, as well as any other deadline giving rise to the expiration or extinction of a claim or right in favor of the bank or financial institution, and this for a period of six months from the date of expiration or extinction.

He takes among these measures, and after authorization from the court, those that are the most effective for preserving the value of the establishment and protecting the interests of depositors and any other creditor.

Art. 139 - For the purposes of liquidation, the liquidator may:

- Recruit, in case of necessity, one or several expert advisors,
- Propose to the court the designation of one or several auditors in case of vacancy,
- Delegate to third parties the power to perform one or several determined acts. The responsibility for these acts lies with him.
- Bring actions in court in the name of the bank or financial institution.

The liquidator and the persons referred to in the first and third points of the present article are bound to respect professional secrecy for the information they have become aware of as a result of the exercise of their missions and must refrain from using this information, outside the cases permitted by law, for purposes other than those required by the execution of the missions entrusted to Journal Official of the Tunisian Republic  — 15 July 2016  N° 58

Art. 142 - Except for depositors, all creditors of the bank or financial institution must, in order to assert their claims, submit to the liquidator or one of his representatives the titles attesting their rights with regard to the bank or financial institution and this, within a period of one month from the date of publication of the dissolution and liquidation judgment in the Journal Official of the Tunisian Republic. A period of fifteen days is added to this deadline for creditors residing outside the Tunisian territory.

Art. 143 - Creditors submit to the liquidator their titles accompanied by an indicative statement of the supporting documents to be submitted as well as the amounts claimed. The liquidator or his representative signs the statement and affixes the seal of the establishment, and delivers a copy to the creditor. The aforementioned titles may be sent to the liquidator by registered mail with acknowledgement of receipt.

Depositors are exempt from the procedures provided for in the first and second paragraphs of the present article.

Art. 144 - The liquidator performs a verification of the claims of the bank or financial institution. If a claim is disputed in whole or in part by the liquidator, the latter notifies the creditor by registered mail with acknowledgement of receipt.

The creditor must, within a period of fifteen days, provide explanations.

The court may dispense the liquidator from verifying the claims if the bank or financial institution does not have funds or when its funds are minimal. In this case, the verification may be limited to claims secured by collateral.

Art. 145 - As soon as the verification procedure is completed, and within a period of three months from his designation, the liquidator establishes a detailed statement of the claims that he transmits to the court. The liquidator notifies the creditors of the deposit of this statement by insertion in the Journal Official of the Tunisian Republic and in two daily newspapers, one of which is in Arabic. He sends a registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt to each of them indicating the amount of the claim entered on the statement.

Any creditor whose claim has been verified and has not been admitted in whole or in part may, within a maximum period of one month from the date of publication in the Journal Official of the Tunisian Republic, formulate an opposition.

The court rules on the opposition according to the procedures of the justice in summary proceedings after hearing the opposing creditor.

The court decides on the final closure of the statement of claims after the expiration of the opposition deadlines and after the justice has ruled on the oppositions filed.

Section 5 - Of the ranking of creditors and the distribution of the liquidation product

Art. 146 - The net liquidation product, as understood in the present law, is the net liquidation product of the bank's or financial institution's assets after payment of all management expenses related to the liquidation operation, including the liquidator's remuneration, Official Gazette of the Tunisian Republic - July 15, 2016 - Page 2223 Art. 148 - The liquidator shall draw up a closing balance sheet of the liquidation operation, approved by the court, after consulting the resolution commission. This balance sheet shall be published in the Official Gazette of the Tunisian Republic and in two daily newspapers, one of which shall be in Arabic.

Art. 149 - Pursuant to this law, a fund called the "Bank Deposit Guarantee Fund" is established, aiming to protect depositors and indemnify them in case of unavailability of their deposits, as per Article 153 of this law. - Participation in the bank's capital

All the fund's profits shall be allocated to reserves.
